| Precise maths against the WGSL builtins (accepted difference in work, 2026-11-05) | Any use of `createCompute()` without the `fastMath` option. | What Margo does extra: the same answer on every GPU within the bounds in the compute README. | Measured ([precise-math-gpu.mjs](../examples/package-benchmarks/precise-math-gpu.mjs), RTX A6000, [result](../examples/package-benchmarks/results/precise-math-gpu.json)): on 16,777,216 values `createCompute()` takes 1.0 to 1.8 times `createCompute({ fastMath: true })` for one call per element, `tan` 2.3 times and `pow` 3.0 times (2.19 against 0.72 ms). The path tracer's panorama and fisheye rays cost 1% to 7% of a traced sample. | Trade-off: `fastMath` is faster and as accurate as the GPU happens to be; the tracer has no such option. |
| Subgroup kernels (`@margoengine/compute/subgroups`, 2026-11-05) | Measured ([compute-subgroups.mjs](../examples/package-benchmarks/compute-subgroups.mjs), RTX A6000, subgroup size 32, 16,777,216 f32 values, busy machine, diagnostic, [result](../examples/package-benchmarks/results/compute-subgroups.json)): sort 11.9 to 7.0 ms (1.7 times), argsort 13.6 to 8.8 ms (1.5 times), sum 0.087 to 0.066 ms (1.3 times), sum along an axis 0.59 ms both, cumsum 0.55 to 0.56 ms (no gain). Correct at subgroup sizes 32 and 4; other sizes not run. | WGSL promises no subgroup size or layout, so each subgroup takes a seat with one atomic, and float sums follow the subgroup size. Sums and scans are limited by memory bandwidth here, so removing barriers saves little. | Float sums differ from the default kernels by rounding and from GPU to GPU; integers, orders and sorts are identical. `f16` arrays, `argmin`, `argmax`, segmented and per-axis scans run the default kernels. | Leave it off where float sums must match across GPUs; `useSubgroups` is a choice per context. |
| Neural networks (`@margoengine/compute/nn`, 2026-11-05) | Enforced by method: f32 only. Convolution and pooling hold their unfolded input, n x output positions x channels x kernel area floats, plus tables of the same shape for one sample, made once per input size and kept until the layer is disposed. Attention holds its [..., t, s] scores. Speed is not measured. | Convolution is a gather and a matrix product, and backward is the gather through the inverse table, so it uses no atomics and runs on every backend, the CPU included, at the price of memory. | A large image or a long sequence runs out of GPU memory before it runs out of time (`failed` on the next wait). `Embedding` gradients add atomically, so their rounding may vary on a GPU. Not included: grouped and transposed convolution, batch normalization, recurrent layers, f16, and GELU's erf form (the tanh form differs by under 0.001). | Split the batch; use a stride or pooling early. |
| Graph algorithms (`@margoengine/compute/graph`, 2026-11-05) | Enforced by method: vertices below 2^30; distances in `shortestPaths` are f32 sums, exact up to 2^24 for whole weights. `bfs` and `shortestPaths` take up to one round per edge of the longest shortest path (`shortestPaths` at most the vertex count, plus one to tell a negative cycle apart), and `connectedComponents` takes about log(vertices) rounds on the graphs tested (2,000-vertex shuffled path: under 64). Speed is not measured. | Each round runs over every edge at once with an atomic minimum, so a graph needs no frontier queue, the code is the same on the GPU and the CPU backend, and negative weights work. | A round visits every edge whether or not its source changed, so a long thin graph costs edges x its depth: a frontier-based search would do less work there. With f32 sums, cycles of total weight 0 that round below it can read as negative; zero-weight cycles can loop `predecessors`. `graph()` builds on the CPU and uses memory for every edge twice over. Not included: strongly connected components, minimum spanning trees, centrality. | Use whole or dyadic weights for exact sums; raise `checkEvery` on deep graphs to read back less often. |
| Workgroup autotuning (`@margoengine/compute/autotune`, 2026-11-05) | Default: 6 candidate sizes, 2 warm-up and 7 timed runs each, so 54 runs of your kernel on the first call and none on later ones. Results last for the context, or across sessions with `store`. | Measuring beats a fixed rule because the best size depends on the GPU and the kernel; timed runs take turns so drift is shared, and the median drops spikes. | The first call pays for those runs and for compiling every candidate. A result holds for the input size measured: name it in `signature`. Browsers round GPU timestamps (steps of 0.066 ms in the Chrome tested), so sizes of a short kernel can tie. Browsers without `device.adapterInfo` (and browsers that hide adapter details) let different GPUs of a store share an entry, which costs speed, never correctness. Driver updates are not seen: use `refresh`. `tuneCompute` covers the context's `reduce`, `scan` and `sort` only: `sum(axis)`, segmented scans and the element-wise kernels keep their fixed sizes, and the CPU backend, `useSubgroups` and the layer's sort ignore the table. The gain depends on the GPU: 8 to 13 percent on a sort on an Apple M6, none on the RTX A6000, where the default 256 is already the best. | Tune once at start-up, or ship a `store`. |
| Render passes of a package's frame | A core mesh in the same scene keeps core's clear pass; a pass after the package keeps core's resolve pass; a glTF model alone in its segment takes core's clear but keeps core's resolve pass, which measured no slower than resolving in the package's pass. | One colour pass when only packages that `join` draw (`createInstancedMesh`, `CulledInstances`, runs of glTF models): 0.024 ms at 1,000 boxes against 0.039 before (RTX A6000, 2026-11-05, perf-history entry 51). Accepted limit (Scott, 2026-11-06): core stays as it is, so a scene mixing core meshes with packages pays one store and reload of the multisampled colour and depth; joining core's batches into a package's pass would be a core change for speed alone. | A scene mixing core meshes with packages pays one store and reload of the multisampled colour and depth. | Draw the scene with package meshes only (`createInstancedMesh`, `CulledInstances`, glTF models), which share one colour pass. |
| Depth-writing lines (`depthWrite` on `LineMaterial`, `@margoengine/lines`) | By method: two draws per line (solid part, then edge ramp) unless `antialias` is false; depth is written where a line is at least half covered, so a crossing line shows through the outer half of the ramp. Depth follows the centre line, not the round profile of a thick line. | Keeping the smooth edge needs the ramp to blend after every solid part. One draw would either cut the ramp or write depth through it. | Twice the vertex work for these lines; a translucent depth-writing line hides what is drawn behind it after it. | Leave `depthWrite` off where lines do not cross, or set `antialias: false` for one draw. |
| GPU picking of lines (`LinePicking` in `@margoengine/lines/pick`) | Enforced: 268,435,456 segments per pick, 8 overlays per `Picking`. By method: a pick answers the nearest thing only; `engine.pick` can only answer meshes, so a line that follows no mesh answers an empty stand-in mesh (`lineOf` maps it back); with an overlay registered every pick draws the 3 x 3 pass with all line vertices, uncropped. | Core is frozen, so `engine.pick` keeps its mesh return type; lines share the pass and depth test of meshes. | Picks cost more with many segments; Picking's cached ID texture goes unused. | Read `hit.line` from `picking.pick`; use `intersectLines` from `@margoengine/bvh/lines` for a sorted list of ray hits. |
| Trails (`Trail` in `@margoengine/lines/trail`) | Enforced: 2 to 65,536 points (`maxPoints`, default 256); past that the oldest point goes and the far end jumps. By method: a trail is a line, so it faces the camera unless `normal` lays it flat (2026-11-07), and a flat trail is one strip with a per-point `normal` it does not have: it lies in a plane facing that one direction, so it does not follow a hill, and its segments are not joined at a corner; a flat trail takes no dashes; a dashed trail ignores `tailWidth`, because dash distances use the value widths are stored in. | One line keeps joins, antialiasing, fog, clipping and picking for free. | A tyre track seen from low down looks like a tube, not a flat strip. | Raise `maxPoints`; build a flat strip as a mesh with `@margoengine/splines/mesh`. |
| Massive line batches (`LineBatch` in `@margoengine/lines/batch`) | Enforced: 67,108,864 segments a batch; one draw per 8,388,608 segments at the default 256 MiB `maxBufferSize`. By method: independent segments with square ends: no joins, round caps, dashes, fog, clipping planes, depth writing or picking; colours at 8 bits a channel; a CPU copy of 32 bytes a segment stays for device loss. | Six vertices and 32 bytes a segment, where `Line` draws 78 vertices and reads a storage buffer whose binding size limits it. | Translucent corners are darker where segments overlap; memory is 64 bytes a segment across CPU and GPU. | Use `Line` where those features matter. |
| Hidden lines (`HiddenLine` in `@margoengine/lines/hidden`, `behind` and `depthBias` on `LineMaterial`) | By method: the test is against scene depth, so surfaces that write no depth hide nothing; `depthBias` (default 0.001 of the distance) decides what counts as on a surface, so an edge closer behind a surface than that shows as seen. Dashes run in world units. Hidden lines do not pick. | A depth test is one draw with no mesh analysis, on any scene; exact CAD hidden-line removal would need the geometry on the CPU. | A very thin wall can show an edge behind it as seen. | Lower `depthBias`, or raise it if a far model flickers. |
| Alpha to coverage on lines (`alphaToCoverage` on `LineMaterial`) | By method: works with MSAA only and falls back to blending without it; opacity comes in steps of one sample, four at 4x MSAA; lines of equal opacity use the same samples, so the later replaces the earlier at a crossing. | MSAA hardware turns alpha into a sample mask, which is what makes it independent of draw order. | Fine opacity changes band at low sample counts. | Leave it off and blend, or raise the sample count. |
| Filled helpers (`solidHead` on `ArrowHelper`, `fillOpacity` on `PlaneHelper`) | By method: a fill is flat colour with no lighting and does not pick. An opaque fill writes depth; translucent fills blend in the order added. | Helpers are guides, so they stay readable in any light and need no material or mesh. | A solid head has no shading, so its shape reads from its outline. | Use a mesh from `@margoengine/core` where lighting matters. |
| Video output (`@margoengine/headless/video`, `/ffmpeg`, 2026-11-05) | `encodeVideo` builds the whole file in memory and needs WebCodecs: browsers and workers have it, Node does not. WebM takes VP8, VP9 and AV1; MP4 takes H.264, VP9 and AV1. WebM times are whole milliseconds, as its default timestamp scale gives. Alpha is dropped. Frames are 8-bit RGBA, so no HDR video. Sound is Opus in WebM and AAC or else Opus in MP4, one or two channels, and comes as plain samples held in memory. | A file built whole has every size known up front, so nothing is patched afterwards and the MP4 index can sit first for playback before the download ends. WebCodecs is the only encoder a page has; shipping one would be a large download. | A very long capture must fit in memory, as compressed bytes only. In Node, `encodeWithFFmpeg` streams to a file instead, and needs ffmpeg installed. The H.264 and VP9 arguments and the rawvideo input ran on real ffmpeg 9.0.2 (`npm run test:real-ffmpeg --workspace @margoengine/headless`): 12 frames each, BT.709 tags read back, colours within 2 of 255 levels. That run needs ffmpeg, so the unit tests keep a stand-in program for failures and aborts. | Render in a browser or worker for `encodeVideo`, or use `/ffmpeg` in Node. | Subsurface scattering blur (`SSS` in `@margoengine/post/sss`, 2026-11-07) | By method: screen space, so only what is on screen scatters; one Gaussian per channel stands in for a measured profile's sum of Gaussians (no long red tail); the kernel stops at 64 px each side, so a surface filling the screen close to the camera scatters less than `radius` asks; taps across a depth step larger than `radius`, off the mask or on the background count as the centre colour. The mask is the user's: a material's `subsurface` value does not mark pixels by itself. One `rgba16float` texture at the frame size; GPU cost not measured (LIM-434). | A separable blur costs two passes of `2 x taps + 1` reads, where a 2-D kernel would cost its square. | Soft skin, wax and marble on marked pixels; red bleeds farthest into shadow edges with the default profile. | Raise `taps` for wide kernels; mark pixels with a `SceneTargets` output or a selection mask. |
| Material decals (`MaterialDecals` in `@margoengine/post/material-decals`, 2026-11-07) | By method: a screen-space relight in a PostStack, not a G-buffer write before lighting. The surface comes from a `SceneTargets` capture (one more scene pass); the change is core's lit model (sun plus ambient) for the new surface minus the old, so gltf-pro and materials models get the sun and ambient part only, not their image-based light; the sun's share is read back per pixel from the lit image, so a pixel the unshadowed sun gives nothing (facing away) is treated as lit; transparent effects drawn over the surface are relit with it; the atlas is read at mip 0; 64 decals, no culling; GPU cost not measured (LIM-441). | Engines that write decals into a deferred G-buffer change the surface before any light; Margo's forward renderer has no such buffer, so the relight works from a capture. | Normal, roughness, metalness and base-colour decals on any surface core or the capture draws, with shadow kept. | Keep decals on core meshes for an exact relight; give the atlas texels as wide as the decal's screen size. |
| Rough reflections (`SSR` with `stochastic: true` in `@margoengine/post/ssr`, 2026-11-08) | By method: one GGX-sampled ray per pixel per frame on surfaces rougher than half of `maxRoughness`, averaged over frames by a history reprojected with the surface's motion and clamped to this frame's 3x3 neighbourhood (mean plus or minus one standard deviation), blend floor 1/16; only what is on screen reflects, as for the mirror path. One history per SSR (a second view in the same frame reprojects against it); a moving camera smears rough reflections for a few frames; some noise stays on a still view (mean frame-to-frame change 0.15/255 against 1.28/255 at the second frame); three more `rgba16float` targets; GPU cost not measured (LIM-446). | One ray per pixel keeps the cost of the mirror path; the frames do the averaging. | Rough floors and brushed metal reflect what is on screen instead of keeping only the environment. | Leave `stochastic` off for deterministic frames (screenshots, tests); pair with TAA for a moving camera. |
| Multi-bounce screen GI (`SSGI` with `multiBounce: true` in `@margoengine/post/ssgi`, 2026-11-08) | By method: each frame adds one bounce by reading the light at ray hits from the previous frame's result, reprojected through the previous camera; only what is on screen bounces; the extra bounces trail a moving camera or light by a few frames; a hit hidden in the previous frame takes the light of what covered it for a frame; one history per SSGI (a second view in the same frame shares it); two more `rgba16float` targets and a display pass when SSGI ends the stack; GPU cost not measured (LIM-455). | Bounces accumulate over frames for the cost of one bounce per frame. | Indoor scenes fill with bounced light on a still or slow camera. | Keep it off for a fast-cutting camera, or accept a few frames of build-up after each cut. |
| Anamorphic streaks (`Anamorphic` in `@margoengine/post/anamorphic`, 2026-11-07) | By method: streaks are horizontal only (no rotation); they are built at half width and a quarter of the height, so a streak is about 4 px tall and a light smaller than a pixel still draws one; each streak is the light's own colour times `tint`, with no spectral split; reach is 2 (3^passes - 1) half-width texels each side; two quarter-size and one full-size `rgba16float` targets; GPU cost not measured (LIM-459). | A chain of sparse 9-tap passes reaches far for a few reads per pixel, where one wide kernel would read hundreds. | Bright points and highlights draw thin tinted lines across the frame. | Lower `passes` for short streaks, raise `threshold` so only lights streak. |
| Blur (`Blur` in `@margoengine/post/blur`, 2026-11-08) | By method: 2 radius + 1 texture reads per pixel per pass, so cost grows with the radius (64 at most, 129 reads a pass); the kernel is cut at 3 sigma for the Gaussian; edges clamp to the nearest pixel, so a bright border bleeds inward; `region` is a rectangle with a hard edge; one or two full-size `rgba16float` targets; GPU cost not measured (LIM-472). | A plain separable loop is exact for every radius and needs no mip chain. | Menus behind glass, focus pulls and custom chains blur by any whole-pixel radius. | Keep the radius small on weak GPUs, or chain two Blurs of half the radius for a wider, cheaper look. |
| Lens model (`Lens` in `@margoengine/post/lens`, 2026-11-08) | By method: one radial distortion term (k r^2), no tangential or chromatic part; distortion resamples the frame bilinearly, so it softens it slightly; the dirt is lit by its own glow at an eighth of the frame size (reach about 50 px), not by the glow of `Bloom`; the built-in dirt is a fixed pattern; two eighth-size and one full-size `rgba16float` targets; GPU cost not measured (LIM-474). | Billboards (`BillboardLayer` in `@margoengine/sprites/billboard`, 2026-11-08) | `capacity` 256 billboards before a buffer grows; at most the device's `maxStorageBufferBindingSize` / 64 per view. | One instanced draw per view, each view with its own sorted buffer, so its memory is 64 B per billboard per view. | By method: blended billboards sort by the pivot's distance, so two that cross draw one over the other whole; pixel-sized ones take their depth from the pivot; `lockY` applies to world sizes only; texels are read with no filtering. | Smooth sprites (`SpriteLayer` `filter: 'linear'` in `@margoengine/sprites`, 2026-11-08) | One copy of the atlas per layer, `rgba8unorm-srgb` with a full mip chain: 4/3 of the atlas size again. | Filtering straight alpha bleeds a transparent texel's colour into edges, and filtering sRGB bytes darkens averages, so the layer keeps a premultiplied, linear-light copy. | By method: mip levels below the first average across neighbouring cells; the copy is made once, so a changed `GPUTexture` atlas needs `setAtlas` again; normals stay exact-pixel; premultiplied 8-bit storage loses colour precision at low alpha. | Live grading (`Grade` in `@margoengine/tonemap/grade`, 2026-11-08) | By method: display-referred, on 0..1 colour after the tone curve; under an HDR `ColorOutput` what lies above white passes ungraded; curves are sampled 33 times and read linearly; the wheels are additive offsets with fixed luminance masks (no pivot or range controls); one uniform of 608 B; GPU cost not measured (LIM-477). | Grading after the curve keeps the controls in the 0..1 range artists know from grading tools. | Wheels, curves and hue against saturation move live with no LUT to bake. | Bake a LUT with `setLUT` for a look outside these controls. |
