| Sciviz unstructured grids (`@margoengine/sciviz/grids`, 2026-11-08) | Linear tetrahedra (10), hexahedra (12), wedges (13) and pyramids (14); `parseVtk` also reads voxels (11) as hexahedra. One value per point or per cell. | Surface and slice are built on the CPU each call; a moved slice is a new `sliceGrid` call and `layer.update(set)`. Cells are taken as convex with planar faces; a twisted hexahedron face is split along its 0-2 diagonal. | `parseVtk` reads legacy files up to version 4.2 (CELLS with a count before each cell); version 5.1 files (OFFSETS and CONNECTIVITY), XML `.vtu`, binary `long` data and other DATASET kinds are refused naming what. | Sciviz graph layouts (`@margoengine/sciviz/graph`, 2026-11-08) | Any node count the memory holds; edges up to the GPU's `maxStorageBufferBindingSize` / 8 per layer (16,777,216 at the 128 MiB default). | The layout runs on the main thread, one iteration per `step()`, about E + N log N work; `run()` yields between iterations. No speed is claimed. | Undirected straight edges; weights scale the pull. No frame walls (a pull toward the origin instead), no edge-crossing or label placement. Like any force layout it can settle in a local minimum; ten 24-node ring seeds at the default theta 0.9 settle with edges 3 % to 6 % uneven and no crossing. The tree opens cells by Barnes's 1994 test (d > side / theta + the centre of mass's offset), not the 1986 one, which kept one ring seed in ten (seed 3) crossed with edges 13 % uneven: on a 20,000-node graph that opens 10 % more cells on the first step in 2D (19 % in 3D) and 21 % (41 %) over the next 100 steps, counted. The layer frames the positions it was made with unless `bounds` is given. Edges are one-pixel lines. | Run the layout in a worker and send `positions` to `layer.setPositions`; pass `bounds` for a layout that will grow. |
| Sciviz geographic layers (`@margoengine/sciviz/geo`, 2026-11-08) | Zoom 0 to 24; up to `maxTiles` tiles per layer (default 256), all loaded at one zoom when the layer is made. | Each tile is a 16 by 16 grid projected in the vertex shader; a 256-tile layer is 256 draws. | Raster tiles only (PNG, JPEG or anything `createImageBitmap` reads), one zoom per layer, no level-of-detail streaming as the camera moves. | Light-tier frame rate | Enforced ([index.ts](../packages/quality/src/index.ts)): `paceEngine` holds the light tier to an even rate of at least 60 FPS: 60 on 60, 120 and 240 Hz, 72 on 144 Hz, 83 on 165 Hz, 67 on 200 Hz, and every refresh of 75, 90 and 100 Hz. | Each frame spans a whole number of refreshes, so the rate cannot land on exactly 60 on every display, and an uneven 60 on 100 Hz would judder. | A 100 Hz display renders 100 FPS on the light tier, which asks twice the GPU work of the 50 FPS it used to get; a GPU that cannot keep up misses refreshes as it would on any uncapped tier. Not yet seen on a physical panel at any of these rates: the numbers come from a stand-in clock, a real page on a simulated 100 Hz clock and a fake clock in the unit test. | `capFrameRate(engine, rate)` sets another rate; `?quality=high` is not paced. |
| Supersampled stills (`@margoengine/quality/ssaa`, 2026-11-06) | Enforced ([ssaa.ts](../packages/quality/src/ssaa.ts)): 1 to 1024 frames, picture size up to the device's `maxTextureDimension2D`. Each sample is a full render, so cost grows with `samples`. Two `rgba32float` sums, the frame and image textures and a read buffer live during a still (44 bytes a pixel, 365 MB at 3840 x 2160). The picture is opaque 8-bit display colour: no alpha, no HDR. A size other than the canvas makes effects that size themselves to the frame rebuild their textures, twice per still, and core keeps its 4x target for that size until the next one. History effects soften a still: with `TAA` attached a 16-sample still reads 27 dB against the same still without it. `TAAUpscale` throws, as it does with any view. | Each sample is a full render, so cost grows with `samples`. | With `TAA` attached a 16-sample still reads 27 dB against the same still without it, and `TAAUpscale` throws. | Dispose `TAA` (and any `TAAUpscale`) before the still and attach it again after, and lower `samples` to cut the cost. |
| Feature scaling (`@margoengine/quality/features`, 2026-11-06) | A step that saved under 3% of the frame rests 120 decisions, about a minute at 60 FPS. | A saving is the frame cost before minus after one step, over one 30-frame window: anything else that moves the cost in that window counts toward it, and a measured value is averaged with the last, so it corrects over time. | A step of shadow `resolution` or `cascades` or of the fog `grid` allocates textures, one hitch each. A `VolumetricFog` switched off keeps its grid and its idle pass. The first use of a shadow filter compiles shaders, one hitch per filter. Cutting `camera.far` removes what lies past it. It lowers nothing when every knob is at its floor or resting. | Leave a target out of `featureKnobs` (for example `shadows`) to keep it fixed, or write your own `FeatureKnob` (see `optionKnob`) with a `weight`. Pair a lowered `camera.far` with fog. |
| Battery and heat (`@margoengine/quality/power`, 2026-11-06) | Heat takes about half a minute to show at 60 FPS, longer at lower rates. | Not measured on a machine really throttling: `FrameDrift` is proved on modelled frame costs. Battery status is Chromium only, and CPU pressure is Chromium only and says nothing of the GPU; elsewhere frame times are the only source, so a machine on battery stays at level 0. | A scene that grows heavier gradually, with no step above 15% between readings, reads as heat. A full-tier page keeps its 4x multisampling until its next load. | Call `restart()` on the watch after a change you made, so growth you caused is not read as heat, and raise `rise` if it fires too soon. | Own physics kernel (`@margoengine/physics/next`, preview, 2026-11-07) | Enforced: 4,194,304 bodies per world, a world per Wasm instance, and 32-bit offsets inside it; `KernelWorld` throws above that or where memory cannot grow. Substeps run from 1 to 65,535. | By method: the integrator's own error against a parabola is `g h t / 2`, so it halves when substeps double; a dynamic body with no mass does not fall, and additional mass is spread as the colliders are, so it scales the inertia with the mass. Shapes today: ball, box, capsule, each with a closed-form mass, and hull. Enforced: a hull is a closed convex polyhedron with flat faces of at most 256 edges and no two neighbours that are one plane split in two, within about 0.8 degrees with every corner within half of FLAT, 1e-4 of the hull's size, of the other's plane (a mesh with such faces loses contact points, Gregorius 2015, so `addHull` refuses it); a real crease under 0.8 degrees between faces too wide to be one flat face is taken, as a hull of random points has them; its rows last for the world's life. By method: the separating axis test is linear in vertices per face and quadratic in edges, with no hill climbing or cached axis yet, so a hull of hundreds of faces costs a step more than it should until the quiet pass. By method: GJK stops after 64 descents, and the expanding polytope holds 96 vertices and 192 faces; a depth search that runs out gives no contact for that step and the next step tries again. By method: a point with a new id continues an old one within 2 cm on the first body, so a contact that jumps further starts its impulses from zero. By method: a contact's normal is found once a step and held for its substeps, and a point the body has not yet reached acts as a plane (Catto 2013's speculative point), so a fast body passing a corner can feel a ghost of that plane; not measured, batch 126 owns it. Contact defaults: 8 substeps, 2 passes, 120 Hz capped at a quarter of the substep rate, damping ratio 10, slop 0.2 mm, push speed 3 m/s. By method (2026-11-08): at one pass a substep a contact between two dynamic bodies that neither dominates is capped at an eighth of the substep rate (30 Hz at 4 substeps) while it carries under 50 times the lighter body's weight, as one pass settles no pile at a quarter; the ground, kinematic and dominant bodies and heavier loads keep the quarter. Measured at 4 substeps of one pass: the 20-row pyramid sleeps at 2.3 s, its top moved 32 mm, its bottom row 1.19 mm into the floor; 30 rows, whose bottom pairs carry about 40 times a cube's weight, sleep at 2.0 s and rest at 5.9e-4 m/s with sleeping off; the 1:100 and 1:1000 stacks keep the quarter and sag 14.4 and 137 mm. A deeper pile whose bottom pairs pass 50 times takes the quarter there; not measured past 30 rows. By method (2026-11-07): a substep relaxes as many times as it pushes, so 2 relaxing passes of joints and contacts at the defaults where there was 1: one pass left the friction anchors' push in a pile of 14 rows or more as speed, and it rocked for good. By method: a manifold's normal rows sweep until no impulse moves by more than rounding, at most 16 sweeps a pass, on the points' speeds alone; a relaxing pass settles in 3 to 8 sweeps on the 1:1000 stack. By method (2026-11-08): a manifold of four points ends each sweep with the exact step along the one pattern of its impulses that moves no body, the points' shares of one load among themselves, which the sweeps settled only by the leak (about 3 percent a sweep), so a soft pass ran all 16; it now settles in about 4 (perf-history 80). Friction keeps one sweep. By method (2026-11-08): inside the slop a biased pass closes a point rigidly to the slop's depth, (gap + slop) / h as a speculative row (Catto's Solver2D soft step), and the soft push acts only past it, so every point of a resting manifold rests at the same depth whatever its load: a cube released on a slope below tan t = mu holds under 1e-6 m from its first second (it moved up to 3.8e-5 m as its points sank at speeds that followed their loads). Measured on the harness, defaults and 4 substeps of one pass: creep 5.5e-5 and 5.9e-6 m to 0; the 1:1000 stack's top drifts 1.6e-8 and 1.4e-7 m (6.6e-7 and 3.7e-6 m before the exact step of the four points' shares); the 20-row pyramid at the defaults sleeps at 1.50 s (1.78 s before that step, 3.2 s earlier), and at 4 substeps of one pass, which fails its bars either way, moved its top 0.291 m (0.277) and its fastest box at 30 s 0.51 m/s (0.18); with the exact step of the four points' shares (2026-11-08) 0.270 m and 0.28 m/s, still awake until the eighth-rate spring of two movable bodies at one pass (above) let it sleep. By method (2026-11-08): a ball or a capsule meets the other surface at its core plus its radius along the normal, wherever it has turned to, so a rolling ball's point stays on the floor; its lever arm stays the step's contact point. A ball from rest at 30 degrees rolls within 1e-5 of 5/7 g sin t (it ran 1.0033 in its first second). By method (2026-11-08): a point struck while its gap is still open notes the speed it will meet the surface with, v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a d over the gap, gravity's gain added, so a ball from 1 m at e 0.5 peaks at 0.2487 m at the defaults and 0.2473 m at 4 substeps of one pass (was 0.2481 and 0.2432). By method: a resting contact sags by its load over its stiffness, which follows the lighter body, so a heavy box on a light one sits deeper: 3.9 mm at 1:100 and 3.5 cm at 1:1000 with metre cubes. A rolling ball slips 0.35 percent of its speed by 2.5 s, as friction is a stiff spring, and lands 0.13 percent over 5/7 g sin t. Enforced: a manifold holds four points. By method: the reduction always keeps the deepest point, so its area can fall short of the best four: 0.711 of the best at worst and 0.9915 on average over 3,000 random sets. Enforced: 536,870,912 pair rows and 32-bit offsets inside the block; a step throws when memory cannot hold the pairs. By method: pairs are found once a step over the motion expected at its start, so a body a contact turns round mid-step can leave its fat box until the next step; the margin is 0.04 m at any body size; a fixed body written by hand needs `touch`; a collider's row comes back only after a step. A single add or removal costs one pass over the lists, so adding one collider a frame to a very large world pays for the whole list. Until the narrow phase lands, two bodies touch when their fat boxes overlap, so islands run larger than they will. Writing a sleeper's columns does not wake it. A body at a steady pose with its energy under the threshold can go to sleep mid-air if nothing pushes it, as gravity is not a force the sleep test sees: a body at rest under gravity moves, so this needs zero gravity or `gravityScale` 0. A snapshot is the whole block, so its size follows capacity, not the bodies in use. By method: f32 state, as a far world needs `FloatingOrigin`. Needs Wasm SIMD, as core's kernel already does, so there is no second blueprint. `Physics`, `PhysicsBody` and `PhysicsCollider` of the entry serve free motion only: `setType`, `follow`, friction and the other contact settings, joints, queries, character controllers and `addModel` throw `unsupported` until their batch. `body.sleep()` and impulses take effect at the next step. A snapshot reads only in the kernel build that wrote it, and a `Physics`-level restore waits for `/snapshot`. Measured (LIM-366): 10,000 steps hash-equal in Node, native x86-64, Chromium 156 and Firefox 157 on one Windows PC; Safari, WebKit, ARM and any other machine are unmeasured. On that PC Windows will not start Playwright's Firefox from the home folder (a side-by-side error on `mozglue`, as Chromium's full `chrome.exe` gives there), so the run used a copy of it under the worktree through `REPLAY_FIREFOX`. | The kernel is staged behind `/next` until the switch; the root entry still runs Rapier. Bit-equal results hold for one kernel build, not across kernel versions. | Use the root entry, which still runs Rapier. |
| Own physics joints (`@margoengine/physics/next`, preview, 2026-11-07) | By method: locks are exact along a path of joints, so a chain of 50 hung straight holds a 1000:1 end mass to under 1e-5 of its length, at rest and swung at 3 m/s. By method: a lock's turning arm is read at the start of a substep, so a light link under a large pull turns as an explicit spring of stiffness about twice the pull times its arm; past about two radians a substep of that turn it grows. A chain of 50 laid out level with a 1000:1 end mass passes 1e-4 of its length at step 32 and 2 times by step 60 with 1 kg links of a sphere's inertia (0.001 kg m2 at 0.05 m arms); 16 substeps hold it to step 66, 32 to step 229, ten times the inertia to step 219 (`docs/known-bugs.md`). By method, four limits on the lock solve, each with a test that fails without it. (1) A row with under n u of its size left after the rows before it depends on them and carries nothing, n the rows of its path and u f32's epsilon (Higham 1990, stop 4.3 at his n u), read off Householder QR of M^-1/2 J^T so the doubles round each row only by its own length: a body held by ten rows on six freedoms stands still where it used to reach 18,904,462 m/s, and a path with 13 rows on 12 freedoms no longer keeps its dependent row (4e-7 of its size by elimination of J M^-1 J^T, 1e-32 now). (2) A lock closes a gap at 3 m/s plus what the turning carries its anchors, the clamp of Buss and Kim 2005, whose D_max,i = d_i + D_max this is. A valid scene reaches it when a body is moved by hand off its joint or a hub turns at 8 rad/s at 100 m. Pairs are found once a step, so without it a joint 6 m open jumps a body past a wall in one substep. Cost: a wide gap takes more steps, and on the proof scenes it acted on 5 rows of 6,960 in the limb and moved no figure. (3) Where rows nearly depend on each other a push is a Gauss-Newton step outside its model, so a body's turn may rise by at most 0.2 rad a substep times N / M, and its centre by that much of its arm, N what the path asks and M what its bodies would each move (Buss and Kim 2005, section 4; they use 0.79 rad for inverse kinematics, here 0.79 lets a taut chain reach 39 m/s and 0.1 starts to cut the chain of fifty). A valid scene reaches it when a chain is pulled straight between two points further apart than it is long, the same pose as an arm reaching past its reach. Cost: what is cut stays open into the next substeps, and the whole path's push is cut, not only its bad direction, as a path has no singular value decomposition. It cut nothing in any scene of `kernel/tests/joints.rs`. (4) A warm start that would add more than a push's energy, half the island's mass times 3 m/s squared, is taken only as far as the minimum of the quadratic the passes descend. A valid scene reaches it when a limit catches a swing, as what the row holds is an impact and no load: once per catch on the proof scenes, keeping 0 to 7 percent. Cost: that row starts its substep cold, and no figure in `kernel/tests/joints.rs` moved. No paper does this; the line search is standard, its use here is our own. By method: a lock is exact and a contact is a capped spring, so a joint stretched through a wall drags its body through at about 1.5 m/s. By method: a turn past about 1 rad a substep leaves rows nothing to read, so a lock on a hub at 77 rad/s holds with 2 substeps, to 13 m on a radius of 10, and with 1 substep runs away and is refused after 59 steps. By design: a body past 1e15 in position or speed stops the world with `failed`, checked at the end of a step: a run away faster than that within one step would get past it, not seen in 200 random webs of 10,000 steps. | Own physics triangle meshes (`@margoengine/physics/next`, preview, 2026-11-07) (LIM-518) | By design: a triangle mesh has no volume, so it gives a body no mass and refuses `mass` and `density`, as a Rapier trimesh gives none; both sides of a triangle collide, so a shape pushed past a triangle's plane is pushed on through it. Not served yet: a mesh against a mesh gives no contacts (Rapier meets composite against composite; batch 139.3). By method: one manifold of up to four points for each triangle a shape touches, each a pair row of its own, so a box across a crease holds both normals and a large box on a fine mesh solves a manifold per triangle under it. By method: `fixInternalEdges` (default false, as in Rapier) sorts an edge as convex, concave or flat from the triangle across it, joined by corner position so texture seams still join, an edge of three triangles staying open; a fold under 1e-3 (about 0.06 degrees) is flat. Loss to fix (batch 129): on that mesh the build takes 65 ms without the edge rule (105 ms with it) where Rapier 0.21 takes 43 ms, and a step of the 1,000 boxes 1.52 ms median, 7.5 ms p95 where Rapier takes 1.14 and 4.8, both measured on a loaded machine; the tree's leaves hold two triangles and every node bins 16 ways. By design: mesh rows last for the world's life. | A manifold a triangle costs solver rows where a merged manifold would cost fewer, and keeps every face's normal | On the 130,050-triangle St Helens mesh the build takes longer than Rapier 0.21, as the row measures. | Turn on `fixInternalEdges` for sliding over a flat mesh. |

| Own physics continuous collision (`@margoengine/physics/next`, preview, 2026-11-08) (LIM-506) | By design: Rapier's `ccd_enabled` as `ccd` on `addBody` and `body.ccd`, and `is_ccd_active` as `body.ccdActive`. A report under `minFrames` when the page closes is lost. `sendBeacon` sends the page's cookies for its endpoint; the `fetch` fallback omits them. Asking users for consent is the app's job. | Percentiles come from 256 logarithmic bins, so they are approximate. | `sent` means handed to the browser, and a report under `minFrames` when the page closes is lost. | Lower `minFrames` (default 60) so a short visit still reports. |

A native file decodes on the calling thread, not in a worker. Files made by KTX-Software; decoded images checked against `ktx extract` on eight small files and three full-size ones. | LIM-215. A Basis file whose level 0 is not a multiple of 4 falls back to RGBA8, and RGB `vkFormat`s gain an opaque alpha. | RGB `vkFormat`s take a third more memory, and a native file decodes on the calling thread, not in a worker. | Author the file with level 0 a multiple of 4 and with an RGBA or Basis format instead of RGB. |
| NRRD volumes (`@margoengine/loaders/nrrd`, 2026-11-06) | By method: raw, ascii, hex, gzip and bzip2 data (bzip2 needs `@margoengine/decoders`); the `block` type is refused with code `unsupported`. 64-bit integers become `Float64Array`, exact up to 2^53. At most 536,870,912 samples by default (`maxSamples`), and the header at most 1 MiB. `bounds` ignores rotation and origin; `matrix` holds them. | `DecompressionStream` has no bzip2, and sciviz takes numbers, not BigInts. gzip and bzip2 decoding stop once the header's samples are out (format section 2: data past them is ignored), so the CRC at the end of such a stream is not read. The `2D-masked-matrix` kind's size is not checked: the format's table gives 4 and lists five components. | A bzip2 file without `@margoengine/decoders` installed is refused. | Install `@margoengine/decoders`, or `unu save -e gzip`; raise `maxSamples`. |
| LDraw models (`@margoengine/loaders/ldraw`, 2026-11-06) | By method: at most 4,000,000 sub-file references (`maxInstances`) and 64 levels (`maxDepth`). Texture maps (`!TEXMAP`) are skipped with a warning, the legacy dithered colours 256 to 511 draw light grey, and `0 !COLOUR` lines apply file-wide. Uncertified polygons cost twice the triangles, being written on both sides. | One merged mesh has no per-group double-sided flag, and textured parts are a small share of the library. | Models expand to plain triangles unless `instanced` is set; then each placed `.dat` part in each colour is stored once, and mirrored placements stay expanded. | Certified parts cost one side; `edges: false` drops the lines; `instanced` for a model of repeated bricks. |
| 3MF materials (`@margoengine/loaders/threemf-materials`, 2026-11-06) | By method: `multiproperties` blend methods are read as mix, and only the first texture layer of a row is kept. | VTK XML (`@margoengine/loaders/vtk-xml`, 2026-11-06) | By method: `.vtp` and `.vtu` only, so image, rectilinear and structured grids are `unsupported`; LZMA blocks need `@margoengine/decoders`. | Rhino 3DM (`@margoengine/loaders/3dm`, 2026-11-06) | By method: reads meshes, saved render meshes, NURBS surface objects and solids that are one plain surface. | Long-tail formats (`/3ds`, `/tds`, `/lwo`, `/amf`, `/md2`, `/pdb`, `/kmz`, 2026-11-06) | By method: 3DS returns cameras, lights and keyframes as data and plays nothing; LWO skips curves and clips that are not still images, reads patch and subdivision polygons as their control cage, and returns bones and weight maps as data, with no real rigged file behind them (a built file is the stand-in); AMF skips curved edges and colour formulas; MD2 computes its normals; PDB loads the first MODEL; KMZ places models only with `origin`, takes altitudes as height above the WGS84 ellipsoid, puts `clampToGround` at height 0 and reads models only. `.tds` is 3DS under a second extension, so this list is six formats. | PCX (`@margoengine/decoders/pcx`, 2026-11-06) | Enforced: 8 bits in 1, 3 or 4 planes, 4 bits in 1 plane, 1 bit in 1 or 4 planes; every other layout, and a header whose line size is too short for its width, is refused. `maxPixels` defaults to 2^26. | Real files (`npm run test:real-files -w @margoengine/loaders`, 2026-11-06) | By method: 124 public files from real tools, one or two per format, are listed by URL and hash in `packages/loaders/tests/real-files/manifest.json` and are not in the repository. | Refused by design on real files (2026-11-06) | By method: `parseUSDA` and `parseUSDZ`, without the `composition()` extension, refuse USDC, subdivision surfaces and arcs to other layers with code `unsupported`. `parseTTF` refuses CFF outlines in `.otf` fonts. `parseDXF` skips `3DSOLID` (binary ACIS) and `HATCH`, and names them in `skipped`. `parseVTK` does not read `LINES`. `parseXYZ` keeps 32-bit floats with no origin, so survey coordinates lose precision: the swisstopo file's metres near 2,600,000 round to steps of 0.25 m. `parseSTL` keeps a file's stored normals, even where they oppose its winding, as `Spider_ascii.stl`'s do, so such a file draws dark. | `@margoengine/usdz` is the full USD reader, and the rest need a solid modelling kernel or a change to the shared result. | Those files load as named errors, or with parts counted as skipped. | `@margoengine/usdz` for USD; `parseLAS` keeps an origin for survey data. |
| USD composition (`@margoengine/usdz/compose`, 2026-11-06) | By method: sublayers, references, payloads, inherits, specializes and variant sets, across text and binary layers and `.usdz` packages, with layer offsets, list edits and `timeCodesPerSecond` scaling. | USD time samples (`@margoengine/usdz/anim`, 2026-11-07) | By method: `timeSamples` on `xformOp`s and `visibility`, as one clip per stage; at most 4,096 keys added between two samples. | USD subdivision (`@margoengine/usdz/subdiv`, 2026-11-07) | Enforced: `level` 0 to 6, default 2; a stage over `maxTriangles` gets a lower level for every mesh, and says so. By method: meshes refine to the level, not to the limit surface. `loop` takes triangles only; other faces refine as `catmullClark`. A face that crosses itself stays a fan, as it has no inside to clip. A value shared by faces that touch only at a point counts as one value: in mode `none` it stays sharp, and Blender gives one such value sharp and the other split, so those two runs differ (10 corners at level 1, up to 2.5e-2). Blender splits a value where faces turn opposite ways in UV space, and this entry keeps it one value, as the file has it: of 109 real meshes with mirrored or zero-area UV faces 41 match Blender and 68 differ, by up to 3.13e-1 near the folds. | NURBS (`@margoengine/loaders/nurbs`, 2026-11-06) | By method: checks plain data and tessellates it on the one evaluator of `@margoengine/geometry/nurbs`, which `parseDXF` uses for SPLINE too. | Download size of the LAS and LAZ readers (`@margoengine/points`, 2026-11-06) | Measured with `npm run quality -- --gate=sizes`, min+gzip. | LAS and LAZ (`@margoengine/loaders/las`, `@margoengine/points/las`, 2026-11-06) | By method: one reader, in `points`; `loaders/las` is a thin layer over it. Formats 0 to 10 equal LASzip and lazrs record for record and field by field on real files (`packages/points/tests/laz-real.test.js`). Stand-in proof only, on the test encoder: compressor 0, compressor 1 with version 2 items, and chunk size 0, because no tool here writes them. Refused with code `unsupported`: LAZ item version 1, coders other than arithmetic, compressors above 3, chunk table versions other than 0, waveform samples that are compressed or not 8, 16 or 32 bits. An extra bytes type above 30 is a `header` error. A LAS 1.4 compatibility mode file reads as stored, not remapped. Positions are 32-bit floats relative to `origin`. | Item version 1 is the coding of LASzip 1.0. The LAZ specification 1.4 R1 calls it outdated and leaves it out, the LASzip paper says it does not describe it, and the clean room rule keeps LASzip's source closed. The specification leaves compatibility mode out too. | Older LASzip files stay closed: three real samples of them were seen. `/las` in `loaders` takes whole files, so a file larger than memory does not open there. | Compress the file again with a current LASzip, or pass `decompress` with a decoder of your own. `loadLAS` of `points/las` streams from a URL; `step` thins a cloud; `maxVertices` refuses one past the limit. |
| OpenVDB volumes (`@margoengine/loaders/vdb`, 2026-11-06) | By method: file versions 222 and later; `float`, `double`, `int32`, `int64`, `vec3s`, `vec3d`, `vec3i` and half grids; uncompressed, zlib and Blosc with LZ4. Other grids and frustum transforms are left out. NanoVDB is not read. Proved on OpenVDB's sample sphere, smoke and fire files, version 222, half floats and two grids in one file, and on a file OpenVDB 13 wrote, version 225, with Blosc, float, double and vector grids: active counts, boxes and sampled values equal what OpenVDB reads (LIM-202). `bool` and mask grids and point data go to `skipped`. | No published byte-level specification, so a file version past 225 may need a new look; the original opt-in files stay out of the repository. | MaterialX and Lottie (`@margoengine/loaders/materialx`, `/lottie`, 2026-11-06) | By method: MaterialX converts four surface shaders and the nodes node materials can hold; emission, opacity, procedural nodes, `uvtiling`, includes and custom nodedefs do not convert; shader defaults match the published nodedefs, with `standard_surface` 1.0.0 taken by `version` or `nodedef`, and `realitykit_pbr_surfaceshader` shares the `UsdPreviewSurface` defaults with no published definition checked. The MaterialX output has not been compared with a reference renderer. | Node materials are a closed set of nodes; a Lottie frame here is paths and images, and those features need a compositor. | MaterialX names each loss in `skipped`, and Lottie each feature in `unsupported`, except expressions. | Bake the feature in the authoring tool, or build the graph with `@margoengine/materials` by hand. |
| Range cache (`@margoengine/cache/ranges`, 2026-11-07) | Proved in a real browser (Chromium and Edge, 2026-11-07): gltf-pro's own streaming code (`GLTFStream`) reads the real SheenChair.glb through `RangeCache.fetch` with the browser's IndexedDB, and its buffers equal the file cold, offline after a reload and when revalidated; the Node tests cover the rest on stand-ins. Not yet run in a service worker, and not timed. By method: blocks are 64 KiB by default; eviction is per file and reads every file's record (one per file, not per block) before each write; two requests in flight at once that share a block both fetch it. | Blocks let a streamed file be stored as it is read, without the whole file. | A cold request is widened to whole blocks, at most one block more on each side. A request needing a block never fetched fails offline. | Use `AssetCache` to store whole files; a smaller `block` widens requests less. |
| Vary keys (`varyKeys` in `@margoengine/cache/vary`, 2026-11-07) | Proved on stand-ins: an in-memory IndexedDB and a stand-in server in Node; not yet run in a browser. By method: each URL and credential set remembers only the last `Vary` it saw; whether a request sends cookies is judged from its `credentials` mode and origin, as the cookies themselves cannot be read. | A page or worker cannot see cookies, and keeping one `Vary` per URL needs one record, not a list. | Without a `partition`, two users signed in with cookies on one browser profile share entries; after a server changes `Vary`, old entries wait for eviction. | Set `partition` to the signed-in user's id; `delete(url)` drops every entry of a URL. |
| Eviction index (`evictionIndex` in `@margoengine/cache/eviction`, 2026-11-07) | Proved on a real browser's IndexedDB (Chromium and Edge, 2026-11-07), counting the records each write reads: 2,000 files, then 30 writes read 120 records with the index and 60,030 without; not timed. By method: the database moves to IndexedDB version 2, and an AssetCache without the index can no longer open it. | An index on last use is how IndexedDB walks records in order without reading them all; the totals live in two records updated in the same transaction. | Opening such a database without the index sends every request to the network. | Open it with `evictionIndex()` every time, or use a new `name`. |
| Asset bundles (`AssetBundles` in `@margoengine/cache/bundles`, 2026-11-07) | Proved on stand-ins: an AssetCache over an in-memory IndexedDB and a stand-in server in Node; not yet run in a browser. By method: every file of a bundle is hashed once per session when loaded, so a load reads each file's bytes once more on the CPU; a file is stored under its URL plus `?v=<hash>`, so the server must serve that query. | Hashes make a file shared by bundles one stored copy and let a release change only what changed. | A first load each session spends CPU time hashing (SHA-256 in the browser's own crypto). | Leave a file out of the manifest to skip its check; it then caches by URL as plain AssetCache files do. |
| Freshness from Expires and Age (`freshness` of `AssetCache` in `@margoengine/cache`, 2026-11-07) | Proved on stand-ins: an in-memory IndexedDB and a stand-in server in Node; not yet run in a browser. By method: no heuristic freshness from `Last-Modified` (RFC 9111 section 4.2.2), so a file with no `max-age` or `Expires` is revalidated each session; `s-maxage` is ignored, as for any private cache. | A heuristic lifetime would serve files the server never said were fresh. `Age` and `Date` are not CORS-safelisted, so cross-origin they count only when exposed. | Cross-origin without exposed `Age` and `Date`, a file is taken as new when it arrives. | Expose `Age` and `Date` (`Access-Control-Expose-Headers`), or send `max-age`; `freshness: 'max-age'` keeps the old rule. |
| Prioritized prefetch (`Prefetcher`, `throttle` in `@margoengine/cache/prefetch`, 2026-11-07) | Proved on stand-ins: stand-in servers, a stand-in `requestIdleCallback` and an in-memory IndexedDB in Node; not yet run in a browser. By method: `throttle` paces reading of response bodies, not the socket, so it holds the rate only once the browser's receive buffers are full; a priority is fixed once a request starts. | A page cannot set the socket's rate; reading slower makes TCP flow control slow the sender. | The first buffers of a download arrive faster than the cap. | Lower `concurrency`, or `pause()` while the app streams something itself. |

### React page

What a minimal React page downloads, and why it is larger than core + stage (23,924 B gzip). The cube page of the
bundler matrix (`Canvas`, `Mesh`, `BoxGeometry`, `PbrMaterial`, `useFrame`, and `OrbitControls` from
`@margoengine/react/controls`), built by Vite 8.3.4, React 19.3 and `@margoengine/react` installed alone with
`@margoengine/controls` (2026-10-27), measured from the build's source maps (minified bytes per package; gzip is each
package's own gzip size, scaled so the parts add up to the chunk's). Core lights every scene by default
(a sun and an ambient term), so this is also the minimal lit page.

| Part | Minified B | Gzip B | Needed for a lit scene? |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `react-dom` (client) | 206,925 | 62,263 | Yes: the app's own UI runtime, not Margo's |
| `react` + `scheduler` | 11,635 | 4,430 | Yes: the app's own |
| `@margoengine/core` (engine, renderer, Wasm kernel, camera, shaders, geometry) | 49,485 | 19,056 | Yes |
| `@margoengine/react` (components, internal, assets, the shadows hook) | 14,241 | 5,488 | Yes: `Canvas`, `Mesh` and the hooks |
| `@margoengine/stage` | 2,771 | 1,405 | Not to draw (core draws and lights the cube); `Canvas` wraps its engine in the stage it hands to `onCreated` and `<Stage>` |
| Vite runtime (preload helper, module preload polyfill), app code and `@margoengine/math` (170 B) | 3,135 | 1,609 | The build's own |
| **Entry, requested before the page runs** | **288,234** | **94,251** | Budget 100,000 B gzip |
| `@margoengine/controls/orbit` + its view helpers + profiles, when `OrbitControls` mounts | 17,999 | 6,951 | Yes, for orbiting |
| **Everything the page fetches** | **306,233** | **101,202** | |

React and React DOM are 66% of the page; Margo's part (core, stage, bindings) is 25,949 B gzip (27,028 B before the
stage feature entries and the React subpaths of 2026-10-27, which took 3,089 B of minified loaders out of the stage). Nothing optional is in
the entry: `PbrMaterial` is core's material and pulls in no other package.

- **Fixed (2026-10-26):** `OrbitControls`, `MapControls` and `CadControls` loaded the `@margoengine/controls` index,
  so mounting them fetched TransformControls, DragControls, the gizmo and the `@margoengine/bvh` raycaster as one
  112,655 B (39,072 B gzip) chunk. They now load `@margoengine/controls/orbit` and `/profiles`, `ArcballControls`
  loads `/arcball` and `TransformControls` loads `/transform`: the mount costs 6,951 B gzip, and a Vite build emits
  107,027 B gzip in all instead of 135,875 B.
- **Emitted, never fetched:** the arcball chunk (3,192 B gzip). Nothing else: since 2026-10-27 neither `Canvas` nor
  the stage reaches an optional package, so there are no stand-in stubs either.
- **A textured model** (`<Gltf src="BoxTextured.glb">` from `@margoengine/react/gltf-pro`, with `@margoengine/gltf-pro`
  installed): the entry grows by
  1,750 B gzip (the `Model` binding), and mounting it fetches gltf-pro (175,257 B, 56,074 B gzip: glTF parsing, the
  PBR material and shader, compression hooks) plus the model. The Draco and Basis Wasm are emitted for files that use
  them; this one does not, and the page does not request them.
- **Through `margoengine/react`:** a page emits no Draco or Basis file. `Model`, `Fbx`, `Animation` and the `materials`
  components reach those decoders, so they are separate entries (`margoengine/react/gltf-pro`, `/fbx`, `/animation`,
  `/materials`); Vite copies a `new URL` file when it reads a module, before tree-shaking.
- **Through a kit or `materials`, `animation`, `fbx`:** no Draco or Basis file either. Only the root of `@margoengine/gltf-pro`
  names the decoders; packages that draw models use `@margoengine/gltf-pro/model`, and `loadGLTF` is imported from
  `margoengine/gltf-pro`, not from `margoengine/game`, `/web` or `/viz`.
- Still on the controls index: `PointerLock` (from `@margoengine/react/controls`), because `@margoengine/controls` has no
  pointer-lock entry; a page that does not use it never emits it.

## External video materials (2026-11-08)

`@margoengine/video/material` adds a caller-owned `HTMLVideoElement` or `VideoFrame` to a `Material.features` list. No JS-side frame upload occurs. The browser/driver may still copy or convert internally; platform zero-copy and throughput are unmeasured. A frame is imported per draw, one sampler per device; there are no mipmaps or repeat wrapping. UV0 (default) and UV1 are supported; `flipY` defaults to true, matching Texture's image orientation (first row at v=1); false puts it at v=0. Sources must be ready/open and origin-clean. WebGL2 returns `MargoError` code `unsupported` with a help link. Core's compact material has no feature slot. Custom WGSL must retain the standard surface/base-colour hook. The existing material's own maps, lighting and other features keep their own costs. External textures consume four sampled-texture slots, one implicit sampler and one uniform slot, in addition to the explicit filtering sampler; a fully mapped material can exceed a device's default limits. Alpha affects colour rendering; auxiliary caster/picking passes retain the material's existing alpha inputs. Generated colour frames and a canvas MediaStream on the RTX A6000/Edge prove imports across tasks, no material-path frame uploads and sRGB byte accuracy within 2 of 255 at 1x and 4x MSAA. Real movie files, other adapters, browser-internal copies, speed and custom shader combinations are unmeasured. Run `node scripts/gpu-lock.mjs run --owner=video-check -- node packages/video/test/material-check.mjs` after a package build.

## Page canvas recording (2026-11-08)

`@margoengine/video/record` records origin-clean page canvases with MediaRecorder, on WebGPU, WebGL2 or 2D. Container support and codecs are the browser's choice: default WebM, optional MP4, otherwise coded unsupported with a help link. The caller supplies optional live audio tracks, cloned so originals remain owned by the caller. No audio mixing is performed. All compressed chunks stay in memory until stop. Real-time capture can drop frames or shorten media on a busy/background page; no exact duration/frame count or A/V synchronization bound is claimed. Stop waits for the final chunk; abort, disposal and errors release owned tracks and discard the result. No Node/OffscreenCanvas API or alternate codec fallback is included. The real RTX A6000/Edge check decodes WebM (VP8/Opus) and MP4 (H.264/Opus) from both backends: generated colour and a tone are stand-ins. Other browsers, players, codecs, microphone permission paths and long recordings are unmeasured. Entry 1,140 B gzip; budget 1,396 B. No speed claim. See LIM-571.

## 360 and stereo video (2026-11-08)

`@margoengine/video/360` uses UV0 of `sphereGeometry`, an unlit back-sided material and a camera at its centre. Image centre -Z, right +X, top +Y. Mono (default) spans the whole source; stereo-left-right holds one complete panorama per half, selected explicitly for a screen material (eye left by default). Stereo sources need at least two pixels across, enforced before binding. Sampling clamps half a texel inside each eye; no mips or repeat wrapping. WebGL2 receives coded unsupported with a help link. One video feature per material; playback and source lifetime remain caller-owned. XR reuses native `XRLayers.video` with an equirectangular sphere, automatic compositor eye choice and radius 0 at infinity; it requires the draft WebXR Layers API and XRMediaBinding. Missing XR support propagates the existing XR error. Generated colour panoramas prove six screen directions and both eyes on RTX A6000/Edge; an integrated stand-in session/binding proves XR delegation and layer lifecycle. No headset, real movie, other browser/GPU or speed evidence. Entry 1,694 B gzip, budget 1,881 B. LIM-573.

## Own 2D certified geometry and solver evidence (2026-11-08)

The optional Rust kernel's exact rectangle SAT path requires a current canonical axis rectangle in pair-local
coordinates, finite vertex squared norms at most 2^120 and B-normal squared norms at most 4. The preferred-face
distance certificate additionally requires a coordinate-magnitude bound M in [1,2^20], positive finite A-face
separation and its finite radius/speculation/result checks. These restrict eligibility for an optimization;
all other inputs retain the full prior collision path. [Proof](architecture/physics2d-manifold-proof.md) and
[entry 101](whitepaper/perf-history.md) record the precise guards and unchanged native/Wasm hashes.

The two-point block solver remains production behavior. Earlier per-point alternatives did not meet all contracts
and establish a browser gain. All original accuracy bars remain unchanged. The subsequent sustained-support fix
establishes the required centered 1:1000 contact stack and deliberately re-pins the mixed scene; see the
[support contract](#own-2d-sustained-contact-support). Owned-2D CCD remains separate T-11 / 127.y work, distinct
from existing 1000:1 joint-chain and 3D CCD evidence.
After browser diagnostics: Edge 3.66/1.69/14.52 ms and Firefox 3.50/1.52/11.20 ms for Margo/Box2D/Rapier; separate
loaded sessions cannot prove before/after speed. The Box2D goal remains open and quiet reruns are required.

### Own 2D input validation

The raw Rust kernel under `packages/physics2d/kernel` exposes checked `Result<_, PhysicsError>` body/shape/chain
creation, world stepping and handle operations, bounds queries, scalar/coherent/four-pair and smooth-chain collision.
The public Rust `solver::solve` entry also checks current inputs and derived outputs; its direct-call substep
must be positive and representable. `World::step` retains its validated nonpositive-step no-op policy.
Use `?` to propagate a refusal, or read `PhysicsError::code()` and `help()`; the latter points to this section.
The Rapier-backed TypeScript facade is a separate API. Pure math and mass-property utilities are not all checked
entry points; in particular, `mass::mass_of` retains its direct `MassData` return.

| Code | Refusal |
| --- | --- |
| `PHYSICS2D_NOT_FINITE` | A required finite input or current-state value is NaN or infinite |
| `PHYSICS2D_INVALID_CORE` | An invalid active core count or radius would make collision data unsafe to index or use |
| `PHYSICS2D_DEGENERATE` | A requested shape/chain has insufficient usable geometry |
| `PHYSICS2D_ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW` | Derived arithmetic cannot represent a required finite value, including positive mass/inertia lost to underflow or an overflowing reciprocal |
| `PHYSICS2D_INVALID_HANDLE` | A body, shape, contact or joint relationship refers outside the current valid objects |
| `PHYSICS2D_INVALID_PARAMETER` | A checked parameter violates its domain, such as negative density, friction or restitution |

Body definitions, collision poses and speculative cutoffs require finite used values. Shape material values are
finite and nonnegative. There is no geometry-independent minimum positive density: shape and aggregate mass,
inertia, moments, centres, extents and required reciprocals must remain representable in their actual arithmetic.
This includes the reciprocal of a positive inverse mass/inertia: a finite first reciprocal can round to a value
whose inverse overflows. Both the rounded centre and reconstructed origin are checked before publication.
Derived contact normal/tangent metrics and their required inverses must also be finite: two individually valid
inverse masses can overflow when added. Such a contact returns `PHYSICS2D_ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW` before solving.
Computed contact-point relative velocity, normal approach and anchor base are also checked; finite body velocity
alone does not imply a representable `v + w cross r` at a very large contact arm.
Nonzero finite rotation pairs use scale-safe normalization when their squared length overflows or underflows;
ordinary normalization bits are retained. Exact zero pairs in a body definition retain the documented identity
conversion. A directly mutated zero stored body rotation is `PHYSICS2D_INVALID_PARAMETER`; a nonfinite or zero
rotation derived during integration returns the arithmetic error rather than becoming identity or zero silently.
An infinite density and a unit box at `f32::from_bits(1)` are refused before publishing a shape or NaN centre.
Genuine zero density or zero-area geometry keeps its zero-mass behavior; a positive mass/inertia rounded to zero
cannot take that fallback. A dynamic body with no mass retains the existing 1 kg, no-turn fallback.

Body/shape creation and an entire `create_chain` call are transactional for validation/arithmetic failures:
no partial body, shape list, mass state or chain proxies are published, and refused IDs remain available.
`World::step` preflights current public mutable data and relationships before simulation work: body state and
shape lists, current core counts/used vertices/normals/radii, materials/chain ghosts, contact handles/counts/used
values and joint handles/state. A stale broad-phase shape ID is checked before callback indexing. A linear
visitation check over shape references refuses duplicate, missing and foreign-body references.
Used cached normal impulses must be nonnegative. Friction retains the ordinary product/sqrt result when that
product is finite and uses a scale-safe geometric mean when it overflows. Invalid derived scalar or SIMD clamp
bounds propagate to the step's coded arithmetic-error check, rather than asserting inside Rust's clamp.
These checks use current data. Explicit documented sentinels, such as a joint motor's
positive-infinite maximum force for an unlimited motor, remain supported. A later simulation arithmetic error
is returned to the caller; the whole step is not a rollback transaction.

At `47f81f909`, the reproduced collision panic requires both a NaN pose and NaN cutoff: a missing closest-distance
candidate leaves a zero hit mask, whose trailing-zero index escapes the candidate rows. The literal NaN-pose
review call with a finite cutoff returned an empty manifold here. The fix rejects nonfinite public inputs and
checks missing face/distance candidates internally, including the four-pair path; it does not treat invalid
input as an ordinary empty contact. Native regressions cover both forms, overflow, current-array mutations,
creation rollback and valid retained-reference results. Each existing Wasm `check(i)` also exercises invalid
input refusal before comparing the same three production hashes. No hash was re-pinned and no speed result is
claimed. [Reproduce](whitepaper/reproduce.md#own-2d-input-validation) lists the commands and baseline failures.

Input validation closes the input/publication and absent-candidate error class. The separately derived support
correction below establishes the required centered contact bar. Owned-2D CCD is separate T-11 / 127.y work.

## Frame-accurate video decoding (2026-11-08)

Optional `@margoengine/video/codecs` fully buffers nonfragmented, self-contained, unencrypted AVC avc1 MP4. It reads the first video track, one sample description, stsz/stsc/stco/co64/stts/ctts/stss and a rate-1 media edit optionally after an empty edit, including 64-bit headers and edit versions 0/1. Movie times have microsecond precision; colliding timestamps are refused. Each request decodes from sync through the GOP, flushing reordering, selecting the requested timestamp and closing other frames. Requests are exclusive and abortable; caller closes returned frames. Edits expose only frames whose PTS starts inside the media edit; empty lead-in clamps to the first visible frame. No audio, streaming, playback scheduler, arbitrary edits, fragmented MP4, WebM, other codecs, rotation/display transforms or external media references. Large files/long GOPs can need substantial memory/CPU. WebCodecs/AVC support is browser-specific and checked; renderer independent, including beside WebGL2 (the external material remains WebGPU-only). Unit stand-ins prove reordered sample tables, edit boundary regression and ownership. Generated AVC MP4 is decoded/rendered on RTX A6000/Edge. The outside CC0 MDN flower clip adds 150 real AVC High frames with B-frame reordering: every edited timestamp matches FFprobe and all 150 copied decoded-frame byte arrays match the independently demuxed WebCodecs reference exactly. This shares the browser decoder and is not cross-decoder accuracy proof. Edit bounds use exact native ticks, with one microsecond rounding after edits; source decode timestamps must also remain unique. Other browsers/GPUs and speed unmeasured. Entry 3,458 B gzip, unchanged budget 3,593 B. LIM-575.

## Own 2D sustained contact support

The recovery cap applies to the combined elastic residual, `max(beta*s+C*lambda,-P)`, rather than penetration
bias alone. For positive recovery speed P, stationary positive support retains the original spring root
`beta*s+C*lambda=0`: the cap imposes no finite force ceiling on feasible, representable loads. This is not an
unbounded floating-point magnitude or arbitrary-geometry stability guarantee. P=0 retains disabled recovery
and may have nonunique overpenetrated stationary states; the coupled correction declines it.

The coupled equilibrium correction is limited to a certified dynamic contact path with one static terminal.
It retains physical masses and the original compliance. Branches, cycles, multiple anchors, joints,
kinematic/sleeping terminals, nonzero restitution, original separating motion, open rows, unsupported gravity
wrenches or uncertified ranks use general capped dynamics. Current geometry, unilateral/friction feasibility,
finite arithmetic, casts, rotations and residuals are certified before an atomic component commit. Recovery
displacement uses the existing P*h substep budget. Sleep observes actual substep pose rate as well as final
relaxed speed, with unchanged thresholds/time and island propagation.

All 29 native physical bars pass, including the unchanged 1:100 and required 1:1000 centered contact predicates,
100-row pile sag, slope creep, bounce, friction, joints and sleep. The 1:1000 result is 0.518550681 m sag versus
0.518550736 m closed form, zero final displacement from the one-second sample, asleep at 0.8833334 s. The
unchanged regression fails on verified main 47f81f909: 1.186208290 m sag and 92.105 mm creep. The mixed-scene pin changes
intentionally from `9acb68471fbe6ba0` to `92db6847c4e919d4`; pyramid/joint-grid pins are unchanged.
The same two stack predicates run inside Wasm `check(0)`; native scalar/SIMD and shipped Wasm SIMD agree on
the stack metrics. Wasm always selects SIMD even when its stored `contact_lanes` setting is false.

The preserved geometry-dependent point spring has a negative local bending direction in the sagged 1:1000
column under small lateral perturbations, independently differentiated and checked with Margo's own manifolds.
Centered axial acceptance does not establish arbitrary lateral stability. No artificial angular stiffness or
mass threshold was fitted to hide it. See the [support derivation](architecture/physics2d-support-proof.md),
[bending analysis and executable probe](architecture/physics2d-support-bending.md), and
[reproduction commands](whitepaper/reproduce.md#own-2d-sustained-support).

The normal solver's finite-predicate reduction relies on actual private caller dataflow, not arbitrary
independent helper arguments. It preserves the same accepted/exceptional lane masks, raw-row and used-soft
domain checks, cap membership, post-motion finiteness and coded errors. The
[IEEE proof and compiler inventory](architecture/physics2d-finite-certificates.md) state those restrictions;
static predicate counts do not establish dynamic instruction counts or a browser speed gain.

The frame planner is linear in bodies, contacts and joints. Its flat graph/path/gap buffers retain capacity
bounded by historical maximum body/contact counts, rather than per-body or per-component capacity maxima.
Current graph contents, eligibility and weights rebuild each frame. General branching graphs skip the extra
substep path work; accepted components still use local allocations and two banded factorizations each substep.
Retaining scratch memory trades its lifetime for fewer allocation calls; this is not an allocation-free world
or a Box2D speed-parity claim. CCD remains outside this correction.

## 2D global illumination (batch 55)

Optional `@margoengine/lighting2d/gi` evaluates 1..8 spatial cascades, 1..32 base directions, angular ratio 1..8,
interval ratio >1, base distance >0, 0..4 finite diffuse bounce orders, albedo 0..1, intensity >=0. Defaults are
4/4/4/4/16/1/.5/1 respectively. World probe spacing doubles from one unit; centres are on the .5 lattice.
The far interval ends at baseDistance * intervalRatio ** (cascades - 1), which must fit float32.
Radiance/transmittance merges trace each of four child connectors before interpolation (RASTI appendix A).
Two-sided surface patches are at most baseDistance long; diffuse gathers use 32 normalized cosine samples and
midpoint-constant patch radiance. Surface gathers offset origins by .001 world units and ignore ray/edge
intersections at distances <= .0001 to avoid self-intersection. Small sources and spatial detail below those samples can be missed. The analytic
radius-six circular-source test over eleven distances 8..60 is within 5% of asin(radius/distance)/pi on CPU and RTX A6000;
this is a measured fixture bound, not an arbitrary-scene accuracy guarantee. No speed claim.
Patch count is capped at 65,536. The CPU hierarchy has an 8,000,000 sample-evaluation ceiling per query/grid.
GPU scene/cascade buffers must each fit maxStorageBufferBindingSize and 1D dispatch groups must fit
maxComputeWorkgroupsPerDimension; excessive combinations throw a coded RangeError instead of truncating work.
Cascade memory is 16 bytes per spatial/angular sample; two surface fields use 64 bytes per patch, plus 32 bytes
geometry per patch, 32 per emitter, 96 per direct light, masks and aligned per-dispatch uniforms.
CPU/GPU options, finite bounce orders, exact opaque visibility/energy fixtures and lifecycle are tested. Native WebGL2
rejects with coded unsupported/help. HDR needs a floating target; an unorm target clamps at presentation. LIM-599.

## Emissive sprites and bloom hookup (batch 55)

## Audio occlusion and obstruction (batch 110)

Optional audio/occlusion uses five CPU rays (one with radius 0) and interpolated gain/low-pass filtering. Radius 0..100 m, default 0.25; blocked gain 0..1, default 0.25; cutoff 10..min(20000, Nyquist) Hz, default 800; smoothing 0..60 s, default listener.smoothing. Source and followed-listener meshes are excluded; each segment excludes 1 mm at both ends. Sampled aperture, not diffraction, physical transmission, material/thickness modelling, reflections or reverb-send control. Visible CPU triangles only; alpha masks and arbitrary shader deformation are absent, active skin/morph needs a static proxy. World matrices and sound/listener poses must be current before explicit update. Keep the sound filter chain in place while active.

Real Edge 157 audio renders beside native WebGPU, WebGL2 and WebGL2 compatibility engines show 2 kHz blocked/clear RMS 0.039128 and 100 Hz 0.249970 with zero GPU validation errors. ## Ambisonic beds (batch 110)

Optional audio/ambisonics: 1,919 B gzip; audio root 7,638 B and core plus stage 23,837 B. First-order four-channel ACN/SN3D W,Y,Z,X buffers only, positive finite duration, explicit convention assumption. Default format ambix; other conventions/channel counts produce linked unsupported. No FuMa/N3D/A-format conversion, higher/mixed orders, appended stereo, CAF adaptor or Opus metadata parser. Loading delegates to existing listener.load with AbortSignal and browser codec support; four-channel 24-bit PCM WAV with 44.1-to-48 kHz resampling is tested.

Default loop true, volume 1 within 0..1, smoothing listener.smoothing (default 0.02 s finite nonnegative time constant). Eight gain paths, one source, splitter and stereo merger per bed. Identity ACN front/left/up maps engine -Z/-X/+Y. Normalized copied world quaternion rotates field; listener forward/up define the inverse head orientation, translation ignored. Collinear directions retain the last independent decoder orientation (initially -Z forward, +Y up). Camera following copies camera.up, including roll and exact poles. Two virtual cardioids at +/-30 degrees output 0.5*(W+direction dot XYZ) times volume. This is stereo ambience, not HRTF/binaural localization or arbitrary loudspeaker decoding. Gain interpolation blends matrices rather than remaining a rigid rotation during fades. Author seamless loops and headroom. Start at/after now; stop/restart resets phase. Listener teardown/dispose cuts sources and frees decoder nodes, preserving buffers.

LIM-610: Node full yaw/elevation/roll basis and lifecycle checks, and real browser PCM on all three routes for generated independent-channel tones/loops and a licensed external rain-stimulus excerpt, each within 1e-6 of float64 channel matrices with zero GPU errors. XR apps feed headset world forward/up through existing listener.setPose; physical headset tracking, subjective localization, other browsers/devices and performance unmeasured.

### Scatter interaction numeric limits (batch 77 audit)

LIM-604 retains its field-size, resolution and 4,096-interactor limits. Every position has three finite f32
components; radius, bend, size and resolution/size must fit positive normal f32 (at least 2^-126), so permitted
subnormal flushing cannot zero a divisor. Strength is a number in [0,1]. A rejected update keeps the last successful
interactors. Shifts beyond the field's side discard its old pushes without signed 32-bit wrapping. Floating-point
world precision still applies; the field reads XZ and does not simulate a physical explosion. The optional interact
entry measures 7,463 minified bytes / 3,318 B gzip with bare peers external. The budget rises from 3,206 to 3,574 B
(the measured entry plus the established 256 B headroom) for input validation, atomic updates, a bounded shift and
overflow-safe distance maths. Those extra checks and ALU preserve finite extreme inputs; no speed is measured.

## React Native target dropped (LIM-615)

React Native is not supported; batch 117 job 6 is dropped. Margo targets the web, including mobile browsers.
The planned native path is the Rust engine. A React Native target would require a native WebGPU surface and
Android/iOS toolchains and devices to prove rendering, loading and lifecycle behavior; this repository provides
no such proof. Checked 2026-11-09: Hermes's current [language feature documentation](https://github.com/meta/hermes/blob/static_h/doc/Features.md)
and [next stable release notes](https://github.com/meta/hermes/blob/static_h/doc/blog/2026-06-05-new-hermes-stable-release.md)
do not document supported WebAssembly execution. The Hermes author's [WebAssembly preview](https://tmikov.blogspot.com/2026/02/webassembly-comes-to-hermes_01829874520.html)
describes experimental execution, not production readiness. This is not a claim that Hermes cannot run Wasm;
neither the preview nor compiling Hermes itself to Wasm establishes Margo phone compatibility.

## Wasm Content Security Policy

A policy that restricts scripts must permit Wasm compilation with `script-src 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` for each Wasm-backed path, including core engine creation and stages. Worker response policies need the permission too. [CSP requirements](csp.md) list the exact header and entries. Blocked initialization reports MargoError code `failed` with a help link; unrelated binary, SIMD and fetch errors retain their identity.

### Lighting2d direct-pass storage and lifetime ceilings

- Rect, circle and polygon masks (including inversion) and layer filtering run on root, soft, cookie and height.
  Circle centres default to world `(0,0)`. Polygon vertices cost 16 bytes each and must fit `maxStorageBufferBindingSize`.
- Height occluders cost 48 bytes each; emissive sprites cost 64 bytes each. Both lists grow to the device storage binding
  limit; the former 64-item truncation is removed. Oversized lists throw before drawing.
- Height light uniforms cost `max(256, minUniformBufferOffsetAlignment)` bytes each, capped by `maxBufferSize`.
  Soft samples are integers 1..64. Cameras require finite values and positive zoom. Mutated lights/sprites are validated.
- Height directional shadow rays are capped at 10,000 world units; elevation for shadow projection clamps to
  `[0.01, PI/2 - 0.01]` radians. Circle footprints are analytic here; ordinary direct shadows use 24-sided circle edges.
- Emissive owns three full-resolution `rgba16float` textures, 24 bytes/pixel, plus caller output and any optional Bloom
  intermediates. HDR values may overflow half precision above 65,504; an unorm presentation clips above 1.
- Native WebGL2 is unsupported by every lighting2d entry. Tests assert the coded rejection rather than a rendered route.
  GPU evidence is one RTX A6000 only. Manually supplied command encoders must be submitted before pass disposal.

Lighting2d repaired entry bytes and exact approved ceilings (min+gzip, other packages external): root 5,394;
soft 5,901; cookie 7,350; GI 8,589; height 6,832; emissive 4,087 B. Scott approved these measured ceilings on
2026-11-09: "Approve new size". No headroom was added. The 293 B shrink retains all work and tests; the remaining
3,273 B over the old ceilings buys the correctness repairs itemized beside the lighting2d table rows above.
Every normal quality gate must pass before landing.

Height lighting accumulates in an owned rgba16float image (8 bytes per target pixel), then converts once to the caller format. Individual sums still have half-float blend precision. The 100-light .001 contribution regression is within one display byte.

Clearcoat job 2: full Khronos ClearCoatTest, 27 primitives, neutral/sRGB, identical camera and sun,
no IBL, 512 x 512. RGB-byte MAE 1.6809107462565105 WebGPU and 1.6809145609537761 WebGL2
compatibility, max 180. Native WebGL2 rejects PBR. Exact integer budgets and frozen hashes:
whitepaper/results/batch-160-clearcoat.json. The image residual remains an open defect, with
formulation differences recorded separately from its unisolated complete cause.

measures 8,234 minified / 3,401 B gzip, within its existing 3,415 B budget. Existing slots, per-tile, GPU binding and

Capacity budgeting includes the GPU's far-distance endpoint and uses uploaded f32 tile coordinates and camera

## Poisson disk placement (LIM-621)

Optional procedural/poisson: 1,335 B min+gzip JavaScript plus a lazy 29,914 B Wasm file (13,192 B gzip).
CPU-only on WebGPU and WebGL2. Rectangle or area-weighted triangle-soup darts, ambient Euclidean separation,
not geodesic spacing. Finite coordinates within +/-1,000,000; radius 0.000001..1,000,000; maximum 65,536 triangles,
65,536 returned points and 2,000,000 candidates. Defaults: seed 1, 4,096 points, 100,000 candidates.
Zero numerical area carries no probability, including cross products rounded to zero. Finite dart budgets need not
cover a domain or return the point limit. No spectral, maximal-covering or frame-time promise. Output is float64;
conversion to float32 can reduce separation. Signals precede synchronous sampling; workers enable in-flight aborts.
Synthetic fixtures and a float64 oracle prove spacing, bounds, area weighting and exact rejection output.
Real production-browser WebGPU/WebGL2 contexts prove lazy assets below a non-root base and independence from
device/context loss. Authored meshes, hardware speed and cross-platform bit identity are unmeasured.

## Caustic path guiding (batch 99, LIM-622)

`@margoengine/voxel-pathtracer/guiding` adds a pure diffuse continuation proposal toward the existing deflector
table: up to eight static orthogonal pure smooth non-dispersive glass instances and eight mirrors. Visible box
faces are sampled by world area; interior origins use enclosing faces, excluding any face containing the origin.
The PDF converts to solid angle and sums all overlapping bounds. Actual voxel traversal and Fresnel transport
remain unchanged. `guideStrength` is finite `0..0.95`, default `0.5`; zero uses the original kernel exactly,
and empty guide tables retain the baseline random stream. No learning, photons or persistent GPU allocation.

Roulette removes accumulated cosine/mixture factors from its survival heuristic so small importance weights
are not immediately discarded. The heuristic scale is bounded `1e-20..1e20`, with actual survival `0.05..1`
after bounce three and actual throughput divided by that survival. Ordinary bounce caps still truncate paths.
Bounds can contain empty geometry or point below the surface, producing zero-contribution proposals. Other
BSDFs, unsupported deflectors and geometry beyond the table retain ordinary path sampling. A geometry prior
can increase variance when its objects contribute little. No general convergence or wall-time gain is claimed.

`tests/guiding-browser.mjs` keeps a fixed 2x squared-RGB-error bar on a generated small-glass caustic at 64 samples
against a 16,384-sample guided reference, with separate independent original-tracer energy comparisons and an
analytic unit furnace. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility run the shader; native WebGL2 refuses with code
`unsupported` and a registered help link. Native device restoration and disposal are exercised.

Entry size with bare peers external: guiding 2,535 B gzip; new budget 2,791 B includes the standard 256 B headroom.
Root 80,431 B, studio 1,047 B, restir 1,934 B and core plus stage 23,837 B remain unchanged. No existing size,
accuracy or time gate was relaxed.

## WFC heap and chunks (batch 69)

Indexed heap, bitset domains and local restarts: 1..4096 tiles, <=1,000,000 cells, <=16,777,216 cell/tile pairs. Rust SIMD auto path requires <=32 unit-weight tiles; all other eligible inputs use TypeScript. One feature crate/artifact, lazily loaded with module-relative new URL; no import-time fetch. ## WFC worker solving (batch 69)

Local heap solves only, same grid/rule/pair/restart bounds and backend selection as chunks. One dedicated browser worker per job, rules/pins cloned, Uint16 result transferred. Main-thread cloning has a cost. Latest-only single-consumer progress is real work, not a percentage; restarts may revisit cells and Wasm counters wrap after 2^32-1. Defaults seed 1, pins empty, attempts 4, auto backend, signal absent and timeout 60000 ms including startup/loading; timeout integer 1..2147483647. Abort/dispose/timeout terminate active work and close progress; result must be awaited for errors. Stopping progress iteration leaves the solve running. Node/SSR construction is coded unsupported. Same-origin worker/CSP and Wasm support apply. Real rendering/progress/abort proof on WebGPU and WebGL2, no frame-time guarantee (LIM-624).

## Multiple-scattering tracer sky (batch 99, LIM-626)

The new optional `@margoengine/voxel-pathtracer/sky` imports the optional sky peer's existing `/hillaire` entry.
`traceSkyEnvironment` calls `bakeHillaireEnvironment`, returning a linear RGBA Float32 map plus a separate attenuated
sun. Bake defaults are 256x128, noon, altitude zero, sun illuminance 20, Earth, multiple scattering and stylized
night enabled. Width is 1..2048, height 1..1024 and storage must fit the device's buffers. Altitude is at most
100000000 metres, sun illuminance at most 1000000, coefficients/albedo at most 1, radii/heights at most 100000 km.
The existing 256x64 transmittance and 32x32 multiple LUTs feed a 64-step ray march per texel. Higher scattering orders
are isotropic, geometry spherical and the observer position fixed by altitude. Re-bake when settings change; this
environment adds no local atmospheric attenuation or aerial perspective. Night reuses the stylized gradient,
procedural stars and moon, time zero without twinkle; unresolved stars retain mean integrated light. It does not
include astronomical catalogues, Milky Way, spectral airglow or spectral transport. Numeric night magnitudes other
than normalized moon direction are at most 1000000. A plain WebGL2 context is refused with coded help; a WebGL2
compatibility device executes the same model. Native and compatibility values, analytic vacuum/ground, traced
lighting, cancellation, resource disposal and real native device restoration are recorded in
`docs/whitepaper/results/batch-99-sky-20261109.json`. No speed or reference-renderer equality claim.

Batch 99 sky entry sizes (bare peers external): lazy tracer sky 212 B gzip, sky Hillaire including the reusable
bake 10822 B; tracer root 80431 B and core plus stage 23837 B unchanged. Entry budgets use the standard
max(256 B, 3%) headroom; the strict core/stage limit remains 25000 B.

The environment bake requires Float32-distinct planet/atmosphere radii and vertical scattering optical depth
at most 6 in every channel (Rayleigh plus scattering Mie, integrated from ground to top). This keeps a
representable escape probability in the geometric-series LUT. Minimum observer clearance is 1 metre or
2 to 4 Float32 radius steps, whichever is larger. Night moonSize must be at least 0.000001 radians; narrower
discs are outside the bake domain. Both equirectangular dimensions determine the night filtering footprint.

## Tileable GPU texture baking (LIM-639)

The optional procedural/textures entry compiles one WebGPU compute pipeline and
bakes RGBA8 linear RGB, alpha 1. Native WebGL2 uses a lazy fragment pass on the
source engine canvas, returning an owned WebGLTexture and its gl context; native
WebGPU returns an owned GPUTexture. Neither handle crosses devices/contexts. Five
stylized patterns: periodic value noise, bricks, tiles, longitudinal wood-like
bands and rust-like threshold patches. No photographic, anatomical, corrosion or
PBR material accuracy is asserted. Four fixed noise periods 4,8,16,32, weights
8,4,2,1, quintic interpolation. Every preset shares a caller-set two-colour palette.
Defaults: bricks, 256 square, seed1, repeats[4,8], detail .2, grout .08, stagger .5,
color[.55,.2,.08], secondary[.15,.12,.1], offset[0,0]. Dimensions16..2048 and device
limit; repeats integer1..64, even brick rows; seed uint32; detail/stagger0..1;
grout0...45; RGB0..1; phase +/-1024 reduced modulo1. Repeat affects brick/tile cells
and wood bands, not fixed noise/rust octaves. No mipmaps or analytic antialiasing;
undersampled mortar/noise can alias. Use repeat-addressed sampling. Neighbouring
pixel centres across a repeat boundary are different samples of a periodic field.
Bakes are async and abortable; incomplete resources are released on failure, abort,
disposal or loss. A replacement device requires a new baker. Outputs are owned;
baker disposal destroys retained outputs. No CPU pixel loop or Wasm is involved.
44,415 GPU channel checks match an independent generated oracle within one RGBA8
quantization step. Integer phase translations are byte exact; one-texel shifts
cross both texture edges. Real WebGPU loss, in-flight abort/disposal and replacement
are tested. Native WebGL2 pixel/state/abort/disposal/loss/restoration tests use
the same one-channel-step tolerance. Mortar on an exact floating-point threshold
can differ across rasterizers. Numerical and lifecycle controls are stand-ins. External reference is
limited to a calibrated row-offset measurement from Lefebvre/Poulin 2000 Fig.1(d),
39/88 pitch with two source pixels of uncertainty, plus GPU raster quantization.
Original PDF/JPEG downloaded for measurement, never redistributed. No external
colour reconstruction, wood/rust realism, cross-device bytes or speed claim.
The WebGL2 shader chunk is lazy; no Wasm or external image asset is required.
Updated entry sizes are recorded with the test-page validation evidence below.
Core plus stage remains 23,837 B gzip, strictly below 25,000 B.

### Spectral transport and chromatic lens (batch 99 job 8, LIM-641)

Optional voxel-pathtracer/spectral traces one RGB path, then importance-samples one hero wavelength
in 380-780 nm only at the first dispersive glass interface or active chromatic camera lens.
Earlier contributions stay RGB, and a path without dispersion has no spectral colour noise. It scales dielectric
transmission by the squared incident/transmitted index ratio, retaining separate light-PDF Jacobians.
RGB coefficients remain RGB; the CIE weights do not reconstruct reflectance or emission spectra.
Captures with wavelength set are monochromatic with unit RGB weight; Albedo, normal and depth use hero samples; instance/palette IDs remain centre-ray values. Transparent alpha averages geometric coverage uniformly over wavelengths, or uses the fixed capture wavelength.

Lens settings are immutable at attachment: lensAbbe 0 or 5-200 (default 0), focalLength 1e-6-1e6 world
units (default 0.05). Only camera projection with nonzero aperture uses longitudinal chromatic power.
There is no lateral colour, physical lens stack, diffraction, lens transmission or measured optical
fidelity. Slope correction permits virtual/infinite wavelength focus without singular division.
One sample uses one traversal; no equal-cost convergence or speed claim. The spectralTransport factory
combines this entry with the other optional tracing features through /compose. Root glass and sampling limitations still apply.

Generated stand-in analytic transport and disk-edge tests run on native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility;
plain WebGL2 gives linked unsupported. The spectral transport repair measured 1083 B gzip (previously 1541 B);

### LIM-650: textured rectangle area lights

Optional `@margoengine/clustered/area-texture` (`AreaLightTextures`): an RGBA8 image on each `AreaLights` rectangle,
sRGB by default, alpha premultiplied. Enforced: at most 16 distinct images, 1,024 texels a side, 4,194,304 texels in all
with their level chains (`RangeError`); one entry per area light (64). The image is stored as half-float linear RGB in a
storage buffer (binding 153), so it adds no sampled texture or sampler. By method: the scalar LTC integral of each lobe
is multiplied by the image filtered over what that lobe sees: the lookup point is where the transformed rectangle's
vector form factor meets its plane, the level is the one whose texel spans the clamped cosine's half-peak footprint
(diameter 1.287 h over the square root of the area, both in the lobe's space), read trilinearly from a box-filtered
chain. It is an approximation: a one-colour image is exact (within half-float rounding, 2^-11), but a detailed image
under a wide lobe is the filtered mean around one point, not the exact integral of the image under the lobe; the
vector form factor ignores the horizon clip; level-0 texels are bilinear with clamped edges, and the chain is
isotropic, so a lobe stretched along one axis of the light reads one blur for both. Built from the LTC paper's integral
and the cosine footprint; the paper's own textured-light section could not be read (docs/clean-room.md, C19).
Proved on stand-ins: the CPU mirror (`packages/clustered/test/area-texture.test.js`) and a real-WebGPU frame check
(`scripts/clustered-light-images-gpu-check.js`: one-colour image against the plain light within 2/255, a split image
lights each side of the floor). No reference against a path tracer yet. Sizes: `npm run quality -- --gate=sizes`.

### LIM-654: light linking and layers

Optional `@margoengine/clustered/layers` (`LightLayers`): a 32-bit layer mask on each clustered point or spot light
(`setLayers`, default 1, layer 0) and on each receiver added through `LightLayers.add` (default 1); a light shades a
receiver when the masks share a bit. Enforced: masks are integers from 0 to 2^32 - 1 and at most 1,024 light masks, one
per clustered light (`RangeError`); a receiver once (`TypeError`). The light masks live in a storage buffer (binding
154); the receiver's mask is a constant in its own shader, so a receiver's layers cost no per-object data, and a change
of a receiver's layers recompiles its shader. By design: core meshes are on layer 0 only (core has no per-mesh slot for
a mask), and area and directional lights are not layered. With every mask 1 the hook is off and the shaders and GPU work
are unchanged. Proved on stand-ins: the CPU mirror (`packages/clustered/test/layers.test.js`: the mask truth table, the
shader rewrite, binding 154 only while needed) and the real-WebGPU `scripts/clustered-light-images-gpu-check.js` (a
layer-1 light leaves a layer-0 floor black, a layer-0 light leaves a layer-1 floor black, a floor on both layers matches
the unlayered light within 2/255). Sizes: `npm run quality -- --gate=sizes`.

### Height-aware grass interaction (batch 77 jobs 3 and 4)

Interactor radius is a sphere in world units, tested at each push-field cell's
bilinearly sampled heightmap height plus the scatter centre Y. Airborne spheres
that miss the surface add no push. The field still stores horizontal vectors,
interpolated at roots, over a camera-centred square; overhangs and multiple
