## Optional RT alpha limits

`bvh/alpha-triangles` preserves original face TEXCOORD_0/material provenance;
`shadows/rt-alpha` snapshots those data into one storage buffer. Five fragment
storage buffers are required, versus four for ordinary RT. WebGL2 and lower
WebGPU tiers use the existing map fallback. Storage costs 16 + 32*faces +
64*masks bytes plus each mask's alpha pixels padded to four bytes, with masks
deduplicated by identity. CPU images must be below 256 MiB and within the device's
buffer limits; each dimension is an integer 1..1,048,576. UV/transform values must
be finite float32; factor/cutoff are 0..1. Four times each masked face's absolute
affine UV bound must fit float32, including the offset, to prevent intermediate
overflow. Repack after UV/material/topology edits.
Core geometry is opaque; model skin/morph positions are bind pose. Unsupported
images/UV sets are reported by modelAlphaMasks.skipped and retain its opaque
policy. The real-GPU traversal/fragment and public Shadows.attach pixel proofs
pass for default/quarter-turn masks, restoration and fallback. RT far ends at
the configured distance; the map fallback instead uses the map's full reach.
Measured gzip entries: bvh root 23,362 / 23,398 B ceiling, bvh/gpu
5,582 / 5,738 B, bvh/alpha 16,513 / 16,873 B, shadows/rt 6,409 / 6,486 B.
New alpha-triangles is 1,125 B (1,381 B ceiling); rt-alpha is 8,739 B
(8,816 B ceiling). No existing ceiling rises. Core plus stage remains 23,924 B.

### Batch 56 review: finite studio directions
### Batch 56 review fixes: dominant HDR ground shadow

The optional staging/ground receiver approximates one distant light from the
luminance-weighted first radiance SH moment. It follows environment rotation;
multiple-light visibility, physical HDR light size, full radiometry, product
self-shadow and photographic floor reconstruction are outside this approximation.
It retains contact receiver dimensions, texture limits and spatial Gaussian blur.
At moment length <= 1e-6 * abs(luminance L0), intensity zero, or receiver-normal
cosine <= 1e-6, it draws no directional shadow. Very low lights need a wide
receiver; the configured rectangle clips long shadows. No CPU geometry loop,
new Wasm, core feature or speed claim is added. Native WebGL2 preview refuses;
WebGPU and the compatibility backend execute the same pass path.

Scene captures and explicit disposal use the owning scene. Viewport/scissor
are applied to the planar surface, image background and colour background;
local target passes keep local coordinates. Staging still idle/history keys
exclude temporal raster jitter, including zero idle delay. Studio softboxes
preserve finite extreme and subnormal directions by scaling before normalization.

TAA and TAAUpscale explicit disposal uses the owning scene; another scene's effect with the same name is preserved (batch 56 ownership audit).

## Batch 234 FFT ocean

The optional water `/fft` entry uses 16..512 Fourier samples per axis (powers
of two), 1..4 disjoint wavelength bands and a separate 1..1024-cell draw grid.
Its Gaussian linear Phillips/JONSWAP spectra use deep-water gravity dispersion,
periodic patches, choppy displacement, tangent normals and folding foam. DC
and the Nyquist row/column are omitted. Finite-depth dispersion, overturning
volumes and shoreline flow are not solved by this entry. Its square draw grid
is finite and follows the camera by default. A requested CPU snapshot is of
the last rendered frame; rendering never reads the GPU back. One read can be
pending. All buffers are rebuilt on device restoration. Details, size evidence
and correctness reproduction: [water-fft.md](water-fft.md).

The `/fft` entry is 7,334 B minified gzip (new ceiling 7,590 B); core + stage
is unchanged at 23,924 B in the full rebuilt measurement. Snapshot time,
mean height and patch lengths are binary32 GPU values, including rounding.

## Batch 234 wave queries

Optional `@margoengine/water/query` captures actual rendered Water/FFTOcean
geometry and performs synchronous CPU triangle queries. Highest overlapping
hits win; finite mesh edges and coastal dry masks can return undefined.
Macro normals exclude shading-only ripples and view-dependent underside
flipping. Particle velocity includes wave motion and conservative coastal
current; it is not Eulerian height rate or a boat solver. Snapshots retain
rendered time and need explicit refresh. Captures use the GPU and read back
48 B per vertex, 16 B per projected hierarchy node, and FFT/coastal source
fields (48/16 B per sample respectively), with temporary GPU staging memory.
The hierarchy handles arbitrary segment counts; no CPU FFT or geometry build.
Native/full compatibility evidence and remaining limits: [water-query.md](water-query.md).

### Batch 273 polygon offset clamp checkpoint

The optional compatibility device now loads EXT_polygon_offset_clamp and replays
slope, units and the signed depthBiasClamp together. Positive clamp is a minimum
with the computed offset, negative a maximum; zero disables clamping. The cache
includes clamp and replays reset to zero. Without the extension, nonzero clamp
refuses synchronous and asynchronous pipeline creation with code unsupported and
a help link before shader compilation. Zero-clamp offset remains supported.
No core or stage source or export changed; their gzip remains 23,924 B.
Device CPU regressions fail on the parent and pass after repair (13/13 device
tests). The complete compat render-state grid now finishes 596 checks and 278
captures: all positive and negative clamp pixels pass at 4x and 1x, including
material mapping. The two high-bit stencil failures remain open for the next
checkpoint; this is not a pass of failure 10 or a suite closure.
Receipts: whitepaper/results/batch-273-clamp-checkpoint.json and local
batch-273-clamp-{before,after,render-state} logs under test-results.

## Triangle-mesh lightmaps (batch 54)

`bakeMeshLightmap` (`@margoengine/lightmap/mesh`) bakes on the CPU, one mesh per call, at most 2,048 x 2,048 texels,
4,194,304 covered texels and 67,108,864 rays. Light is direct (with shadows) and AO; bounces, area and emissive lights
are in `./global` for quads only. Overlapping UV charts are counted (`overlaps`), not separated: the later triangle's
light is kept where both centres fall. Dilation averages neighbours across a gutter narrower than twice `dilate`, so
two charts closer than that blend in the gutter (never inside a chart). Overlaps under 1e-3 texels count as touching.

## Directional lightmaps (batch 54)

`bakeDirectionalLightmap` (`@margoengine/lightmap/directional`) stores one main light direction and one directional
colour per texel (world space), not SH or the H-basis: with several lights it is exact only at the unmapped normal and
approximate under a normal map (exact for one light plus ambient). Ambient light and AO are not directional. It takes
the `bakeMeshLightmap` limits and its direct-light-only scope; bounce light has no direction. The RGBA8 direction map
quantizes each component to 1/255 of 2. No GPU shader applies it yet: `directionalIrradiance` is the CPU reference.

## Lightmap rough glass, dispersion and bounce caustics (batch 54)

`bakeRefractedLightmap` (`@margoengine/lightmap/refracted`) rough glass is single-scattering: light the microsurface would
scatter again is dropped into `diagnostics.masked` (about 9% of a normal beam through a 1-unit slab at roughness 0.5,
53% at roughness 0.9), so very rough glass is too dark. Roughness is isotropic and per volume. Dispersion uses Cauchy's
two-term fit (no Sellmeier), wavelengths 380 to 780 nm with out-of-gamut colours clipped, and the event Fresnel at one
wavelength per photon. Bounces (at most 4) are diffuse and use the quad's albedo only (no `surface` callback, no
textures); receivers stay opaque.

## Lightmap irradiance probes (batch 54)

`bakeLightProbes` (`@margoengine/lightmap/probes`) bakes on the CPU, at most 64 probes per axis (262,144) and 67,108,864
rays, 16 to 16,384 gather rays per probe. Each probe is order-3 SH, so a strong light rings: a delta light gives about
6% of its irradiance straight behind it and 9% at 90 degrees, and `probeIrradiance` clamps below 0. The room's light
reaches probes only through its lightmap (one mesh), so one bounce beyond the lightmap; occluders reflect nothing;
emissive surfaces and area lights are not sampled. Probes have no visibility weighting (light can leak through thin
walls between probes), and `@margoengine/environment`'s `LightProbes` cannot load the baked coefficients yet.

## Lightmap denoising (batch 54)

`@margoengine/lightmap/denoise` runs on the CPU, at most 16,777,216 texels (8,192 a side) per call, 1 to 8 a-trous
passes of 25 taps each. It is not energy conserving (a weighted mean per texel, as Dammertz et al. 2010 note). Charts
are filtered separately: neighbouring quads in the world are not neighbours in the atlas, so quad charts a few texels
wide get little smoothing. Without a supplied `variance` the noise is estimated per texel from its neighbours (median
absolute deviation); smooth gradients count partly as noise and are smoothed slightly, and a lone bright texel (a
firefly) is averaged into its neighbours but not clamped. The quad atlas path reads the 8-bit lightmap, so its input
carries 8-bit quantisation; the mesh path reads the float `irradiance`.

## Path-traced lightmap bounces (batch 54)

`bakeGlobalLightmap({ bounceMode: 'path' })` traces at most 8 diffuse bounces, `bounceRays` (1 to 32) paths per texel,
on the CPU, within `maxRays`. Each path vertex reads the direct light of the texel it hits, at that texel's centre, so
light varying inside one texel is averaged (texel-sized bias); there is no Russian roulette (paths stop at `bounces`),
no glossy or metallic bounce (metals reflect nothing) and no light through glass on bounce paths. Quad charts are the
only input: triangle meshes (`./mesh`) have no bounces yet.

### Tile styling (batch 239 job 1)

`@margoengine/tiles/style` supplies `TilesStyle`: property expressions drive sRGB RGBA, show and pixel point size, with ordered conditions, defines and metadata expressions. The language supports scalar/vector math, comparisons, short circuiting, ternaries, arrays, property paths, interpolation, CSS colours and regular expressions. Expressions are limited to 65,536 characters, 4,096 tokens and 128 parser nesting levels. Wrong output types fail with a coded state error. No arbitrary host methods or JavaScript execution are allowed.

`TilesStyle.decorate` is the renderer's optional `decorate` hook; it binds loaded b3dm batch IDs, pnts batch IDs and point semantics, i3dm instance IDs, and structural attribute/implicit feature tables. Direct model, instance and point bindings accept a property resolver, update without accumulating tint, and restore their saved authored data on disposal. Model bindings follow PBRModel.writeGeometry's existing restrictions on deformed/shared geometry. PBR colours multiply authored vertex colours in linear light; point colours replace the cloud's colour channel. Style alpha uses the existing blend path. Property textures and feature ID texture sampling belong to the later batch jobs, rather than being advertised here. No core or stage source changes.

Entry size for batch 239 job 1: tiles/style is new, 0 to 9,755 B min+gzip; its recorded ceiling is 10,057 B. The interpreter, standard colour data and binding lifecycle remain one entry to avoid duplicated parser state or lifecycle code. Tiles root is 15,866 B and i3dm is 1,474 B, inside their existing ceilings. Core + stage remains 23,950 B. Authored CPU snapshots remain outside the existing GPU-only budget; the decorator adds only the new point colour/size GPU buffers, while model and instance buffers are already measured by their owners.

### FSM invoked services (batch 250 job 3)
Optional fsm/invoke adds state-scoped tasks with unique ids. Stable nonfinal states start tasks outermost first; transient states do not start work. Exit aborts before re-entry, including within one macrostep; common ancestors retain their tasks. done.invoke.id carries {output}; error.invoke.id carries {error}. Sync throws are errors. Old results are ignored by identity, never delivered into a newer state entry. invocations retains the latest record per id. settled resolves after delivery or cancellation and exposes handler failures as rejection. An abort cannot stop JavaScript that ignores its signal, but cancellation releases settled and suppresses its late result. Dispose or the optional external signal cancels all work and prevents new tasks/events. No actor spawning or message-receiving service protocol is claimed by this promise-task entry.


Batch 250 job 3: fsm/invoke 0 to 3609 B min+gzip, ceiling 3865 B. Optional runtime is not loaded by the FSM root or core/stage.

### Save OPFS (batch 255 job 3)

The optional save/opfs entry uses a private subdirectory, default margo-saves, and atomically replaces a file at FileSystemWritableFileStream.close. The API needs a secure origin and navigator.storage.getDirectory or an injected private directory; no fallback hides unsupported OPFS. Keys are well-formed nonempty Unicode, at most 175 UTF-8 bytes. Filenames encode keys so slashes cannot escape the namespace. Each value costs five framing bytes. Interrupted first writes leave empty placeholders hidden from reads/keys. Per-key operations serialize per adapter; separate adapters/tabs use the browser's last-close-wins behavior. This is single-key atomicity, not a transaction across keys or a claim of hardware power-loss durability. Abort is checked at filesystem boundaries before the irreversible close; cancellation during close cannot undo a committed write. Native permission, quota and locking failures propagate. README work is owed in docs/work-lists/readme-owed.md.

Save/opfs entry: 1,507 B min+gzip (before: absent, 0 B), ceiling 1,763 B. Core plus stage stays 23,950 B. Measured with scripts/measure-size.js bundleBytes and measureCoreStage; optional adapter code does not enter either root.

This is sampled visibility, not a swept camera volume: thin obstacles between samples and asymmetric frusta need application-specific collision queries. A blocker at the target leaves a 1e-6 nonzero arm. Collision may retract inside minDistance to protect visibility. Applications exclude their target object from colliders. ## Batch 171 derived flow fields

Optional @margoengine/sciviz/derive: absent -> 3993 B gzip, ceiling 4249 B (256 B headroom).
Keep validation, second-order boundaries, six owned output arrays, float64 CPU reference and GPU Jacobi
in one synchronous entry rather than split the mathematical contract. Root 50599, flow 8665, LIC 23461,
tubes 2533, core+stage 23924 B unchanged. No core/stage or physics source changes; no speed claim.

Cartesian regular grids only, x fastest, at most 1000000 points. Finite f32 velocities, NaN missing,
finite normal signed f32 inverse spacing I; equal bounds on singleton axes, derivative zero.
Conservative envelope D=8*max(maxAbsVelocity,2^-126)*maxAbsInverseSpacing <=1e18; rescale units
outside that domain. Second-order central/one-sided stencils, first-order secant for two samples.
Missing centres or required neighbours make all six point outputs NaN without bridging or downgrade.
Q is rotation dominance even for nonzero divergence, not the general second invariant. Lambda-2 is the
middle eigenvalue of S^2+Omega^2; a sign alone proves neither a material vortex nor a pressure minimum.

CPU/GPU absolute comparison: e=2^-23,t=2^-126,I=maxAbsInverseSpacing,L=32eD+32t*max(1,I).
Gradient <=L, divergence/curl <=4L, vorticity <=8L, Q <=256eD^2+128t,
lambda2 <=1024eD^2+128t. These include float rounding, FTZ and checked Jacobi residual, not spatial
truncation or measurement uncertainty. Sign within the bound is unresolved. GPU needs eight storage
bindings and 36 bytes per point within a storage buffer limit; 84 bytes/point output+temporary storage,

### Sprites slice entry (batch 245 job 1)
`@margoengine/sprites/slice` exports SliceLayer, SliceSprite and sliceParts.

### Signed safe saves (batch 255 job 4)

The optional save/signed entry exposes signedStorage(storage, key, options), returning the full SafeStorage read/write/delete/keys/check interface. It authenticates each complete safe frame including generation under its physical key using WebCrypto HMAC-SHA-256. Raw keys must have at least 32 bytes; CryptoKeys must be secret HMAC/SHA-256 keys of at least 256 bits with sign and verify usages. Raw key bytes are copied, imported lazily, nonextractable, and never written into the save. The caller owns generating, retaining and distributing a secret key; embedded client application keys cannot resist an attacker controlling that client. Authentication detects edits, format changes, role swaps and cross-key copies. It does not encrypt, prevent deletion, or reject replay of an older authenticated frame in the same physical key. Unsigned legacy saves fail closed, including a runtime legacy:true option. A damaged newest copy recovers from an older authenticated one and invokes onRecover; both bad reject with a coded error. Crypto awaits observe AbortSignal before storage writes. The format costs 37 bytes per copy beyond safeStorage's 24 bytes, or 122 bytes of framing across two stored payload copies. The default provider is globalThis.crypto.subtle; options.subtle supports an explicit provider. Existing safe verify/onRecover options apply. README work is owed in docs/work-lists/readme-owed.md.

Save/signed entry: 2,581 B min+gzip (before: absent, 0 B), ceiling 2,837 B, including the safeStorage implementation it composes. Core plus stage stays 23,950 B. Keeping authentication and recovery together avoids a caller accidentally authenticating only payload bytes while trusting an edited generation or copy role.
### Batch 197 BoxGizmo

Optional controls/box-gizmo exports BoxGizmo, eight corner scale handles and twelve edge midpoint rotation handles. One live engine mesh with nonempty Geometry is attached at a time; recompute bounds with refreshBounds after vertex edits. Defaults: 12 CSS-pixel handles, uniform scaling, opposite-corner pivot, no scale or rotation snapping. scaleFromCenter selects the centre pivot; uniformScaling=false projects each local scale axis onto the screen. Hidden axes preserve their scale. Positive scale factors clamp to 0.0001, preserving a mirrored mesh's sign. Edge rotation uses local axes around the bounds centre. Parent transforms, including nonuniform scaling, preserve the chosen local pivot; rotating a child under a nonuniform parent follows that parent's affine frame. UI is an overlay, including occluded handles, and nearest-depth handles win screen overlaps. Escape, pointercancel and disconnect restore the original pose; pointerup commits. Mesh or engine disposal removes references, listeners, passes and GPU buffers.

## Fuzzy decisions (batch 251)

New behavior/fuzzy measures 2,621 B min+gzip (previously absent), generated umbrella
alias 61 B external; no existing ceiling raised. Inputs are finite world/domain
values, and memberships outside a shape's finite domain are zero. Default output

### SCXML document subset (batch 250 job 5)
Optional fsm/scxml converts definitions to/from MachineDocument. Input supports the W3C SCXML namespace and version 1.0, state hierarchy, explicit/implicit initial states, parallel state regions, one history pseudo-state per state, single-target event transitions, symbolic guards, and named entry/exit hooks. History fallback must match ordinary initial because the native document has one initial field. Cross-region targets, wildcard/list events, executable transition content, arbitrary script/guard expressions, DTDs/entities, final/invoke/eventless constructs and unknown elements/attributes reject. Final/invoke definitions belong to separate optional runtimes, not MachineDocument. Session name/datamodel metadata is accepted but is not saved.
Native extensions in urn:margoengine:fsm:1 are enabled by default on export and retain delay, cross-fade duration, update hook, region history, transition ordering, arbitrary binding/state names and explicit native region boundaries. A parallel holder with separate hierarchical children is outside this subset. extensions:false produces the common standard hierarchy/event/named-hook subset and rejects native-only fields. This is document conversion, not a conforming SCXML processor: Margo retains exact event names, remembered-parent targeting and common-ancestor transition semantics. The importer never evaluates an expression or invokes a hook. Browser DOMParser is the default; Node must supply options.parser, with no new parser runtime dependency.
Input/output limit: 1 MiB UTF-8; 10,000 XML elements; 128 XML nesting levels; export preflight limits native region nesting to 64 and rejects cycles. Plain XML ids use the ASCII identifier subset; arbitrary native names use generated ids plus namespaced names. XML 1.0 forbidden characters reject. Shared region definition objects are valid; cycles are not.

Batch 250 job 5: fsm/scxml 0 to 4970 B min+gzip, ceiling 5226 B. Optional runtime is not loaded by the FSM root or core/stage.

## Trigger regions (batch 251)

New behavior/triggers: 1,606 B min+gzip (previously absent), umbrella alias 64 B

### Batch 171 atmosphere on the globe

The new optional sciviz/atmosphere entry composes geo's WGS84 globe with sky/planet's existing Hillaire RGB medium. Importing sciviz root, geo, grids or flow without atmosphere adds no sky dependency to the runtime graph. A GPUDevice is required: WebGPU and webgl2-compat, not the separate native WebGL2 sciviz driver. Perspective cameras only; the observer must remain outside the ellipsoid. Figure model inversion handles arbitrary nonsingular data-to-scene affine transforms.

Data positions use longitude/latitude degrees and geodetic metres above WGS84. Scalar triangle values/masks are retained; points are tangent-disc glyphs with a physical radius (default 10000 m, maximum 1000000 m). Geographic wind uses east/north/up m/s and seconds, converted once at input samples by WGS84 curvature to degree/degree/metre rates. The existing GPU RK4, temporal/spatial interpolation, seeding, trails, respawn and replay remain unchanged. Grid latitudes exclude the exact poles; longitude width is at most 360 degrees, with boundary respawn instead of implicit periodic interpolation. No per-frame CPU particle readback. Linear interpolation of the converted angular field is an approximation to interpolation of local physical vectors.

The medium stretches the polar coordinate by 1/(1-f), mapping the exact WGS84 ground to the sphere used by Hillaire. Transport distances and geodetic normal heights change by at most 0.3365 percent, and phase/solar angles are correspondingly approximated. Geometry is not stretched. Tile chord fragments use the reference ground radius for lighting/transport, avoiding underground integration. This is not exact ellipsoidal, spectral or weather radiative transfer. Data-fragment transport uses 24 steps; background uses 32; existing transmittance/multiple-scattering tables retain their resolutions and method. Radii are at most 100000 km and vertical scattering depth at most 6; exposure -20..20, top-of-atmosphere illuminance 0..1000000 (default 20).

Optional clouds accept geographic shell triangles and scalar density clamped to [0,1], including NaN as empty. They are solar-lit data shells with aerial transport; no inferred cloud thickness, volumetric self-shadow or shadow map. Transparent layers retain the renderer's layer sorting. Globe owns its returned layers until disposed; individually removed layers may retain their CPU records until that owner is disposed. The data coordinates remain inspectable through the supplied arrays and existing layer APIs.

The official NOAA demo uses the hash-pinned public-domain wind.bin. Sigma 0.995 is not a height. Wind at 20000 m, speed colours at 1000 m and reference glyphs at 100000 m are explicitly labelled display placements, not measured atmospheric altitudes. See examples/assets/sciviz/atmosphere.json. No speed assertion, benchmark or core/stage source change.

## Batch 258 image scope

ImageTexture copies straight-alpha RGBA8 sRGB pixels, decodes browser images with AbortSignal, and snapshots canvas/image/video sources. Images default to contain, centered in the content box; cover crops and fill stretches. Source is an integer pixel atlas cell. Nine-slice borders are source pixels times borderScale (default 1); they override fit and shrink uniformly if the target cannot fit both borders. Tint defaults to opaque white. No GPU objects are exposed or borrowed from core.

Cells are cached as 60-pixel tiles with a one-texel neighbor gutter per side. Filter footprints clamp at cell boundaries, and alpha is premultiplied before filtering. Source pixel buffers and cached tiles are CPU memory retained with ImageTexture. Dropping it releases unreferenced source storage; tiles already admitted to a renderer atlas remain until atlas eviction or renderer disposal. Edits use a new ImageTexture. Raw preview GL retains its existing encoded-space compositing; complete compatibility follows the WebGPU path. No speed claim or GPU render-target input is made.

### Batch 254 global voice budget
Optional @margoengine/audio/voices: 2117 B minified gzip, new entry from 0 B. AudioVoiceManager has maxVoices=32 (integer >=0) and linear threshold=0.0001. add(sound,{priority=0,gain=()=>1}) returns a managed transport. All registered decoded-buffer sounds on one listener share the cap, including global, stereo and positional sounds. Larger finite priority wins, then volume/fade/master/distance/cone/custom gain; ties retain registration order. Each frame updates managed poses before ranking. Losers release buffer sources before winners allocate, so the cap is never transiently exceeded. Virtual voices allocate no buffer source; logical phase advances on context.currentTime, wraps configured loops and integrates playbackRate*2^(detune/1200). Handle play/pause/stop/seek, playbackRate and detune own transport; pitch changes restart a physical source at the exact phase. Do not call raw sound/pool transport, replace buffers, automate source pitch, or attach Doppler/timeline transport while managed. Raw volume, pose, filters and fades remain available. Media/stream/node sources cannot be phase-virtualized by this buffer-only manager. gain is a caller-supplied estimate for effects/occlusion/bus gain; no perceptual masking analysis. Selection occurs on updates, not within an audio render quantum. Handles/manager stop sources on dispose and preserve caller-owned sounds/buffers; listener teardown owns the sounds. Core/stage unchanged.

`@margoengine/stats/gl` provides GLStats. Custom loops call beginFrame(gl), beginPass/endPass or pass(name, work), endFrame, then poll from a later task. ### Stats panels entry

`@margoengine/stats/panels` provides StatsPanels, attach/sample/refresh/toJSON/dispose, with four chronological fixed Float64Array histories and a named GPU list. Defaults: samples 120 (2..4096), refreshMilliseconds 150 (16..60000), parent document.body; owned panel width 360 CSS pixels within the viewport. Options.stats borrows an already attached Stats without transferring its ownership. CPU milliseconds come from FramePhases work in the frame task, FPS from the rolling Stats interval, GPU from the latest completed asynchronous sample. GPU history therefore holds the latest valid result between readbacks, rather than pretending each frame has a fresh query. WebGPU samples one encoder in 15, at most 128 passes, preserves existing timestampWrites and needs timestamp-query enabled on the device. Pass descriptors supply names, with deterministic render N/compute N fallback names. WebGL2 uses the gl entry's limits and early-registration naming rules. Memory defaults to tracked WebGPU descriptor bytes created after attachment; without WebGPU, performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize is used only where exposed. Those sources are labelled separately, omit driver padding and are not interchangeable. A custom memory callback can supply another byte measurement, or null. Unsupported readings appear as gaps and unavailable text, never zero. Custom loops may supply PanelSample values directly. Sampling does not write DOM; refresh draws and labels the graphs. Disposal removes owned collectors and DOM, and restores a borrowed Stats graph. New entry: 9,895 B gzip, ceiling 10,192 B. Its bytes provide coherent collector ownership and all four graphs on both backends; splitting would require users to assemble and manage the collectors themselves. Root and core/stage are unchanged.

Batch 257 job 4, browser matrix evidence, not native Safari certification: Firefox 157.0 on Windows/headless has transferControlToOffscreen, worker OffscreenCanvas, RAF and WebGL2; worker WebGPU adapter is unavailable with the default test profile. The unchanged shared WebGL2 scene selected worker mode, transferred its buffer, displayed centre RGBA [213,26,1,255] and disposed successfully. Windows Playwright WebKit 27.2 exposes neither canvas transfer, worker OffscreenCanvas/RAF nor worker graphics contexts. It selected the original page canvas, retained the input buffer and displayed the same centre pixel, then disposed. Its Safari-shaped user agent and Apple GPU renderer string do not establish an Apple host or native Safari support. Both page hardware probes report no WebGPU adapter. The strict full suite therefore fails on the absent WebGPU/worker capabilities; those assertions were not loosened. Apple no longer updates Safari for Windows, and Playwright WebKit is a separate build. Native Safari/macOS hardware proof remains owed in private/handoffs/finish-later.md; job 4 is DONE under Scott's 95% rule.

### Batch 245 per-sprite blend modes

The optional `@margoengine/sprites/blend` entry exports BlendLayer, BlendSprite, blendBatches and their types. Modes are normal (default), add, multiply and screen; addBlend creates sprites and blendMode is mutable. Ordinary add sprites use normal. Contiguous visible runs share a draw, with original z/y/insertion order retained. Multiply uses two interleaved draws per sprite to keep uncovered source colour on transparent backdrops. Atlas pages, nearest/linear filtering, mipmaps, camera, masks, view layers, targets, normal output and lifecycle are inherited; custom fragment shaders are excluded from BlendLayerOptions because the entry owns premultiplication and correction.

Blending uses premultiplied colour in the target's blend space. Add sums colour and alpha, clamped by normalized targets; the other modes use source-over alpha. Smooth sRGB targets blend decoded linear colour; nearest keeps the base layer's numeric texels. Render targets contain premultiplied colour. Intermediate RGBA8 multiply rounding is at most one byte in the asserted single-sprite fixtures. No universal accumulation error bound or speed claim is made. The readback fixtures cover 146 cases on each backend, including sRGB/unorm targets, both filters, transparent/partial/opaque backgrounds, three atlas alpha values, mixed runs, nonzero instance starts and overlapping multiply sprites.

Batch 225 job 2: splines/query provides splineBounds, splineExtrema, intersectSplines, intersectSplineRay and intersectSplinePlane. Bounds and extrema solve each cubic analytically; joins are candidates on all axes and constant coordinates have no isolated stationary roots. Plane equation normal dot point + constant = 0; rays use origin + direction * otherT, so otherT is not world distance unless direction is unit length. Results separate isolated points and continuous overlaps. Defaults: tolerance=1e-7 world units, parameterTolerance=1e-7, maxWork=200000 curve-pair nodes. Increasing maxWork or splitting the curves resolves the explicit limit error; no incomplete result is returned. Parameters within parameterTolerance are merged, so reduce it for closely spaced hits. Interval boxes include a machine-roundoff margin, then hits verify spatial residuals; this is floating-point geometry, not symbolic certification. Closed t=0 and t=1 remain distinct parameter endpoints. No GPU state or GPU tests; core/stage unchanged.

Unsubscribed listeners receive nothing further. stop detaches and clears without exit callbacks. Field writes do not change membership.

## WFC 3D overlapping (batch 237)
Optional wfc/overlapping3d learns N x N x N patterns from finite-number voxel labels, X fastest, with N 2..5 (default 2). Input wraps by default; identity symmetry is default, with optional four Y turns or 24 cube rotations and reflections (2, 8 or 48 orientations). Sample limit 1,048,576 voxels, pattern limit 4096; nonperiodic source dimensions must still be at least N. Output defaults to nonperiodic, seed 1, four attempts and 10000 backtracks per attempt; dimensions must be at least N unless periodic. Output limit 1,000,000 voxels and 16,777,216 lattice cell/pattern pairs. Voxel pins constrain every covering pattern, including seams and outer corners. Samples and rules are copied. Chronological backtracking never undoes pins; exhausted budgets throw coded failed with help link, and cancellation preserves the exact reason. CPU-only synchronous solving cannot receive event-loop aborts while running; no worker or Wasm backend is claimed for this new model. Arc propagation is generic within the optional entry; neither core nor stage imports it. Hashing overlap slabs avoids pairwise voxel comparisons; no timing gain is claimed. Memory remains proportional to domains, pattern adjacency, and pinned domains.

Batch 225 job 3: splines/offset exports offsetSplineAt (exact offset point), offsetSpline (cubic approximation plus ranges/maxError/work), reverseSpline (exact geometry and t -> 1-t). Positive distance follows normal cross source tangent; normal defaults to [0,0,1] and can define a lateral offset of a spatial curve whenever transverse to the tangent. Defaults: tolerance=0.001 world units, maxDepth=20 (0..30), maxSegments=16384 (1..333333), maxWork=1000000 interval nodes, divisions=max(256,8*outputPieces) capped at 1000000. The local approximation has a conservative floating-point interval enclosure plus roundoff allowance; formal exact-arithmetic certification is not claimed. maxError excludes bevel joins, whose ranges have equal endpoints. Output t distributes equally over output pieces, so ranges maps it to source t. Closed paths get a closing bevel if needed. Stationary/parallel-normal source points have undefined nonzero offset and reject with singular; zero offset remains valid. Exhausted depth, work or piece budgets reject with limit and no partial result. Raw offsets retain loops/cusps and do not perform outline trimming or Boolean cleanup. Controls are independent copies, closure is preserved by reverse, arc lengths stay sampled. No GPU implementation, GPU tests or core/stage changes.

### BVH parallel construction (batch 221)

Optional bvh/parallel adds buildParallel(source, options). workers defaults to min(8, hardwareConcurrency - 1), at least 1, accepts integers 1..64 and counts leaf workers plus one coordinator. The shallow frontier targets four tasks per requested worker; actual workers are capped by unfinished subtrees. The existing maxDepth, maxLeafTriangles, bins and strategy apply globally. Every numeric build, planning and packing pass runs off the main thread when Worker exists; source normalization/cloning and final result validation still have linear caller-thread costs. No Worker means the existing synchronous builder on the next microtask, with pre-build cancellation only. Worker builds have a finite positive timeoutMs (default 120000, maximum 2147483647). Abort/deadline/error terminates the coordinator and its nested worker pool. No transfer option: caller buffers stay attached and unchanged, including source face order. Source positions must remain stable until completion; later edits plus refit are supported. SharedArrayBuffer permits one shared immutable position snapshot across leaf workers; otherwise each leaf worker retains one cloned position buffer. This fallback uses additional memory proportional to worker count. Subtree indices/results are transferred. Parallel and serial packed topology/index/face arrays are byte-identical in the retained correctness cases. No speed ratio claimed.

## Procedural skeleton trees (batch 230)
`@margoengine/procedural/tree-mesh` adds meshTree, generateParametricTree and meshTreeLODs. TreeSkeleton from /trees is accepted directly. Parent-first XYZ nodes become capped, smooth tapered tubes with duplicated UV seams, arc-length V and tangents. Optional radii and architectural orders override the derived support-length radii. Leaf cards are single, crossed double, or three-plane clusters, with UVs and an owned alpha atlas. Material descriptors carry tint, alpha cutoff, two-sided foliage and bark texture settings. Limits: 16384 nodes, 1 million vertices per output part, 65536 planned leaves, 0..4 recursive orders, 1..64 axial sections, 3..32 radial segments, at most 8 strictly increasing LOD thresholds starting at zero. Degenerate edges, cycles, malformed radii and invalid controls reject with a coded error. Synchronous work checks AbortSignal before execution; use a worker for in-flight cancellation. Root-only skeletons produce empty meshes. Fork surfaces overlap within parent tubes, rather than forming a Boolean-unioned manifold. Procedural 64x64 RGBA bark/leaf atlases are authored patterns, not photographic species reconstructions. OFF keeps colormap indices as `properties.colorIndex`; mapping them requires the caller's external palette. Binary OFF uses big-endian int32 counts/indices and float32 attributes, four vertex color components and 0/1/3/4 face color components. Existing non-3D OFF variants remain unsupported. Face lists are capped at 65,536 corners; vertex and triangle limits retain their existing defaults.
`/ply`: 3,702 to 3,973 B min+gzip; `/off`: 2,201 to 2,736 B. These now-public optional entries include owned face metadata and binary OFF validation. Their separate budgets include standard headroom; sharing the existing reader avoids duplicate parsers. Loader root: 52,087 to 52,868 B; core plus stage: 24,209 B unchanged.

## Batch 265 adaptive performance

The optional @margoengine/react/performance entry exports PerformanceMonitor, AdaptiveDpr, usePerformanceMonitor and PerformanceController. Defaults: 250 ms windows, 10 windows per decision, 0.75 required fraction, factor 1, step 0.1, unlimited direction reversals, fallbackFactor 0. Bounds default to [50,57] FPS, or [50,90] when a measured window exceeds 90 Hz. A 60 Hz presentation can therefore recover quality. FPS is frames divided by summed measured milliseconds; observed refresh is a high window average, not a display capability query. It is cadence, not GPU execution time. A sample prop accepts measured milliseconds or null from an application's collector; default intervals use the monotonic performance clock without the engine's delta cap. Hidden tabs and unsampled demand frames discard incomplete windows. Active slow frames remain measurements. Snapshots retain at most 4096 frame intervals per window while all intervals count toward the average. A direction reversal beyond flipflops fixes the factor at fallbackFactor until reset.

AdaptiveDpr defaults to min 0.5, max 1, pixelated false. Fractions apply to the Canvas's native resolution, not CSS layout. A package-owned target scales scene raster dimensions; native MSAA stays intact. Reduced frames add one full-canvas presentation triangle. Scale 1 returns to the original renderer, allowing exact restored pixels. Multiple holds use the lowest scale and nearest presentation if any requests it. Named Scenes and Canvas views retain their scene, camera, layers, clear and scissor. Explicit offscreen targets and tracked XR eye targets retain their owner's resolution. Picking uses original Canvas view coordinates. Removing the last hold destroys its texture immediately and retains only logical picking until the next Canvas draw; engine disposal always releases the adapter. Resources recreate after device restore. WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer are supported; native preview reports unsupported. No timing or throughput gain is claimed during the build phase.

Adaptive performance size: optional entry 0 -> 5619 B minified gzip, ceiling 5769 B. Keeping measurement, presentation and picking in one optional entry avoids duplicate lifetime and asynchronous render boundaries. Core + stage stays 24209 B on the current main baseline.

Adaptive diagnostics use stable MargoError codes and help links. The final React root is 10259 B gzip, React XR 4159 B; the performance entry above includes coded presentation-owner diagnostics.
Batch 219 job 1: optional geometry/nurbs-edit supports immutable rational curve/surface knot insertion and degree elevation on either surface axis; knot parameters and interior multiplicity/continuity are preserved. Unclamped inputs are restricted to the same active domain with clamped endpoints for elevation. Default insertion/elevation count is 1; zero copies, invalid counts and excess multiplicity reject. Trimming accepts retained UV polygons or closed 2D rational curves, holes and multiple islands; regions outside [0,1] are clipped. Default slices/stacks=32, trimTolerance=0.0001 UV units. Surface tessellation has explicit resolution, no model-space error guarantee. Trim curve sampling inherits the existing 12-level subdivision limit. Polygon intersection snaps to its 2^26 grid and features below two steps may disappear; cell pieces retain separate vertices and normals from their own side of knot creases. Degree elevation uses floating-point homogeneous arithmetic, not symbolic arithmetic. Surface file parsing remains in loaders. New entry absent -> 11646 B gzip, ceiling 11996 B; refinement and trim operations share surface evaluation, clipping and triangulation, so splitting would fragment the editing workflow. Core + stage unchanged at 24209 B gzip.

Batch 219: NurbsSurface.derivatives(u,v,leftU=false,leftV=false) exposes the exact side of a repeated knot on either axis. ## Mesh repair (batch 224 job 3)
The optional mesh-edit/repair entry exports repairMesh(input, options). Input is a polygon soup with unique nonempty face IDs, xyz vertices and index loops; corner UVs are optional. Defaults: distance 0 (exact duplicates), fillHoles true, maxHoleEdges 256. Up to 200000 input vertices and faces and 4096 corners per input face; output remains within standard PolygonMesh limits. Near welding is non-chaining and keeps the earliest eligible position. Nonfinite positions and invalid-index faces are discarded and named; structural array/ID errors reject. Missing or invalid UV corners reset to [0,0] with diagnostics. Concave/warped polygons split through existing mesh editing rules; unresolved, pinched and degenerate polygons are discarded.
When more than two faces compete for an edge, descending face area then input order select the retained manifold subset. A contradictory orientation constraint removes the encountered conflicting face and reports it. Disconnected vertex fans split identities. Existing hole filling uses triangles, refine false and fair false, so it adds a closure without moving surviving scan vertices; holes above maxHoleEdges stay open and are reported. Nested closed shells orient by solid-angle containment (cavities inward). Self-intersections and intersecting-shell intent are not reconstructed or certified. readyForBoolean checks closed opposing edge incidences and positive volume, followed by the actual solid validator; it is false for empty, open or zero-volume output. It does not promise valid geometric self-intersection behavior for arbitrary damaged scans. Result fields include every removed face/vertex, flipped/filled face, weld/fan counts and source face/vertex maps. Source and output arrays are independent. Cooperative AbortSignal checks bound work between traversal steps; no interactive latency claim.
Repair entry size: 0 to 9631 gzip bytes, with a 9920-byte ceiling. The optional entry includes the established hole filler and topology validation so repair stays complete; splitting them would add API complexity without reducing bytes when closure is needed. Core plus stage remains 24209 bytes.

### Optional CPU occlusion on the full WebGL2 layer

`@margoengine/culling/webgl2` supplies `WebGL2Culling` for opaque core meshes on

### FBX optional texture formats (batch 205)

`@margoengine/fbx/textures` exports `textures`, passed in `FBXOptions.extensions`. It routes embedded
and external TGA, DDS, TIFF/TIF and BMP through decoder entries, lazily, then encodes PNG. Default
FBX byte and pixel budgets still apply. DDS material images must be 2D; only the base mip is embedded
in GLB, whose runtime generates its mips. Float TIFF/DDS values clamp to 0..1 and encode to sRGB PNG. The decoder entries define
format support; damaged recognized inputs reject instead of silently dropping a texture. Unknown
formats and missing files retain the existing missing-texture record. Multiple image hooks are tried
in extension order, and the first successful conversion wins.

`@margoengine/decoders/bmp` exports `parseBMP`, `BMPOptions`, `DecodedBMP`. Default maxPixels is
67,108,864. OS/2 core and Windows 40/52/56/108/124-byte DIB headers, indexed 1/4/8-bit, RGB 16/24/32-bit,
RGB/alpha bitfields, RLE4/RLE8 and top-down uncompressed rows are supported. BI_RGB 32-bit spare bytes
are opaque. JPEG/PNG-in-BMP, OS/2 v2 compression and embedded colour-profile transforms are not supported.

### Batch 243 optional learned denoiser
`voxel-pathtracer/denoise-ml` exposes DenoiseML.create(engine, {signal}), denoise(image, {signal}), whenIdle, dispose and Symbol.dispose. It requires an engine WebGPU compute device (the existing WebGL2 compatibility device is supported), finite RGB Float32 color/albedo/normal guides from renderImage with aovs:true, positive integer dimensions totaling at most 16,777,216 pixels, positive samples and optional coverage in [0,1]. Color is nonnegative through the Float32 representation of 1e16, albedo [0,1], normal components [-1,1]. Device binding/buffer/grid limits apply in addition. Device changes rebuild weights and the pipeline; each request snapshots every input AOV, owns its output and preserves alpha, albedo, normal, depth, instance and palette arrays. Cancellation rejects queued/active waits promptly and disposal releases owned buffers. GPU failures use coded failed errors with their platform cause.
The 321-parameter, two-hidden-layer network predicts a single 3x3 positive reconstruction kernel; it is spatial, with no temporal history, downloaded weights or external inference runtime. Input guides are required. HDR normalization and softmax preserve finite constant fields and bound reconstructed RGB by observed neighbor radiance. Synthetic training and the licensed Box holdout are narrow correctness/quality evidence, not a claim of universal image-quality superiority.
The new entry measures 6,767 B min+gzip (ceiling 7,023 B), previously absent. Root/core/stage gain no code. Core plus stage is 24,209 B on this main base, unchanged by the entry and below 25,000 B. The difference from earlier 23,950 B batch records is the upstream version guard. No speed or wall-clock claim is made.

### Geospatial vector formats (batch 202)
The optional `@margoengine/loaders/geo` provides parseGeoJSON, parseShapefile, parseGPX, parseKML and parseMVT. ## Mesh convex hull and Minkowski sum (batch 224 job 4)
geometry/hull exports convexHullTriangles(points, {signal}) with outward indices into the original flat/nested xyz positions. Empty or lower-dimensional sets return empty indices. The existing Quickhull predicates use a translated unit frame and a 1e-10 coordinate-scale tolerance; this is a floating hull, not an exact predicate claim. Worst-case BSP decomposition and pair enumeration can be large, so no interactive or speed claim is made. Core/stage remain unchanged.

## Batch 207 job 3: meshopt .margo geometry
New blender/meshopt is 8304 gzip bytes (before 0, ceiling 8560), including optional variant validation paths. Blender root changes 4340 to 4397 B for a named meshopt-file refusal; KTX2 is 5270 B after sharing the existing container writer; its pre-job entry size was not measured separately. compressMargoMeshopt losslessly encodes packed 24/80-byte vertices and 16/32-bit indices with existing meshopt version-0 attribute streams. Indices are encoded as raw four-byte groups (zero padding is discarded), preserving every index and provoking vertex rather than rotating triangles. Small/uncompressible sections remain native; the entire original file is returned if it is smaller. expandMargoMeshopt supports static, animated, shapes and KTX2 containers without changing metadata/image/animation bytes; decodeMargoMeshopt is the static prepared reader. parse/load default to parseMargo; use options.parse for compatible PBRModel parsers such as parseAnimatedMargo, parseMargoKTX2 or parseMargoLightmap. Shapes can use the expanded bytes with the curves loader. AbortSignal is checked between sections, before allocation and before load; a single existing synchronous codec call cannot be interrupted.
Expanded file and aggregate section allocation are bounded at 256 MiB before decode; vertex count per section at 1 million, original table/manifest limits retained. PNG/KTX2/animation sections stay uncompressed. No lossy quantization, triangle reordering or geometry simplification. Seven own fixtures keep every section byte and manifest value; anim 28924 to 19516 B, objects 13940 to 12348 B, lightmap 1396 to 1276 B, curves 18180 to 17988 B. Native/compat frames are identical for original and compressed static/animated models, with zero validation errors. These are deterministic byte counts, not timing benchmarks.

### Native 3MF lattice and slice data (batch 202)

### Optional front-to-back instance ordering

`@margoengine/culling/sort` exports FrontToBack for kept core batches (including
DynamicInstances) and registered model instances, SortedInstances for the static
CulledInstances draw path, and InstanceSorter for 96-byte GPU lists. Sorting is
optional; enabled and sortEnabled default true on the respective optional
classes and can change at runtime. Core and model sorting executes after culling
and before drawing, independent of registration order. Model tint/transmission
lists and alphaMode BLEND primitives retain their existing order. Plain model
primitives keep their original draws; deformed models retain their bypass.
Each range orders by its transformed local center along the current view
forward direction, with original row indices breaking equal-depth ties. It
supports perspective and orthographic views, reflection and node transforms.
Ordering is per batch, as with specialised batched renderers, rather than across
materials or geometries. Counts, picking/caster buffers and every record field
stay unchanged. Opaque surfaces that overlap at equal surface depth but have
different center depths can resolve in the new order, the usual draw-order
consequence of sorting. Transparent geometry must never be passed to the raw
sorter. Importing ordinary cullers does not load ordering code.
InstanceSorter accepts capacity 0 through 4,194,304 within device storage limits;
its key network rounds to a power of two. O(n log-squared n) key comparisons and
one gather are encoded; no per-instance CPU work or GPU readback occurs. Each
view and stage owns distinct parameter storage. Input instance buffers require
STORAGE; supplied argument buffers require STORAGE and COPY_SRC. Software
occlusion arguments now expose those flags too. No speed claim is made.

Removed sort owners release all their view resources with InstanceSorter.forget;
FrontToBack also collects owners absent from the preceding frame and releases
registered model resources on removal. Cleanup happens before a later frame,
after the prior frame's command submission; existing view uploads stay distinct.

Batch 223 job 3 minified gzip: /sort is new, 0 to 14060 B. /webgl2 stays 3028 B while exposing storage/copy access to its argument buffer. /bounds stays 19447 B. The sort entry shares one network implementation across drawing routes and reuses the existing static culler; a split would duplicate resource state and complicate import/use. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. firstInstance prefixes are included in capacity; their indirect word and draw offset are preserved, along with every other indirect word.

## Mesh-surface scatter (batch 231 job 2)

scatterSurface(geometryData, count, options) from @margoengine/scatter/surface returns owned transforms, positions, normals, uvs and colors arrays. Defaults: seed 1; scale [1,1]; yaw [0,2*pi] radians; align 1; offset 0; source matrix identity; no weights or painted colours; no cancellation signal. Count is 0..1000000. Source triangles must have positive weighted area even with count 0. Vertex weights are nonnegative and interpolated linearly within each triangle. Areas are measured in world space after options.matrix, including nonuniform scale; normals use its inverse transpose. Arrays and source geometry are not mutated. Sources and outputs must fit finite f32 values; placements are nonsingular affine world matrices with uniform scale. Use an identity TexturedScatter model root for world placements, or convert into that root's space.

Output costs 112 bytes per placement (16 matrix, 3 position, 3 normal, 2 UV and 4 colour floats), plus the sampler's triangle CDF and transformed source copies when a matrix is supplied. Alignment is the shortest rotation from world +Y, then optional local yaw; the antipodal -Y case chooses +X as its turn axis. Offset is along the sampled normal. No mesh-to-heightmap projection: cliffs, roofs and undersides are sampled directly. Resample when source geometry or weights change. Entry gzip 0 to 1259 bytes, ceiling 1515 bytes; core plus stage remains 24209 bytes.
Batch 172 /glyph: optional instanced glyphs and scalar/vector warp, with at most 1000000 input points (images follow imageGrid's existing 2D/3D limits). Stride/mask apply to original row IDs; zero instance scale is omitted. Cell centres are vertex means. Finite f32 render transforms/bounds; grid warp coordinates are f64 and surface output is f32. Line sources are thin tubes; custom meshes use +X and retain their own origin. Bounds are conservative spheres; explicit triangle normals rebuild after warp, while arbitrary field arrays remain borrowed. No tensor transport, element-inversion guarantee or timing claim. Core/stage unchanged at 24209 B gzip.

Batch 172 /glyph entry: new 0 to 4388 B min+gzip, ceiling 4644 B; optional placement, shapes, warp and ownership stay together to avoid API fragmentation. Core/stage unchanged at 24209 B.

Batch 205 job 4: `@margoengine/fbx/surfaces` exports `surfaces`, an optional extension on page and worker conversion. It tessellates Nurb/NurbsSurface and Patch geometry, including older inline Model geometry after legacyFBX normalization, independently of extension ordering. NURBS orders 2..32, positive rational weights, open/closed/periodic nets and every nonempty knot span use loaders/nurbs. FBX Step controls subdivisions per span; absent Step defaults to four times degree. Bezier cubic, BezierQuadric quadratic, Cardinal cubic, uniform cubic BSpline and Linear patch bases may differ on U and V. Open Bezier nets require 1 modulo degree control points; closed nets add their seam point; Cardinal open spans interpolate the interior controls and closed spans wrap. Closure wraps the necessary weighted rows/columns. Parametric UVs, analytic/pole normals, FlipNormals, material links, model transforms and animation remain in the ordinary FBX path. UCapped/VCapped generate flat-normal cap polygons, with the existing 4,096-corner polygon limit. All generated work and buffers charge the import budgets before allocation; vertex/corner limits include caps.
The output is the whole parametric surface, not trimmed topology. Control-point skin/morph deformation cannot in general be represented exactly by one glTF vertex bind position; it fails with coded unsupported/help and a polygon-bake remedy, rather than misapplying original control-point indices to generated vertices. Ordinary polygon skin/morph import is unchanged. Separate Maya ASCII/binary exports contain different near-zero control coordinates; exact front-end parity is proven by encoding the same real control net both ways, without rounding the product output.

### Weighted bone masks (batch 211 job 4)

animator/masks provides createBoneMask(nodeCount, entries?, defaultWeight=0) and addWeightedLayer(owner, {clip or graph, mask, weight?, blend?}). The builder returns a mutable Float32Array in glTF node order; entries are unique [node,weight] pairs. Weights and defaultWeight must be finite 0..1. An attached mask has exactly one value per model node and is read and validated every frame. Each value affects its own node; ancestry is not expanded automatically. Effective influence is layer strength times bone weight; zero retains the lower pose and one applies full influence. Defaults are layer weight 1 and override mode. Additive uses the owner's loaded local pose and identity scale delta on a zero reference axis. Morph weights use the corresponding node influence. Vertex skin weights remain asset data. The returned StateLayer exposes its independent graph controls and shares the layers entry's class identity. Disposal removes the complete layer; owner pause/speed and lifetime apply as for graph layers.
Entry sizes: masks 0 -> 11,033 B gzip, ceiling 11,364 B; shared layers 10,730 -> 10,828 B within its 11,052 B ceiling. The masks entry includes the complete existing state-layer controller, preserving graph and clip behaviour without a second sampler. Importing only the mask builder tree-shakes the controller. No core/stage changes, benchmark or speed assertion.
### Painted 2D geometry (batch 247 job 1)
`@margoengine/lighting2d/sdf` exports `SDFScene2D`, consumed as borrowed `GILighting2DOptions.painted`. Source alpha at least alphaThreshold (default .5, always positive) defines opaque axis-aligned pixel cells; RGB is linear straight albedo. Separate emission defaults to source, uses RGB times alpha times emissionIntensity (default 1, nonnegative), and only occupied cells emit. Black art blocks without emitting. Camera defaults {x:0,y:0,zoom:1}, top-left origin, pixels per world unit, independent of the receiver camera. Changes are sampled every GI frame before cascades. Inputs are single-sample 2D single-layer RGBA/BGRA unorm/sRGB or RGBA16/32 float TEXTURE_BINDING textures of matching dimensions; textures and the SDFScene2D are borrowed by GI. Source and output must be distinct textures. sRGB textures decode on load. HDR needs a floating emission image and output.
The exact sampled-centre signed distance field stores R distance in pixels, G occupancy in rgba32float (16 B/pixel). All-empty/full opposite-class distances use finite magnitude 1e10. Three GPU passes plus scratch cost 48 B/source pixel plus 32 B uniforms (row 8, hull 16, squared 8, field 16); scratch buffers must fit device maxStorageBufferBindingSize/maxBufferSize and dispatches must fit maxComputeWorkgroupsPerDimension. The transform is exact at pixel centres, not a continuous vector outline; opacity is thresholded, not transmissive. Nearest opaque cell emission terminates each ray, including inside a source. No frame-rate or general transport-error claim. Painted surface reflection and temporal reuse are batch 247 job 2.

Batch 247 job 1 entry sizes (min+gzip, other packages external): new SDF 0 to 2,667 B, ceiling 2,923 B; GI 8,834 to 9,670 B, ceiling 9,100 to 9,961 B. The GI increase buys painted visibility for the same interval connectors, source bindings and lifecycle; separating that shader contract into another adapter would fragment nearest-hit handling and complicate the API. Optional ceilings raised under Scott's 2026-11-10 ruling. Measured core plus stage remains 24,209 B, below 25,000 B; neither source was edited.

### Splat interchange formats (batch 238)
splats/formats reads KSplat 0.1 compression 0/1/2, multiple sections and capacities, full and partial spatial buckets and SH degrees 0 to 2 (the supported writer's maximum). It promotes mixed section degrees with neutral missing higher bands. Count is capped at 3,000,000, PLY header at 64 KiB; malformed schemas, lengths and bucket ranges reject before reading attributes. These are synchronous CPU readers; no worker or reduced peak-memory claim. Exact opacity 0/1 writes limiting IEEE infinity logits. GPU rendering uses the existing Splats pipeline unchanged.

### Painted GI and temporal intervals (batch 247 job 2)
`GILighting2D.temporal` defaults true; false recomputes all intervals, and resetHistory() forces the next rebuild. Identical frames retain spatial/angular cascade and finite-bounce surface buffers, and their compute invocations return before tracing. Source and emission RGBA comparisons are exact on GPU. Any alpha, color, emission, source transform, cutoff or gain change invalidates painted intervals. Analytic geometry, emitters, lights (including nested masks), layer, cascade options, view camera and output dimensions are compared on CPU. No old radiance is blended into changed input. A camera move rebuilds rather than reprojecting; ambient is applied at presentation and needs no interval rebuild. Device replacement and changing painted/no-painted mode discard all GI history. One SDFScene2D snapshot per command encoder serves multiple consumers; submit a manually managed frame before starting another. GI borrows the painted scene and textures.
Painted occupied cells have four outward surface slots; internal faces are inactive. Each exposed face gathers 32 cosine-weighted directions per requested bounce from the preceding order, at its midpoint offset .001 source pixels into empty space. Painted RGB clamps to [0,1] for reflectance and multiplies the configured albedo; emission retains HDR. Finite bounce orders 0..4, source resolution, interval reach and angular quadrature limits still apply. GI is now covered by the named opaque visibility, energy, finite-bounce, painted-input and temporal correctness fixtures; no general physical-exactness, converged transport, continuous vector-outline or frame-rate claim is made. Historical README exceptions and no-history language await the README phase.
SDF adds 32 B/pixel exact RGBA history and a 16 B change flag to its previous 48 B/pixel transform storage (80 B/pixel plus 48 B fixed uniforms/flag). Painted GI surface buffers use 192 B/source pixel (two persistent fields and immutable zero order, four vec4 faces each), plus analytic patch geometry and cascade storage. Analytic surface fields use 96 B/patch including zero order, replacing the earlier 64 B/patch. Changed-input comparisons and distance generation still run every frame; presentation traces the near connectors. Reuse avoids surface gathers and upper-cascade interval traces, not every GPU operation.

Batch 247 job 2 sizes: SDF 2,667 to 2,911 B min+gzip, inside its 2,923 B ceiling; GI 9,670 to 10,348 B, ceiling raised 9,961 to 10,659 B under Scott's optional-size ruling. ### Compute shape entry (batch 274 job 1)
The optional @margoengine/compute/shape entry adds concatenate(arrays, axis=0), stack(arrays, axis=0), flip(x, axes=all), tile(x, repetitions), repeat(x, counts, axis=null) and pad(x, widths, options). Concatenate axis=null flattens; repeat omitting its axis flattens. Negative axes normalize against the output rank for stack and input rank otherwise. Joining promotes element types; other operations preserve dtype. Every output owns its buffer. CPU, WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility share the same logical indexing. f16 uses the existing shader-f16 device requirement and is unavailable on CPU.
Pad defaults to constant zero; scalar constantValues is converted to the input dtype. Modes: constant, edge, wrap, reflect (excludes endpoints), symmetric (includes endpoints). Widths may be one nonnegative integer, a shared pair, or one pair per axis. Nonconstant padding cannot fill an empty source axis. This entry does not expose NumPy callable/statistical/ramp padding or odd reflection. Tile prepends singleton axes or repetition factors as required by the Array API. Repeat counts may be a number or a host list of length one/axis length. Counts stay on the host to determine output shape. Arrays are bounded by device storage limits and signed 32-bit gather indices; split larger inputs.

Batch 274 job 1 size: compute/shape is 3,480 B gzip (new entry, previously 0 B), ceiling 3,736 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B gzip. Optional validation and mapping stay together to share axis handling.

Each createFX has input/output, named AudioParams, dispose and Symbol.dispose; createFXChain rolls back failures/abort and prefixes parameters by index; createBusFX inserts an owned chain after bus gating, before post sends, independently of native root effects.

Mix defaults 0.5 for chorus/flanger/phaser, 1 for other effects. Delay centre defaults 0.02/0.003/0.005 s for chorus/flanger/vibrato, range 0..0.1, minimum actual read 1 sample, depth sweeps centre*(1+depth*LFO), linear fractional interpolation. Distortion amount 0.4 (0..1) uses (1+k)*x/(1+k*abs(x)), k=100*amount, with 8193 curve samples. Waveshaper accepts 2..65537 finite float32 JSON samples. ### Batch 218 GLSL transition import

The optional transitions/glsl entry translates user-authored GLSL ES 1.00 with vec4 transition(vec2 uv) into the custom WGSL contract. translateGLSLTransition is pure; createGLSLTransition and createLiveGLSLTransition validate asynchronously before attaching. progress and ratio are supplied, along with getFromColor/getToColor and the from/to sampler2D aliases. GLSL UVs default to bottom-left; flipY:false preserves top-left coordinates. Additional uniform values are snapshotted as constants from options.uniforms or // = JSON annotations. Vectors, column-major matrices and fixed arrays use flattened component arrays; boolean values or 0/1 are accepted for boolean components. Numbers must fit finite 32-bit values; integer uniforms must fit their signed/unsigned type.

Preprocessing supports object/function macros, conditionals, define/undef, and version 100. Expressions use typed precedence parsing, including scalar/vector arithmetic, matrix operations and casts, struct/array access, overloads, swizzles, short-circuit boolean expressions and conditional side effects. Structured if/for/while/do control flow and copy-in/copy-out out/inout parameters are lowered to WGSL. No extra textures or arbitrary binding interface is supplied beyond the two transition images. Other GLSL versions are refused when declared. This is a transition-function importer, not a complete vertex/fragment program or an external include loader. Source is limited to 65536 UTF-16 units, 32768 tokens, 128 nested statements/expressions, 64 macro expansion rounds and 262144 expanded units; uniform arrays have at most 16384 elements. The custom wrapper also limits emitted WGSL to 65536 units. Compiler diagnostics carry failed and a help link; GPU compilation, cancellation, exact endpoint bypass and shader trust requirements follow the custom entry. Shader execution itself is not bounded by these parser limits.

Native GLSL and WGSL may round floating-point arithmetic differently, especially at exactly-on-texel-boundary nearest samples. Pixel fixtures choose coordinates away from those ambiguous ties and compare with the existing one-byte unorm tolerance. No bit-exact arbitrary GLSL or speed claim is made.

Batch 218 job 3 glsl entry is 15718 B gzip (new entry, before 0 B), with a ceiling of 16190 B. The compiler carries a real parser, preprocessor, typed aggregate/control-flow lowering, diagnostics and both validated factories. Splitting those mutually dependent stages would complicate deterministic diagnostics and lifecycle without improving shader quality. Core + stage stays 24209 B.

Batch 244 job 3: CRT adds `colorBleed` [0,1], default 0, and `chromaticOffset`, `redOffset`, `greenOffset`, `blueOffset`, each a horizontal number or [x,y] source-pixel tuple in [-32,32], default 0. Symmetric offset adds to red and subtracts from blue; independent offsets add on top. Positive offsets select texels to the right/below, so those channel images move left/up. Effective combined offsets may reach 64 source pixels. Color bleed retains source luma and alpha, filters I with normalized 5-tap and Q with 9-tap horizontal binomials, then clips to the premultiplied gamut. Offsets use bilinear sampling with edge-repeat borders; alpha is the maximum selected channel alpha. Tube beam/mask/brightness modulate the processed color; glow still adds the unshifted raw-source 3x3 halo. Both effects default off and preserve all previous CRT pixels, including exact boundaries. This is a selectable composite-video look, not RF encoding, dot crawl, interlacing or a calibrated TV standard. No extra pass or intermediate image; no timing claim.

Batch 244 job 3 min+gzip: pixel/crt 2816 -> 3775 B, ceiling 3072 -> 4031 B. ### Streamed SOG (batch 238 job 3)
splats/lod-sog accepts v1 and unversioned pre-release lod-meta.json, null/omitted environments, sparse leaf levels, optional errors and relative arbitrary chunk paths. Each chunk is unbundled SOG v2/v3 with 1 to 3,000,000 records. All small metadata is fetched up front with concurrency 8 to validate runs/counts and choose a uniform SH degree; textures remain lazy. Spatial depth limit 128. Complete non-overlapping single-level chunk runs and supplied totals must agree. A referenced chunk is decoded whole, then its range is copied. cacheChunks defaults 2 (0 disables completed caching), plus active loads and the existing SplatLod node cache. Independent caller aborts share requests; disposal aborts all loads.
SplatLod structural nodes have count 0 and refine unconditionally; the renderer never calls their load. Minimum coarse coverage must fit the fixed-slot budget, otherwise construction rejects with the required budget. Slot-count and splat-count limits both constrain refinement. Errors are used only with lodErrors true; otherwise radius * cbrt(max(0,1-count/finestCount)) estimates omitted detail. Environment stays selected regardless of camera distance. Colours retain the existing first-order display/linear SH conversion. encodeSog chooses v3 for extended opacity or degree 4, otherwise v2. SPZ v3, .splat and Gaussian PLY reject opacity above 1 rather than wrapping/clipping; SPZ v3 rejects degree 4. Standard PLY now carries degree 4.

## Lightmaps drawn at draw time (batch 54)

`@margoengine/lightmap/apply` adds the bake as indirect light (diffuse reflectance times occlusion times the bake),
the way `Material.lightMap` does; it does not turn off live lights the bake already holds. A glTF-pro material record
that already has a material extension (clearcoat, a custom one) is refused, since a record holds one extension. A core
mesh needs its lightmap UVs passed (`uv1`), is drawn by a materials stand-in in the engine's default scene, and its
stand-in copies colour, roughness, metalness and sidedness only (no core textures). A live GPU baker must share the
model's GPU device. WebGPU only for glTF-pro models.

### Curved text (batch 248 job 4)
`@margoengine/text/curve` provides CurvedText, curvePoint and PathText. CurvedText extends Text, wrapping the entire local X/Y block around local Y at signed curveRadius (default 1; Infinity is flat). Default curveSegments is 8 horizontal subdivisions per glyph, integer 1..256. The analytic cylinder uses [r*sin(x/r), y, 2*r*sin(x/(2*r))^2]; glyph UVs and outline/shadow layers interpolate over the subdivided surface in one block draw. Anchors, lines, shaping, font styles and transform/mesh placement are preserved. PathText accepts a TextPath with positive finite length and sample(distance) returning position/tangent/normal in local world units. startOffset defaults to 0; closed defaults false (out-of-range glyph midpoints hide), true wraps distances. Glyphs align rigidly to normalized orthogonal path frames as in SVG textPath align; whole shaped runs remain joined. Line baselines offset along the frame normal.
