## Batch 212 job 4: mixer/dynamics
Extended dynamics entry: 2,856 B gzip, budget 3,112 B. New optional gate/expander/three-band compressor with explicit linked speaker channels 1..32 (default 2), fixed construction options, AudioWorklet/CSP/AbortSignal/owned bus lifecycle as the existing worklet entry. No lookahead (latencyFrames 0), automatic makeup, clipping or true-peak limiting. Crossover phase is inherent; flat magnitude does not mean sample-identical input. Use existing worklet limiting after this stage for peak safety.
Gate defaults threshold -40 dBFS (-120..0), hysteresis 3 dB (0..40), hold 0.05 s (0..10), floor -Infinity (silence, or -120..0 dB), attack 0.001 s and release 0.1 s (0..10). Peak >= threshold opens; while open, peak >= threshold-hysteresis resets hold. Exactly holdFrames below-closing-threshold samples remain open, then closing begins. Expander defaults threshold -40, ratio 2, knee 6 dB, range 80 dB (0..120), makeup 0; below-threshold slope ratio and a quadratic knee join continuously to unity. Band defaults threshold -24, knee 6 (0..40), ratio 4 (1..100), attack 0.003, release 0.1 (0..10), makeup 0 (-24..24). Attack/release are one-pole gain time constants: compressor attenuation/recovery, gate/expander opening/closing; zero jumps. Pure expanderCurve returns output dB and handles silent -Infinity.
Multiband crossovers default [250,2500] Hz, ordered 10..0.45*sampleRate; separate low/mid/high BandDynamics. Each split is two cascaded Butterworth biquads per low/high path (24 dB/octave). Low-band high-crossover phase compensation keeps the unity sum flat. Per-band detector is linked maximum absolute sample. Ratios 1 and makeup 0 retain the crossover's allpass response. Tests prove independent RBJ convolution, closed-form knees/gains and flat impulse-response magnitude across the spectrum; real renders beside both backends. Headroom, perceptual tuning, other browsers and performance remain unmeasured. No core/stage change.
## Batch 173: optional transfer classification
`@margoengine/sciviz/transfer` adds joint value/gradient histograms, rectangle, triangle and Gaussian classifiers, 1D ordered preintegration, CT/MRI/PET display presets and an owned HTML editor. LUT resolution is 2..2048 per axis; default 256 for widgets, 128 for preintegration. Colours are linear light, opacity per reference voxel. Points and widget coordinates use physical scalar units and scalar units/data unit for gradients. Histograms require 2+ samples per axis, at most 64 million samples, x fastest; NaN/nonfinite centres or derivative neighbours are excluded. Histograms own two float64 scratch arrays (16 bytes/sample) and a 4-byte count per bin. Scalar values/gradients outside the selected histogram axes clamp to the edge bins.
Volume textures retain signed normalized scalar values outside the display range so their gradients remain meaningful; binary16 limits normalized values to [-65504,65504] and rounds them. Histogram derivatives use original CPU values; render derivatives use the half-float, trilinearly sampled field. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are supported. The separate native `sciviz/webgl2` fallback, bricked volumes and extracted isosurfaces do not consume this scalar VolumeLayer API. The editor can bind any existing scalar VolumeLayer without recreating its data; function points are resampled into the layer's existing range. Slice colours update with the same classifier. Slice opacity remains its independently specified opacity.
Preintegration uses 8..2048 midpoint samples (default 128), linear scalar variation over an ordered front/back segment and RGBA8 output. Generate for the layer's `step=1/quality` and density. Regenerate after changing quality/density for the most accurate colour integral. The marcher corrects opacity when step/density differ, but unpremultiplied integrated colour remains an approximation in that case, at clipped segment endpoints and in the existing 2048-sample cap. Gradient classification is evaluated at march samples, not preintegrated in 2D. MIP is scalar-maximum projection, not a 2D classification maximum.
The HTML component has no import side effects, supports add/select/delete, pointer/key translation, colour/opacity, rectangle extents, Gaussian sigma and explicit triangle vertices. Disposing the editor removes DOM/listeners and restores the layer's original classifier. Preintegration and histograms accept AbortSignal and yield during work. No timing or superiority claim. Transfer entry: 5996 bytes min+gzip (new entry, formerly 0; ceiling 6252). Sciviz root: measured parent 50597 to 52045 bytes; its optional ceiling rises from 51813 to 53607 for physical classifier hooks and safe owned-buffer PNG capture. Core + stage: unchanged 24209 bytes. The combined editor, histogram and classification contract stays together; splitting would add import/ownership complexity without reducing full-feature bytes.



### Batch 243 traced glTF extension lobes
mesh-pbr now carries clearcoat, sheen, iridescence and specular factors and all specified extension textures from loaded glTF snapshots. Clearcoat has independent roughness and tangent-space normal state, and attenuates underlying emission. Sheen uses Charlie, clamped Neubelt visibility and the existing Margo directional-albedo fit. Specular color is linear/sRGB-decoded, clamped after multiplying dielectric F0, while strength scales dielectric F0 and F90; metals retain their own Fresnel. Iridescence uses the shared two-order Fourier thin-film model and the green thickness channel, or maximum thickness without a map. Factors default to the Khronos values. Thin-film IOR is bounded to [1,10], thickness to [0,1e8] nm with minimum at most maximum; color factors allow up to 1e8 for specular and [0,1] for sheen. The existing source-definition snapshot and base-mip texture limits continue to apply. Clearcoat normal maps use the same derived/provided tangent frame logic as base normals.
Private PBR material records grow from 32 to 64 words. Mesh-pbr grows from 43,550 to 47,760 B min+gzip, its ceiling from 44,857 to 47,905 B. This retains all four lobes and maps together; a split would repeat material snapshots and mixture-PDF ownership. Mesh grows from 40,351 to 41,299 B within its 41,562 B ceiling, including the bounded proposal schedule and corrected geometry-limit validation in its lazy Wasm kernel. Denoise-ml is 6,768 B, within 7,023 B; core plus stage remains 24,209 B. No core/stage feature or performance claim is introduced.

Batch 243 final acceptance: six extension-lobe cases pass on each backend with maximum factor-scene error 2.384185791015625e-6 below the unchanged 1e-5 bound. The inclusive geometry coordinate bound remains +/-1e8: tagged one-ULP BLAS padding is excluded only from validation, while full padded boxes and conservative affine rounding remain in traversal. One true geometry ULP beyond either boundary still rejects. The extra cache-disabled compatibility compile defect remains in known-bugs.md; no cold-cache guarantee or speed claim is made.


## Lens drops (batch 236 job 3)
Optional weather/lens is 3,601 B min+gzip, new from 0 B, ceiling 3,815 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. LensDrops joins PostStack as an HDR stage, including WebGL2 compatibility at the half-float tier. Defaults: wetness 0.6, radius 0.025 image heights (0.002..0.06), speed 0.08 heights/s (0..1), distortion 0.7 (0..2), streaks 0.65 (0..1), seed 1 (integer 0..16777215), enabled true, time accumulated from frame deltas; an explicit time supports 0..1000000 s. An optional weather.wetness overrides wetness. The field considers 18 nearby cells per pixel, in stationary and moving layers. ## Batch 212 job 5: mixer/pitch
Pitch entry: 2,366 B gzip, budget 2,622 B. New optional time-domain transposer emits exactly one frame per input frame, with linked read-head phase for explicit speaker channels 1..32 (default 2). Defaults: pitch 0 semitones (-48..48, fractional), windowSize 0.1 s (0.005..1, fixed at construction), delayTime 0 s (0..1), feedback 0 (-0.95..0.95), mix 1 (0..1), antiAlias true (boolean). Pitch/mix/feedback/delayTime are native audio-rate controls; setPitch validates schedule atomically and defaults to immediate, or an exponential fade settling about 98% over seconds. Zero wet and default unison preserve bits, including initial samples. Unison with configured delay/feedback reads a fixed delay, minimum 1 sample for feedback.
Two half-cycle-offset read heads use complementary Hann weights and linear interpolation. Nonzero-pitch wet delay spans additional delay plus 1..windowFrames+1 samples; there is no single fixed latency. Source event times/duration stay on the same clock, with that bounded wet tail; keep feeding zeros to flush it. Memory per channel is ceil(sampleRate+windowFrames)+4 float64 samples plus filter state, allocated once. No per-sample allocation, FFT, offline resampling or timer. Upward antiAlias filtering is two Butterworth biquads at 0.45*sampleRate/ratio before the delay; aliases can remain and high frequencies are attenuated. Linear interpolation also rolls off high frequencies. No formant preservation, transient protection, speech-quality, polyphonic transparency or alias-free claim; this is the requested delay-line effect class and can have window coloration. Feedback is a creative transposed delay, not pitch-preserving echo. Requires secure AudioWorklet and blob CSP permission. Abort/disposal and bus-owned inserts follow the other optional worklets. No core/stage change; tested in Edge beside both backends, other browsers/listening/performance unmeasured.


### Voxel image and text generation (batch 241 job 1)
`@margoengine/voxel-edit/generate` provides `heightmapToVoxels` and `textToVoxels`. Grey8/RGBA8 row-major images produce Y columns: nearest whole-cell height, black zero, white `height` (default 32), X image columns and Z image rows. RGBA defaults to encoded BT.709 luma, with explicit red/green/blue/alpha and inversion options. Alpha at or below `alphaThreshold` (default 0) is air. Source RGBA is retained, with the existing deterministic reduction above 255 colours.
Text takes a required CSS `font`, default depth 1, coverage threshold 127 and opaque white colour. Native canvas shaping preserves Unicode, kerning, ligatures and holes; callers load custom fonts first. Multiline default spacing is 1.2 times measured Mg ink height. Negative bearings and descenders are included; Y is up, extrusion is positive Z. Empty text is empty storage with positive dimensions. An optional supplied context is resized and cleared; otherwise Canvas is created at call time. Fonts and platform rasterizers can differ, so font masks are not cross-platform bit-identical. There are no import-time DOM accesses. Both APIs take AbortSignal and the standard 16,777,216-cell default / 67,108,864-cell maximum budget, checked before grid allocation. Text needs a native 2D canvas; Node hosts can supply one. No new rendering backend or core code.
Entry size: /generate is new (0 to 2,479 B min+gzip, recorded ceiling 2,735 B). The bytes cover image validation, palette generation, native text bounds and extrusion together; splitting would duplicate their shared grid and validation code. Core and stage are unchanged.

### Batch 214: chain avoidance
The optional kinematics-constraints/chain entry supports CCD and FABRIK on 1..256 positive-length links, 1..256 candidate poses (default 32), and 1..1024 sweeps per candidate (default 64). ### Per-splat GPU modifiers (batch 238 job 4)
splats/modify supplies SplatModifier.create(cloud, options), attach(engine,cloud,options) and splatModifierShaders. Creation asynchronously snapshots current cloud data; signal abort rejects creation and later disposes the modifier. Already submitted readback work completes normally. One active modifier per cloud; combine hook logic into its WGSL bodies. Hooks position/opacity/color default to identity; declarations defaults empty; up to 64 parameter floats default zero, exposed as u.parameters[0..15] vec4f values. Each body has index, time and delta; position takes canonical position and returns vec3f; opacity takes the modified position and canonical opacity and returns f32; color takes modified position and evaluated linear RGB and returns vec3f.
time defaults 0, playing true, speed 1, enabled true. Clock advances once in the first view; seek with playing false. Geometry runs at -7.25 before projection/sorting, colour at -6.95 after SH/fog and before relighting. All SH degrees are evaluated at the modified centre. Covariances and SH remain the source's; this position-only warp does not deform ellipsoid axes. Geometry/opacity is written to the cloud inputs, including alpha readback, so existing geometric consumers see it. Colour changes are transient evaluated output. Opacity is clamped to 0..1.5625, colour to nonnegative HDR values. Shader/compiler errors remain visible through normal WebGPU validation.
Canonical position/opacity costs 16 bytes per splat on CPU plus 16 bytes per splat on GPU and a 288-byte uniform. Per frame: two compute passes, no canonical geometry readback. Ordinary source edits to centres/opacity must also call setRest with a full same-count SplatData; source RGB/SH/covariance edits flow normally. Disabling and disposal restore canonical centres/opacity; a fresh projection restores colour. Device restoration uploads the CPU canonical snapshot and retains clock/parameters. Composition with another position-writing animation needs an explicit canonical update; the plugin never silently stacks multiple owners.

Batch 238 job 4 minified gzip: modify new 0 to 20174 B, ceiling 20780 B. It retains canonical state, asynchronous snapshot/cancellation, typed WGSL hooks and both compute passes in one optional entry; splitting would add lifetime/ownership coordination without reducing a user's imported effect. The existing entries retain their job 3 sizes, including lod-sog 20,369 B; core plus stage remains 24209 B.

### Screen-space voxel selections (batch 241 job 2)

### Shaped and variable-font extrusion (batch 248 job 5)
`text/extrude` accepts `shapedRuns`, ordered visual glyph IDs with xAdvance/yAdvance/xOffset/yOffset in em units, optional UTF-16 cluster and zero-based line. It respects ligatures, reordered RTL runs, mark offsets, vertical advances and multiple runs per line without remapping IDs through cmap. A FontLike.shape(text) provider is called once when runs are absent; without either input, the existing Unicode cmap path remains. This is a shaping-result interface, with no built-in script shaper or network dependency. Normalize shaper positions by its font scale and use the same font instance and axes as the run.
`parseFontOutlines(bytes,{variations})`, FontOutlines.withVariations(values) and extrudeText's variations option select instances; omitted axes use fvar defaults, out-of-range values clamp, unknown/nonfinite axes fail with a linked coded error. variationAxes exposes tags/min/default/max. Existing 96-hint, 10-subroutine, 100,000-token and 16,384-flattened-vertex budgets remain; malformed ranges/counts reject. CFF1 and static TrueType behavior remain covered by the existing tests. Glyphs remain unhinted; font-wide MVAR/VVAR metrics are not consumed because block line height and supplied vertical advances own placement here. Parsed instances currently reparse their source bytes; no timing claim.
The existing optional extrude entry grows from 10,834 to 14,894 B gzip; its ceiling is raised in the same commit. ## Batch 173: labels and registered multi-component volumes
Optional `@margoengine/sciviz/labels` adds `fusionVolume`, `FusionLayer` and `labelLegend`. One drawable, one fullscreen triangle and one march combine 1..4 sources; each source is categories, RGB, RGBA or 1..4 independent scalar components. Components are interleaved, x fastest. Arrays and transfer results are snapshotted. Each source retains its own dimensions and invertible affine unit-box-to-data mapping, with no registration resampling. Bounds default to [0,nx-1,0,ny-1,0,nz-1]; transform replaces bounds. Dimension and category counts obey the device's 3D/2D texture limits (palette needs one extra transparent slot). Each dimension is at least two.
Category IDs are exact unsigned 32-bit integers, including zero and 4294967295; never interpolate them. Unlisted IDs are transparent but retain distinct boundaries. Each listed category has linear-light RGBA and an optional separate outline RGBA and integer framebuffer-pixel width 1..16 (default 1). Eight nearest-category neighbours per radius detect label-to-label and external boundaries at each ray sample. This is a projected neighbourhood outline, not a smoothed subvoxel segmentation or mesh. `setLabels` atomically validates and snapshots replacements; `labelLegend.update()` refreshes accessible HTML text after edits.
RGB/RGBA channels are linear light, default divisor 255 for byte arrays and 1 otherwise; alpha shares that divisor. RGB opacity defaults to 0.1; RGBA uses its alpha. Colour and intensity sampling is trilinear; component functions are evaluated at 256 physical scalar values into binary16 RGBA tables, and source scalar components are normalized/clamped to their declared range in binary16. No gradient or preintegrated component functions in this entry. Component and source weight default 1; zero hides them. `TransferFunction.evaluate` can supply a 1D function directly; update a snapshotted function by rebuilding the layer.
Default optical mixing sums extinction and weights colours by optical depth; over gives earlier sources/components priority at each sample; maximum selects the largest corrected opacity (earlier wins ties). All three mix before front-to-back ray compositing, never as separately sorted volume draws. Quality defaults to 1.5 samples per projected voxel; density defaults to 1. Step opacity uses distance through each source's voxel coordinates. Each ray caps at 2048 midpoint segments and terminates at alpha >0.9999. Small features thinner than a step can be missed; increase quality within the cap. No native WebGL2 fallback driver; WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are supported. Internal opaque-geometry termination is the separate volume-quality job, not supplied here.
Entry min+gzip: 6292 B (new, formerly 0), ceiling 6548 B. Sciviz root remains 52045 B and core+stage remains 24209 B. Palette ownership, transforms, component mixing and the one march remain together; splitting would fragment the same source lifecycle without removing full-feature bytes. The MSD demo reduction is 60x60x39, gzip 180024 B intensities and 661 B labels; see its source record for exact output sizes/hashes. Data are demo-only CC BY-SA 4.0, separate from engine source. OpenNeuro RGBA uses the existing CC0 T1.


Batch 203 JPEG entries: decoders/jpeg is a new optional 3,774 B minified gzip entry (previously absent); exporters/jpeg-read remains 3,774 B through the shared implementation. Its size baseline adds 256 B headroom. Core plus stage is unchanged at 24,209 B. No new dependency, Wasm asset or CPU loop was added.

### Batch 240 job 2: object blocks

Optional voxel/objects provides VoxelObjects(engine,world). Its define(name,source,options?) snapshots a core Mesh or the root/meshes graph of a core glTF Model. Nodes copy local TRS, names and receiveShadow, while Geometry and PbrMaterial identities stay shared. Source meshes remain caller owned and can be disposed after definition. Storage defaults are solid=false, opacity=0 and light=0; optional solid=true uses existing whole-cell voxel collision, not arbitrary mesh collision. Material appearance belongs to source meshes.

Call update before render. World edits reconcile only touched chunks, retaining unchanged cell handles; chunk unload/disposal releases placements and subscriptions. at(x,y,z) exposes root-first handles, and stats counts chunks/cells/mesh nodes. Core performs instanced geometry batches and per-placement frustum culling, so objects crossing chunk bounds retain correct bounds. The packed voxel mesher does not draw object cube faces. Loaded-world and engine node capacity bound memory; each placement has a transform root plus its source graph nodes. Static core glTF materials are supported; animated/skinned PBRModel graphs belong to their existing packages and are not silently converted into core meshes. ### Voxel-net recording and replay (batch 242 job 2)
Optional /replay records the exact per-recipient outbound message stream using server.onSend, including welcome and spawn; attach before clients join. Default queued bytes 64 MiB, hard per-message bound 16 MiB. Overflow and I/O errors stop recording and reject flush/close. MVR1 carries protocol version 6, tick rate, recipient id, tick and raw payload; a complete-file footer is mandatory. readVoxelRecording has a default 256 MiB file limit, configurable; playback holds validated records in memory. Files include names, application messages and resume tokens and belong with private bug reports. Select one recipient and use a fresh VoxelNetClient/world with no-op send; advanceTo is forward-only, play defaults to speed 1 and a 1-hour hard bound with AbortSignal. Playback completion means packets delivered to receive; chunk decompression completes asynchronously through the normal client. Seeking backward requires a fresh client/world. This reconstructs server-visible states, not unsent predicted local inputs or deterministic server execution. No GPU work.

# Batch 185 job 2: volume and array storage

`@margoengine/shader/compute-volume` adds `storageVolume(width, height, depth, options)` and `ComputeVolume`. ## Batch 203 standalone compression
Zstandard is an optional entry over the existing clean-room decoder: concatenated and skippable frames, checksums, a caller destination, default 256 MiB output and 128 MiB declared window. External Zstandard dictionaries remain unsupported with a coded error. LZ4 decodes standard and legacy concatenated frames, metadata, linked/independent blocks and raw blocks with an explicit decoded size. All descriptor/block/content checksums are verified. It accepts an external dictionary (last 65,536 bytes) and optional dictionaryId, rejects a missing required dictionary, caps total output at 256 MiB by default (configurable integer 0..2147483647), and yields after 8 MiB or 128 blocks for cancellation. Each call receives its complete compressed byte stream and returns all output bytes; no incremental transport API is claimed. Decoded blocks, frame assembly and final assembly may coexist, plus up to one 8 MiB legacy block and its dictionary; maxOutputSize bounds decoded bytes, not peak process memory. No timing claim.

## Batch 173 job 3: sciviz/cinematic
`cinematicVolume(figure, volume, options)` wraps an existing composite VolumeLayer, shares its scalar and classifier textures, hides the base drawable and restores its previous visibility on disposal. No core or stage imports of cinematic lighting are added. Ordinary slices remain available. Gradient and preintegrated classifiers are accepted; preintegration is treated as local diagonal extinction for secondary paths, not a claim of exact nonlocal preintegrated transport. Source gradient surface shading is replaced by scattering lighting.
All three expensive modes default off. Ambient radius defaults to 8 smallest scene voxels, 8 directions (1..64) and 8 integration steps (1..256). Shadows default to 32 steps (1..2048), toward [0.4,0.6,1]. Ambient radiance defaults [0.3,0.3,0.3], directional radiance [0.7,0.7,0.7]. Path tracing defaults g=0 (-1<g<1), 8 bounces (1..32), albedo 0.9 ([0,1]), seed 1 (uint32), 4096 accumulated samples (1..16777216). Paths converge to the chosen finite-bounce, piecewise-constant integration model, not an unbounded-bounce exact solution. Local AO applies to the deterministic march; path tracing computes ambient visibility by physical path escape instead. Each segment uses the classifier's per-voxel alpha as extinction, scaled by density and the smallest scene voxel. Both ray direction and light distance use scene metric, preserving nonuniform volume transforms. The primary/each scattering march caps at 2048 segments and widens the step to cover the box; shadow/local integral resolutions are explicit quality controls.
Accumulation uses two RGBA32float images plus an RGBA32uint work image (48 bytes per viewport pixel), one integration pass then a display triangle. Counters are always available, so even the unlit wrapper pays those passes and writes compared with ordinary VolumeLayer. `cost({signal})` reads exact last-frame scalar fetches, shadow rays, ambient rays and collisions, with a 30-second mapping deadline. Camera matrix, transform, density, quality, clips, classifier/source replacement and resize reset accumulation. Call reset() after externally updating an existing GPU source texture. configure() validates atomically, snapshots inputs and resets. Sources rebuild through VolumeLayer after device replacement; lighting clears its own history. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are tested; native GL fallback is unsupported and fails before allocation.
Scene-depth termination is owned by batch 173 job 4; this entry currently has the same opaque-interior limitation as the ordinary volume path. Multiple translucent drawables sort as whole layers, not interleaved samples. The EMD-8117 demo contains 64^3 original density samples, reduced from 192^3 at stride 3, without intensity scaling. This is an educational view, not medical evidence.

## Batch 214 job 3: multi-goal IK
The optional @margoengine/kinematics-constraints/multi-goal entry accepts 1..256 joints and at most 256 combined goals and loop closures. Fixed, revolute and prismatic scalar joints compose into spherical and floating joints; rest/attachment quaternions use x,y,z,w and normalize nonzero inputs. Joint parents may be unordered but must form a forest; explicit attachment-frame closures join branches, trees or world anchors. World position and rotation-vector channel masks and nonnegative objective weights are supported. Hard scalar bounds apply to every returned pose, including failed solves. All active constraints must meet unweighted physical tolerances before resolved is true; conflicting weighted goals return a bounded best compromise with resolved false. Defaults: 128 iterations per seed, 4 deterministic seeds, 1e-5 metre/radian tolerances, 0.01 initial damping, 0.25 radian/metre maximum scalar step, +Z joint axes, identity rest/attachment transforms, unbounded scalars, initial value zero. Point closures match position by default; orientation is opt-in. The dense local nonlinear solve is bounded and not a proof of global feasibility; iteration-limit and stalled are explicit. Returned failures are diagnostic poses, not certified closed chains. Rotation masks select world logarithm components, not Euler angles. No dynamic constraints, obstacle/path certificate, renderer, core or stage dependency is added. Use existing optional chain/swept entries for collision queries. No speed result is published.
For multi-goal IK, the numerical scalar envelope is -1e6..1e6 even when a bound is omitted, so every returned value remains valid as a warm start and for forward evaluation. It is enforced during every candidate and step.
Multi-goal entry size: 8,535 minified bytes, 3,375 gzip bytes (new entry, previously 0), ceiling 3,631 bytes. The optional bytes provide the complete coupled solver; splitting its math would complicate one isolated feature. Core plus stage remains 24,209 gzip bytes.

### Anisotropic painterly filter (batch 271 job 4)
`@margoengine/creative/paint-aniso` exports AnisotropicPainterly, an LDR PostStack effect. Defaults: radius 3 (integer 1..8), strength 1 (0..1), anisotropy 1 (0..1), sharpness 8 (1..8), enabled true. The RGB Sobel structure tensor receives separable 5-tap [1,4,6,4,1]/16 smoothing. Eight overlapping polynomial sectors follow its minor eigenvector; ellipse radii are r*(1+A) and r/(1+A), at most 2r and at least r/2. Weighted RGB variance combines means; centre alpha is preserved. The Gaussian radial weight has a Wendland C2 taper to zero at the ellipse boundary. This is a single-scale variant, not the papers' exact sampled weighting texture or a multiscale solver. All reads clamp to the current viewport. Two rgba32float intermediates cost 32 bytes per target pixel per retained view, capped at 512 MiB per view; inputs are display-space, without alpha-weighted filtering. Zero strength/disabled is an exact copy and omits both tensor passes. Native WebGPU and full WebGL2 are checked; the preview refuses. Per-view buffers/textures/groups are retained, resize replaces them, and device restoration recreates them. No speed, aesthetic or other-device claim.

### Compute dense decompositions (batch 274)

The optional compute/decomp entry returns owned f32 arrays in the input context. It handles real finite matrices, arbitrary leading batches, broadcast solve RHS matrices (only 1-D RHS is a vector), strided/expression inputs, square/tall/wide/reduced/full and empty factors. Arithmetic is f64 in a lazily loaded per-call Rust SIMD Wasm instance on every backend, including native WebGPU and compatibility; GPU inputs incur a readback and results an upload. This is a correctness route, with no device-native decomposition or speed claim. Singular solve/inv, non-positive-definite Cholesky, nonsymmetric eigen/Cholesky input, nonfinite input, f32 output overflow and iteration exhaustion reject. det(singular)=0 and det(0x0)=1. SVD values descend; symmetric eigenvalues ascend. Real symmetric inputs must match across their diagonal exactly; complex/Hermitian arrays are outside compute's supported dtypes. Limits: each matrix dimension and RHS column count <=4096; 16,777,216 f64 workspace words by the checked algorithm bound, and that many f32 output elements per call; Jacobi maxSweeps 100 by default, 1..1000 configurable. Cancellation covers loading, readbacks and batch boundaries (event-loop yield each 16 matrices), not the middle of a synchronous matrix factorization. Concurrent calls own separate Wasm instances; no arena survives a call.
Batch 274 job 2 measured gzip sizes: compute/decomp 0 -> 3617 B (ceiling 3835 B); separate lazy decomp-kernel.wasm 64419 B raw / 25233 B gzip. Compute root remains 39118 B; combined core + stage remains 24209 B. ## Batch 173 job 4: volume-quality and opaque scene termination
Optional `qualityVolume(figure, volume, options)` shares the source data, classifier, clips and transform, hides the ordinary drawable and restores its previous visibility on disposal. Defaults: emptySpaceSkipping=true; blockSize=8 cells (2..32); jitter=true; adaptive={tolerance:0.01,maxStep:4}, tolerance (0,1] in normalized scalar units and maxStep [1,16]; refinement=12 (4..24). isovalue defaults absent, selecting composite or MIP from the source; a supplied isovalue must be finite within the source range and selects the first detected crossing. Optional surface color is linear RGB [0,1], otherwise the classifier at the hit. Clipped samples do not create cap surfaces.
GPU block bounds contain a one-voxel interpolation halo. A 256x256 opacity-range table conservatively includes all gradient/front-back classification rows and interpolation support; classifier replacement rebuilds it. Source/device/block-size changes rebuild min/max blocks. Call invalidate() after updating an existing GPU texture in place. Max block-texture width/height is the device's 2D texture limit; increase blockSize if needed. Each block uses 16 bytes plus a 65536-byte opacity lookup and a 2048-byte rank texture. Original source storage is shared. CPU envelope preparation is bounded by the already uploaded classifier (at most 2048x2048) plus 32896 interval unions; field reduction runs on the GPU, and the expensive noise optimization is offline, not a browser CPU loop.
Adaptive integration widens steps in low-variation blocks and corrects opacity for actual segment length. It is a quality control, not a certified error bound for arbitrarily narrow transfer functions. Steps are bounded by block exits; base spacing is at least the ray interval/2048, with a 4096-iteration traversal cap. Bisection refines the first detected crossing; multiple crossings wholly between sampled endpoints may require higher source quality. Refined isosurface values use explicit float32 trilinear interpolation; general compositing uses hardware filtering. The input scalar texture is still normalized binary16, so source quantization is unchanged. MIP remains available; opacity-based skipping is disabled for it. Integration distances use the smallest scene voxel metric and sample centres map exactly to the first/last grid points.
Opaque scene depth now terminates ordinary, registered fusion, cinematic and quality paths, including cameras inside a volume. No core/stage change. One capture is shared per engine and existing post captures are borrowed; scientific opaque layers render before the snapshot and transparent integration. Depth capture presents at graph order 39; custom scientific renderer orders must remain before that. A single nearest reversed-Z depth is used per pixel (maximum covered MSAA sample), so volume coverage at opaque silhouettes is conservative, not independent per-sample integration. Whole transparent layers still sort by centre, not interleaved ray samples. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are covered; native GL fallback remains unsupported for these layers.
Cinematic history now stores per-pixel depth and count in two RG32float images. Changed opaque depth resets only affected pixels, even at the sample cap; unchanged saturated pixels perform no transport. Exact cost counters use RG32uint with mode-specific lossless packing. Total cinematic history/work image storage is now 56 bytes per viewport pixel (previous 48). Colour remains float32. cost() reports zero transport work for saturated pixels in a no-op frame; read it immediately after the frame to be measured, before an extra image capture render. The extra depth/count attachment and packed counters fit 32 bytes of colour attachments per sample. Camera/volume/classifier changes still clear all history.
The demo reuses the original CC0 OpenNeuro T1 asset and shows composite, MIP and refined isosurface modes with an interior 151-point linked probe. No new dataset download or derivative intensity change.

Batch 173 job 4 entry sizes (min+gzip): sciviz root 52045 -> 54985 B (ceiling 56635), cinematic 6006 -> 6442 B (ceiling 6698), labels 6292 -> 6529 B (existing 6548 ceiling), new volume-quality 0 -> 8509 B (ceiling 8765). Default opaque-depth termination must stay with ordinary volumes in sciviz; separate required capture would preserve the defect. Optional sampling/refinement and its generated mask retain one resource owner. Core + stage unchanged at 24209 B before/after. Full viz kit measured 256216 B and its guide is updated in the same job.

Cinematic samples reports camera-stable submitted frames capped at the target; local opaque-depth changes reset individual pixel histories without resetting that global frame counter. The cost pixels field counts dispatched viewport pixels, including saturated no-op pixels.

### Demand rendering (batch 195 job 1)
quality/demand renderOnDemand stops the continuous engine loop and schedules only dirty frames. Defaults: initial true, maxDelta 0.1 seconds, browser animation-frame scheduler, no sources/update/signal. invalidate(n=1) coalesces to the maximum outstanding count; animate() holds are independent and released idempotently; loaded(promise) wakes on success and preserves rejection. sources listen to start/change/end/load. Attached controls and plugins update in render; existing engine.onFrame app callbacks must be supplied as update instead. update returns true to continue animation. Unannounced scene mutation and autoRotate need explicit invalidate or an animation hold. Idle has no RAF or timer, and the app update callback first steps zero after idle; plugin rendering bootstraps with min(maxDelta, 1/60) seconds so damped controls consume queued motion. Abort, scene/plugin disposal and explicit disposal cancel pending work and listeners. Device restoration requests two settling frames. Temporal effects may request additional frames with invalidate(n). Does not restart the old continuous loop on dispose. Core/stage unchanged.


Demand entry size: new 0 to 928 B gzip, ceiling 1184 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. The optional scheduler keeps cancellation, control events and animation ownership in one entry.
The VFX GPU checks are split into test:gpu (the existing render checks) and test:gpu:parity (all five parity features, both backends). CI discovers both scripts; each parity backend runs once. Runtime sizes are unchanged.

### Adaptive events (batch 195 job 3)
quality/events adaptiveEvents(handler, options) returns run(...args), regress, setMoving, flush, moving, pending and disposable lifecycle. Defaults: interval 100 ms during motion, debounce 120 ms after start/change/end, no sources or signal, performance.now and native timeout clock. Interval/debounce are nonnegative through 2147483647 ms; interval also accepts Infinity to suppress all motion picks. Control events reset the inactivity timer; setMoving(true) remains in force until false or a later regress timeout. At rest there is no intentional throttle. Queued calls retain only the latest arguments and resolve all coalesced callers with that invocation's result; active async calls finish first, so results cannot arrive out of order. Click/drag handlers stay direct. Rest immediately flushes queued input; a stationary pointer with no queued request is not polled or repicked. flush bypasses the interval without overlapping an active call. Handler rejection reaches every corresponding caller; disposal/abort rejects queued and active result promises, cancels timers and subscriptions, and ignores late completion without cancelling the caller-owned GPU task. No idle polling and no scene/core changes. Applications pass an AbortSignal for owner disposal. Native and compatibility picks tested.

Adaptive events entry size: new 0 to 967 B gzip, ceiling 1223 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. One optional entry keeps deadlines, latest-input promises and lifecycle ownership together.

### Composed physical materials on 16-unit compatibility devices
Full physical shaders and extended materials with six or more distinct extension maps pack the five base maps into one linear RGBA32F array. The remaining eight extension maps, all material lobes, transmission, shadows, clustered/local shadows and IBL remain. Logical dimensions, authored mip chains, independent UVs/transforms, all six glTF minification modes, two magnification modes and three wrapping modes remain. Sampler LOD clamps are applied before min/mag selection, matching the existing WebGPU sampler state. Native physical permutations with fewer maps keep their original layout. Packed arrays are shared by source views, dimensions, mip ranges and sampler state on each device, and released after their last model user. Float array storage per unique set uses 80 bytes per texel at the maximum base-map width/height, times its mip pyramid (roughly 4/3 for a complete square pyramid), plus a 160-byte parameter buffer. Allocation is device-limited; no reduced source images or channels are used. Mip copies run on upload/rebind; streams expose actual resident view dimensions. This correctness fix makes no speed claim.

The 360-case sampling oracle measures at most 0.0000402 absolute channel error against the continuous filtering equations on both tested backends. Native fixed-precision HDR bilinear filtering differs by up to 0.00792 (a fixture with radiance up to 2); packed RGBA32F interpolation retains the continuous reference rather than reproducing that hardware quantization. Custom shading hooks keep their original separate base-map binding contract and own their additional resource budget. No existing composed pipeline assertion changes.

## Batch 177: optional 2D contours

Entry size: 0 B before (absent), 3,802 B min+gzip after, 4,058 B initial ceiling. These bytes hold both interpolation models, exact triangulation predicates, bands, stitching and SVG export together; splitting would duplicate topology or force extra user orchestration. The core + stage root remains 24,209 B gzip. Work is bounded to 4,000,000 cell-level combinations per request; reduce either sampling or levels beyond this allocation bound.

`@margoengine/sciviz/contour2d` has no root/core/stage dependency. `contour2D` accepts strictly monotone rectilinear axes, x-fastest scalar samples, 2x2 through 1,000,000 points; `scatteredContour2D` accepts 3 through 10,000 distinct sites with a noncollinear hull. Coordinates and finite scalars have magnitude at most 1e100; NaN scalars mask incident cells. All 1 through 256 finite levels must strictly increase. Bands cover adjacent levels only; no under/over band is invented. Lines connect exact symbolic cell-edge identities; grid interpolation is bilinear with straight marching chords and the asymptotic decider, with the 0-2 diagonal for an exact saddle tie. Scattered interpolation is linear over the Delaunay convex hull; there is no extrapolation or inferred land mask. Cocircular ties follow input order. Exact dyadic predicates protect triangulation signs; exported intersections use float64 arithmetic.

Polygon rings use even-odd filling and include cell boundaries; they are exportable polygons, without a global polygon-union simplifier. SVG defaults to 800x500, 36 px padding, 1 px dark isolines, six blue-red band colours, labels on, title `Contour plot`. Labels are rotated at half the projected path length, omitted below 48 px, and use a white halo. Global collision avoidance is not claimed. Cancellation checks before snapshots and between bounded batches, with exact abort reasons. Inputs are snapshotted; results own their memory. CPU triangulation is quadratic in the worst case; no timing or Wasm acceleration claim. The demo is standalone SVG and does not mutate the existing Figure or core/stage. Known correctness defects found by this job: none open after the analytical regressions.


### Fresnel reflector floor (batch 188)

Optional environment/reflector-pbr adds PBRReflector, reflectorFresnel and reflectorBlurFraction. New entry 0 to 3,340 B min+gzip; shared reflector 11,355 B, refractor 11,312 B, cube-camera 5,756 B, prefiltered 3,693 B; core + stage stays 24,209 B. Reflection uses Schlick Fresnel (ior default 1.5, allowed 1..4, metalness default 0, allowed 0..1) mixed with baseColor (default #808080). Inherited color tints the reflection. baseColor is an artist-selected constant linear floor term, not direct-light shading. All options are live uniforms.

Inherited roughness (default 0) sets the maximum mip blur. Captured geometry at the plane stays sharp; its world normal distance / blurDistance (default 10 metres, a positive normal float32 from 2^-126 to 3.4028234663852886e38) scales the blur, saturating at the maximum. Empty depth takes maximum blur. Actual inverse oblique projection works for perspective and orthographic captures; there is no assumption of an ordinary depth projection. Up to eight existing box-filtered mips: this is mip blur, not a GGX convolution or screen-space ray tracer. Normal maps distort the lookup; Fresnel uses the geometric plane normal. The standard Reflector's visibility, passes, layer selection, transform convention, capture-only mode and lifecycle remain in effect. Native WebGPU and full WebGL2 compatibility are supported; the lightweight WebGL2 preview still refuses the capture.

### Precipitation cover (batch 236 job 2)
Optional weather/cover is 1,539 B min+gzip, new from 0 B. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. PrecipitationCover takes an unattached WeatherFX and reuses its top-down depth map (graph order -3) for rain, core Puddles and Snow (order -0.5) and GLTFWeather (cover option). WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility. Bias defaults to 0.02 m (finite, 0 or more). The map is the WeatherFX square of side 2 x Weather radius centred on the camera, at WeatherFX resolution (default 50 m over 256 texels): surfaces outside it count as exposed, so set radius to reach the sheltered surfaces in view. A receiver is sheltered by the highest occluder of the four texels around it: every point under an occluder at least one texel wide stays dry, and up to one texel past an edge does too. Receivers are tested at the shaded point; with multisampling an edge pixel is shaded at its centre, which can lie up to a pixel outside its surface, so a surface that ends exactly at a shelter edge can show a one pixel exposed fringe. Give shelters a small overhang. The capture splash and lens passes are not installed.

### Batch 186 job 2: shared shadow atlas
ShadowAtlas from /shadow-atlas replaces LocalShadows on one Clustered instance, retaining its maxLights (1..16, default 4), casters, PCF/PCSS, biases, receiveShadow and clipping. It allocates one depth32float array layer, resolution squared times four bytes, plus a 4096-byte uniform table of guarded rectangles. Default atlas 2048, minimum face 32, maximum face 1024, texelDensity 1. Dimensions are powers of two from 16 to 16384, minimum <= maximum <= atlas, limited further by the device. Point/hemisphere lights retain six faces, spots one; directional cascades and area faces share the image.
Point/spot face demand follows the conservative projected world-range box clipped to the viewport. A near-plane intersection requests full viewport demand; a wholly behind-camera bound requests minimum demand. Authored resolution caps demand. Directional/area faces use authored sizes or maximum face size. All tiles are square. Least-screen-important lights lose one resolution level at a time until all faces fit, retaining every face. If minimum demand cannot fit, RangeError asks for a larger atlas or lower minimum; lights are never silently dropped. At most 256 logical faces. Since batch 52 job 4 the atlas caches each face in its own tile (next section). No hysteresis claim.
Deterministic packing proof: sixteen six-face lights at 16 texels use 24,576 rasterized depth texels; four six-face lights requesting 64 texels use 61,440 after fitting a 256 atlas. Both retain every face. This is a work count, not a wall-clock speed result. Source tests cover non-overlap, input immutability, priority, camera-driven viewport changes and caching. Real GPU tests cover point, spot and combined rectangle/sphere filtering on native WebGPU and full WebGL2.

### Batch 52 job 4: cached shadow atlas faces
ShadowAtlas keeps a face's tile while its size class is unchanged: faces that change size or are new take free tiles from a buddy allocator, largest first; only when fragmentation leaves no room is every face placed afresh (and redrawn). A face re-renders only when its light changes (position, direction, range, cone, near/far, shadow size), its tile moves, or a caster whose old or new bounding sphere reaches the face's frustum moves, shows, hides, is added or is removed. A partial redraw keeps the atlas (load) and clears each redrawn tile alone with one depth-0 triangle under its viewport and scissor; a full redraw clears the atlas once. Casters without bounds (instanced or displaced), opacity-mapped and displaced casters (redrawn every frame), a source's shadowVersion, invalidate() and device restore still re-render every face they may reach or every face. Camera-fitted directional cascades follow the camera as before. Point/spot sizes have no hysteresis, so a camera moving across a power-of-two coverage boundary moves and redraws that light's tiles. LocalShadows (the texture array) keeps its whole-array redraw on a caster change. Work count (CPU test, two lights, seven faces): first frame 7 faces, a still frame 0, a box moved under the point light 1 (before this job 7), a hidden, shown, added or removed box under the spot 1, an added third light 1 with the other tiles in place.



## Batch 136: clean-room Draco encoder

The default exporters/draco entry loads one optional Rust/Wasm SIMD encoder on first compression, in a browser worker or in the Node process. The public compressDraco API, abort behavior, GLB preservation and caller-supplied Emscripten encoderPath remain compatible. Sequential and standard/valence EdgeBreaker preserve oriented triangles; independent attribute seams share exact values. Prediction and quantization are described in clean-room.md. A packet is at most 256 MiB, 16,777,216 input points, 50,331,648 indices and 255 attributes; each attribute has one through four components. Floats must be finite. Normal quantization accepts 0 or 2 through 30 bits; a one-bit octahedron has no positive reconstruction range and is rejected. Other quantized floats accept 1 through 30 bits, or 0 for exact values. Fan splitting can increase output point count, which the result and GLB accessors report.

Initial replacement measurement: 181,081 -> 89,161 B min+gzip, with Wasm 156,788 B raw / 58,216 B gzip. The complete proof version below is 91,248 B min+gzip, with Wasm 160,900 B raw / 59,962 B gzip. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B. The old prebuilt encoder files have now been removed from source and distribution. No end-to-end speed claim. The byte-output bridge uses eight Wasm boundary calls regardless of output length, rather than one GetValue call per output byte. This counts bridge calls only, not encoding arithmetic or wall-clock time. Quiet speed-phase timing is owed.

At default settings the development comparison preserves exact oriented corner identities and Margo/native-prebuilt decoded result equality on the real fixtures listed in clean-room.md. Box stream 119 vs 130 B; Fox 7,086 vs 7,566 B; the small refrigerator primitive's bounded seed choice gives 352 vs 358 B without changing decoded attributes. This is corpus evidence, not a universal compression-ratio guarantee for arbitrary inputs. The portable normal fixture's maximum Euclidean direction error is below the opaque old encoder at 2/3/8/10/16/24 bits, without weakening its bounds. More settings/corpus evidence belongs to the following proof job.
Batch 191 post/curvature is LDR view-dependent ridge/valley enhancement, not an object-space curvature measurement. Ridge/valley 0..100 (default 1), radius integer 1..16 px (2), gradient threshold 0..1 (0), relative linear-depth rejection >0..1 (0.02). Signed xyz normals come from owned SceneTargets or an any-size callback; supplied normalSpace is world (default) or view. Core meshes capture automatically; optional models use add(model). Empty normals, clear depth and rejected neighbours cannot add silhouette shading. Camera right/up convert world normal derivatives to view space, including rotated and orthographic cameras. The owned capture has the same rgba16float normal/depth footprint as Pixelate. Normal-provider identity is selected at setup; removing a supplied callback later is a tracked configuration defect for Pixelate and Curvature, while changing the texture returned by a stable callback works.

## Scientific datasets (batch 176 job 1)
The optional @margoengine/sciviz/datasets entry normalizes structured curvilinear, rectilinear, mixed PolyData, unstructured, multiblock and partitioned inputs to an AnalysisGrid-compatible DataSet. Fields and geometry are owned snapshots; source cell IDs, sparse blocks, names and top-level block IDs are retained. Composite topology is concatenated without welding separate blocks. Flattened arrays are the intersection of block field names; heterogeneous fields remain available on the original blocks. Shared field widths must agree. Use each block when a field is not common. Empty blocks are null. Source dimensions live under dimensions, not the regular-image dims discriminator. Existing pipeline, contour, clip, calculator, probe and glyph entries consume the normalized type directly. Contours of line cells return points, and matching isolated vertices are retained; clipping supports these dimensions too. Constant line cells do not emit infinitely many contour points.

Defaults: maxPoints=1000000 (allowed 1..10000000), subdivisions=2 (1..64, rounded upward to a power of two). Source cells are bounded by maxPoints and output cells by 4*maxPoints; tessellated points are bounded by maxPoints. Lagrange curve/triangle/quad/tetrahedron/hexahedron/wedge orders 1..10 use equispaced nodes. Quadratic curve, triangle, quad, tetrahedron, hexahedron, wedge and pyramid use the standard 3/6/8/10/20/15/13-node spaces. Explicit referenceNodes may permute the standard lattice. Higher-order cells are uniformly approximated with interpolated simplex vertices; callers raise subdivisions for finer approximation. This is deterministic h-refinement, not adaptive error-controlled refinement or an exact curved-cell filter. Matching generated nodes share original-ID interpolation keys across cells. Independent composite blocks remain independent, including ghost boundaries; ghost arrays are retained, not implicitly removed.

PolyData source order is vertices, lines, polygons, strips. Polygons must be simple and planar (relative planarity threshold 1e-10); concave polygons are ear clipped. Polyhedron face streams must be closed and consistently oriented with planar simple faces. Nonconvex cells use a face-plane arrangement, limited to 4096 regions per source cell, and signed solid-angle interior classification. Generated interpolation uses mean-value coordinates with boundary handling and affine checks. Arrangement point merging uses 128*Number.EPSILON times the source diagonal. Self-intersecting surfaces and degenerate cells are not supported input. Linearized filtering follows the existing filter entry's numerical domain and interpolation policy; source curved-cell interpolation is not re-evaluated after each filter.

Readers: .vtr, .vts, .vtu, .vtp, .vtm, .vtpd/.vtpc, with numeric VTK payloads decoded by @margoengine/loaders/vtk-xml. Raw-appended arrays use its bounded range reader; metadata sniffing and composite XML are bounded by maxBytes (default 64 MiB). Every retained array is decoded when creating the owned dataset. Composite references resolve against the input URL or baseURL, or an explicit files map; nesting is limited to 64 and cycles reject. Relative string inputs use baseURL, or document.baseURI in a browser. Files must fit the specified per-read and decoded-array limits. All numeric point/cell tuples are retained; scalar defaults to the first one-component point field. PLOT3D covers whole-grid 2D/3D, single/multiblock, formatted Fortran D/E exponents, stream binary and 4-byte-record-marker unformatted, both byte orders, 4/8-byte coordinates and optional iblank. Defaults: 3D, formatted, multiblock, no blanking; binary defaults little endian, float64, record markers. Options explicitly disambiguate variants. Iblank is retained as an array, not a rendering mask. Solution Q/function files, plane-record layouts and 8-byte record markers are not claimed. The NASA originals use the supported formatted whole-grid variant. No file is fetched or GPU device created on import, and cancellation preserves its exact reason. No core or stage change and no measured speed claim.

Dataset entry size: 35,806 minified bytes and 13,072 gzip bytes, previously 0, optional ceiling 13,423 bytes. The entry keeps topology normalization, interpolation, nonconvex scientific-cell decomposition and VTK/PLOT3D adaptation together; splitting would add cross-entry orchestration for the same bytes to users of this one feature. Core plus stage remains 24,209 gzip bytes.
### Batch 217 job 3: scroll and range playback

Optional cutscene/scroll exports RangePlayback and ScrollPlayback. Range defaults: entire timeline, iterationCount 1 (nonnegative fractions and Infinity supported), normal direction, speed 1. Directions are normal, reverse, alternate and alternateReverse. update(delta) runs the borrowed player's skip() for each crossed leg, preserving instant order; seek resets each repeated leg without firing its start instant. At most 1000 boundaries per update; larger deltas reject before mutation. play resolves true at completion, false on pause/stop, rejects on AbortSignal; pause resumes progress, completion restarts. Instants stay on the player, iteration/finish events on the controller. Controllers own advancement, so pause the base player and update the controller only.

Scroll defaults: window, physical y axis, start 0, end current maximum scroll offset, whole timeline range, scrub 0 seconds (immediate), automatic events/frames true. Pixel offsets and seconds are clamped to the supplied interval. A positive scrub is an exponential time constant; automatic smoothing settles to the target within 1e-7 seconds. automatic false uses update(delta) from the app's clock. refresh() re-reads content bounds; resize and scroll events refresh automatically. No-scroll sources hold the start. Physical horizontal offsets can use explicit signed start/end for RTL layouts. Abort/dispose cancels callbacks and keeps the borrowed player usable. No renderer or core additions, and no speed claim.

Batch 217 job 3 measured min+gzip: new scroll entry 0 to 2,048 B, ceiling 2,304 B. The optional entry combines clock ownership and cleanup for both timeline drivers; splitting those controllers would add entry and integration complexity. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.

## Batch 177 job 2: statistical charts

Student-t critical values support positive fractional residual df through 100000, including LOESS df below one. Bracketing rejects critical values above 1e150 with a remedy to increase residual df; no fixed-range clipping or unconverged fraction is returned. The continued fraction has a 2048-iteration hard limit and checked relative convergence. The low-df regression includes independent SciPy values at df 0.2 and 0.5.

Entry gzip sizes: `/stats` absent (0 B) to 6,719 B, initial ceiling 6,975 B; `/maths` 5,703 B to 8,854 B, ceiling raised from 5,959 B to 9,120 B. Sharing the math functions between direct transforms and chart marks avoids independent implementations; splitting the public CPU utility entry would add import orchestration and break the requested `/maths` access. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B.

`/stats` creates owned CPU marks and standalone vector SVG with axes, ticks, titles and labels; it introduces no Figure/core/stage API or GPU pass. Error bars support x/y symmetric or asymmetric amounts, caps and points. Box plots use interpolated quartiles, median, Tukey adjacent-value whiskers and outliers; violins use 96 Gaussian KDE queries over data range plus three bandwidths, maximum half-width 0.4 per category. Area and pre/post/mid step lines preserve missing-data breaks. Signed area/bar stacks keep separate positive/negative bases, with optional independent unit normalization. ECDF is right-continuous, two-sample Q-Q interpolates common midpoint probabilities, 2D density is a diagonal Gaussian KDE, and hexagons expose exact input membership. All mathematics is also exported from `/maths`.

Defaults: SVG 800x480, padding 58 px (minimum 24), white background, empty title/x/y labels, six categorical colours, automatic linear axes with nice ticks; point radius 2.5 px, line width 1.4 px. Box width 0.6; whisker multiplier 1.5; area baseline 0; stack kind area, normalization off, bar width 0.8 of smallest positive x gap; step mode post; density queries 32x32 (2..256); hex radius supplied in data units. Silverman bandwidth uses sample SD and IQR/1.34; constant observations use 1% of max(1,abs(value)) before the Silverman factor. Optional bandwidths must be positive. Violins independently normalize maximum width, not sample count. Named box/violin groups label the categorical x axis. Stack series use category colours in input order.

Linear and LOESS confidence defaults to 0.95, accepted range (0,0.999]. OLS needs three paired finite samples and nonconstant x. LOESS local degree is one, span 0.5, two robustness iterations (integer 0..10), at least three neighbours and three finite pairs. Tricube weights exclude the furthest selected neighbour. Queries default to sorted observed x; optional `at` permits explicit positions. Local zero-weight or nonpositive residual-df cases reject with a suggested remedy. LOESS intervals condition on final robust weights and are approximate pointwise mean bands, not simultaneous, prediction or extrapolation guarantees. Missing xy pairs are removed from statistical fits; area/step drawings retain gaps, stack NaN contributes zero. Errors must be nonnegative magnitudes; signed NASA lower errors are converted to magnitude only when drawing their bars.

Inputs are finite with magnitude at most 1e100, with NaN denoting missing. At most 100000 observations per series, 100000 Q-Q queries, 1000000 stack cells, 4000000 sample/query or LOESS fit/sample pairs, and 200000 SVG marks. This bounds allocations/work; reduce the dataset or query resolution beyond it. Maths is synchronous and owns results; import has no DOM, network or global side effects. Argument failures are linked RangeErrors carrying code `out-of-range`. No speed gain, exact confidence coverage, journal layout or new interactive Figure claim. The 13-chart real-data demo includes downloads and a 390 px layout.
Batch 175 optional entry min+gzip: sciviz/omezarr 0 -> 20,866 B, recorded ceiling 21,492 B. These bytes include the shared Zarr region reader, store validation, scalar adapters and codec pipelines. Keeping them together preserves one reader and source contract; splitting the entry solely for a smaller recorded size would duplicate validation or require additional imports for a cloud source. Core and stage source are unchanged.
Batch 175 core plus stage measurement: unchanged at 24,209 B gzip, below the 25,000 B gate.

### Compute Rust SIMD CPU backend (batch 274 job 3)

createCpuWasm from compute/cpu-wasm returns the existing CPU API, with f32/i32/u32 values and all existing built-in CPU operations. Custom WGSL remains unsupported. Every context loads an isolated SIMD-required Wasm instance on demand; creation accepts AbortSignal and normalizes load/compile failures to a coded MargoError. Numerical calls are synchronous and cannot be interrupted mid-dispatch. No GPU or worker is required. Arrays remain normal owned host buffers, so memory growth never invalidates an array or a returned readback. The transient packet limit is 8,388,608 f64 words (including descriptors and parameters); larger work rejects with RangeError and can use smaller stream chunks. The module has a 512 MiB memory ceiling. Transcendental operations use host Math imports; exact A/B equivalence is against the JavaScript CPU backend on the same host. Expression intermediates cross the bulk bridge; there is no wall-clock speed claim. Core plus stage remains 24,209 B gzip. Final entry and Wasm sizes are recorded with the job's size gate.

### Compute NN extras (batch 274 job 4)

compute/nn-extra adds BatchNorm, GroupNorm, ConvTranspose2d, LSTM, GRU, upsample and Upsample. All support Tensor gradients and the existing JavaScript CPU, Rust SIMD CPU, WebGPU and compatibility routes. Data and parameters use the context's float32 primitives. Norm eps defaults 1e-5 and affine defaults true. BatchNorm accepts rank >=2 and a channel axis (default 1); training needs >1 value per channel. Running mean starts at zero, variance at one; momentum is the new-batch contribution (default 0.1, null cumulative); trackRunningStats defaults true. Inference uses saved buffers. GroupNorm takes NCHW-style [batch,channels,...spatial], channels divisible by groups, and the same statistics in train/eval. Module stateDict/loadStateDict include nested module state; BatchNorm stores running mean, running variance and batch count in addition to learned parameters. Batch count persistence uses f32, so integer counts above 16777216 lose unit resolution.

ConvTranspose2d input is [N,C,H,W], weight [inChannels,outChannels/groups,kh,kw]; stride/dilation default 1, padding/outputPadding 0, groups 1, bias true. Output padding must be below stride or dilation. withOutputSize selects dimensions in the stride-derived output range. Output geometry is (input-1)*stride-2*padding+dilation*(kernel-1)+1+outputPadding. Metadata uses O(outputH*outputW*inChannels/groups*kernelH*kernelW) indices/masks per group and a batch-offset table; backward scatter sums overlapping float contributions in the backend's order. Use smaller batches/images to respect device buffer limits; no tiling is claimed.

Recurrent input/output is [time,batch,features] by default (batchFirst false). numLayers 1, bidirectional false, bias true, dropout 0. Dropout applies between stacked layers while training. LSTM uses i,f,g,o gates; GRU uses r,z,n, with reset applied after recurrent candidate projection. run returns sequence, final h and LSTM c, with state shape [layers*directions,batch,hidden]. Optional lengths mask padded output and retain previous state for each batch item. forward returns sequence only; run's returned tensors share a differentiation graph and must remain alive through their backward uses. States are explicit, never held between calls. Recurrent state/table storage grows with sequence length through the tape.

Upsampling takes [batch,channels,1..3 spatial axes]. Choose size or scaleFactor (default 2), nearest by default. Linear/bilinear/trilinear use half-pixel centers unless alignCorners true; bicubic is 2D with a=-0.75 and clamped edges. Nearest uses floor(outputCoordinate*inputSize/outputSize). Scale-derived sizes floor their products. Interpolation metadata is O(outputPixels*taps^rank), with 1/2/4 taps per spatial axis. It does not implement antialiased downsampling. Different data layouts compose the existing permute operation.

Measured sizes: compute/nn-extra 0 to 20860 B gzip, ceiling 21486 B; compute/nn 19137 to 18873 B; compute root remains 39851 B and core plus stage remains 24209 B. One optional entry shares tape/selection helpers; a split would duplicate them. No wall-clock speed claim.
### Depth, MSAA and mip targets (batch 271 job 1)
`@margoengine/creative/targets-depth` exports DepthTextureRenderTarget, a TextureRenderTarget (cube, array or 3D; rgba8unorm or rgba16float) with per-surface depth, 4x multisampling and mip generation. Defaults: depth true, depthFormat depth32float (also depth24plus, depth24plus-stencil8), samples 1 (1 or 4), per pass depthLoadOp clear and clearDepth 0 (reversed Z, as the engine). Each mip and layer or volume slice owns its own 2D depth texture (multisampled when samples is 4); depth is not resolved or mipmapped, since WebGPU has no depth resolve. At 4x, cube and array layers resolve straight into their layer; a volume slice resolves into a 2D scratch that is copied into the slice when the pass ends. generateMipmaps(encoder) fills mips 1 and up from mip 0 with an exact area-weighted box footprint, so odd sizes (5 to 2 to 1) weight edge texels by their covered fraction; volumes also filter across slices. Allocation, counting colour, retained depth, multisample colour and volume scratch, is capped at 256 MiB per target. restore(device) drops every attachment and pipeline; callers redraw. On the WebGL2 layer, volume slices drawn with depth go through the layer's 2D stand-in (two blits per such pass; operational playbook 3.2). Native WebGPU and full WebGL2 are checked; no speed claim.

Depth target entry: before 0 B, after 3398 B gzip, optional ceiling 3654 B. TextureRenderTarget gains one protected textureUsage() hook (COPY_DST for the volume resolve copy); the /targets entry stays within its ceiling. Core plus stage remains 24209 B.

The umbrella npm test command discovers tests/*.test.js, matching its current test directory and the repository coverage invariant. This manifest-only repair changes no runtime entry, API or size ceiling; other test extensions and nested directories are outside that existing invariant.




## Typed tables and cross-filter (batch 174 job 2)

`@margoengine/sciviz/table` is an independent optional entry, 12,324 B min+gzip from 0 B, ceiling 12,694 B. `@margoengine/decoders/snappy` is 1,250 B from 0 B, ceiling 1,506 B. The bytes buy scalar CSV/Arrow/Parquet readers, null/int64 preservation, indexed filters and deterministic aggregation; splitting the table API would complicate shared column and filter identity. Core + stage stays 24,209 B.

Tables borrow immutable equal-length typed columns. Dictionary strings use Uint32 indices; validity is a separate bitmap. Integer and time values retain signed/unsigned 64-bit storage. Wide decimal and opaque binary scalars are lossless dictionary strings (unscaled decimal with its scale, or hex). Readers accept flat scalar tables, not nested/repeated arrays, tensors, encrypted/external Parquet chunks, obsolete LZO/Hadoop LZ4 or Arrow view layouts. Flatten nested sources before reading. Arrow files and streams support dictionaries, replacement/delta dictionaries and LZ4-frame/Zstd buffer compression. Parquet supports flat row groups, v1/v2 pages, plain, dictionary, RLE, delta binary/length/prefix and byte-stream-split encodings, six modern codecs and page CRC. The readers default to 100,000,000 rows and 536,870,912 input/decoded-block bytes; overrides are explicit. Streaming/range reads belong to the separate large-series job.

Range filters are [lower, upper); set filters use exact typed equality, including explicit null. Dimensions intersect; a cleared dimension passes nulls. Every dimension builds its own index once. Boundary/set changes touch only changed row spans/postings and changed bitmap words; first-time indexing and switching filter kinds are full-index operations. Duplicate row values are retained.

Aggregation supports up to 4,096 1D/2D bins per call, final upper edge included. Host classification uses numeric column values; supplied GPU context performs all count, valid-count, sum, minimum and maximum tile reductions. Mean uses the merged sum/valid count. Rows without a valid coordinate do not enter bins. Null/nonfinite values do not enter numeric statistics. Counts are exact Uint32. Numeric inputs round to f32, each tile adds in fixed source order, and host totals merge in float64; this is not exact-real or float64-input summation. A tile's sum error relative to its f32 inputs follows gamma(255) times its absolute input sum, before host rounding. Rescale values if f32 inputs/tile sums overflow. Empty numeric bins return NaN. CPU fallback follows the same tile order. No timing or rival-throughput claim is made.

The 10,000,000-row correctness proof repeats the 4,096 licensed TLC observations, selects 9,670,406 rows and compares every bin statistic with an independent exhaustive reference on WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility. The linked demo selects 2,211 observations below two miles and changes both rendered charts.

## Engineering file readers (batch 176 job 2)
Six optional entries: sciviz/hdf5, /cgns, /xdmf, /exodus, /openfoam and /ensight. No new core or stage code. FileOptions maxBytes defaults to 64 MiB per read/metadata object/decoded selection; normalized geometry uses the existing DataSet maxPoints/subdivisions bounds. Calculated boundary values must be written by the solver; this reader does not execute boundary-condition code, includes or dictionary macros. Multi-region/decomposed cases can be resolved as separate calls.
EnSight Gold: ascii, C binary and Fortran record binary geometry; unstructured common linear/quadratic, nsided/nfaced and structured/rectilinear/uniform blocks; scalar/vector/tensor node/element files; case wildcards and timeIndex selection. littleEndian defaults true. Original part and source-cell boundaries remain intact. These are file-format limits, not speed or universal-format claims.

Open SelectionStore universes enumerate explicit selected keys only; inactive rowIds is empty while has(key) follows the empty predicate. ### Batch 173 job 6: direct tetrahedral volumes
Optional sciviz/tetvolume accepts conforming, non-overlapping VTK type-10 grids with shared node IDs. Point scalars interpolate linearly in barycentric coordinates; cell scalars are constant. Geometry/scalars are immutable snapshots; NaN at any supported vertex masks that cell. Adjacency is indexed by the opposite local vertex; boundary is -1. Degenerate cells, repeated nodes, invalid offsets/indices, more than two owners of a face and same-side owners reject. Normalized determinant must exceed 1e-10 times the product of the three edge lengths. Global self-intersections and nonconforming duplicate geometric vertices remain caller constraints.
The float32 cell packet is 96 bytes/cell, with approximately 64 bytes/cell for a binary bounds tree, plus padded texture rows, a 272-byte uniform and the shared classifier source. CPU replay retains those packets and 16 bytes/cell of adjacency. Float-encoded topology caps at 8,388,607 cells; the GPU 2D texture capacity can impose a smaller limit. CPU construction is synchronous; throughput evidence is owed to the speed phase.
The ray uses adjacency when a neighbour has a positive-length interval, then a spatial entry query for boundaries or disconnected pieces. Convex cells are integrated front-to-back once, with at most cellCount+1 traversal iterations. Up to 2048 midpoint segments per cell cover its entire clipped interval; long cells widen the step rather than truncate the ray. Default referenceStep is the smallest physical edge, quality 1.5, association point; other defaults follow VolumeLayerOptions. Physical extinction uses a normalized metric to avoid squared-unit overflow/underflow. Scene depth and up to four source clip planes truncate the ray. MIP finds the exact maximum of each cell's linear field along its ray interval, then uses the classifier opacity.
Native WebGPU and WebGL2 compatibility are supported; the native GL-only sciviz driver is not. Classifier, density, quality, mode, shading and clips live on the hidden owned layer.source; disposing the tetrahedral layer removes all its owned resources and source. Opaque classifier alpha stays exactly opaque even for a very large referenceStep. Gradient classification uses the constant physical cell gradient; preintegrated classifiers keep the existing segment/density contract. Finite sampling and float32 plane/interpolation precision remain accuracy limits.
The NASA demo uses 2146 original sampled scalar values, extruded as a span-invariant field on 6048 tetrahedra, with height exaggerated 12x. Its 65x3x65 reference is resampled from those same cells with CellLocator; physical opacity is matched nonlinearly at each density. Original zip, output hashes and transforms are recorded in tmr-tet.json. No timing claim.

Tetrahedral entry size: 6322 B min+gzip (ceiling 6578 B), previously absent; core + stage unchanged at 24209 B.

### Scientific figure state, version 1 (batch 179)
`@margoengine/sciviz/spec` is optional; core and stage have no new imports or features. Saves are asynchronous: serialize `await fig.toJSON()`, then restore with `Figure.fromJSON(spec, canvas)`. Default binary allocation budget is 256 MiB per save/load, including timeline snapshots; `maxBytes` raises it explicitly. Depth is at most 128 nested values. Numeric arrays preserve little-endian bytes, dtype, NaNs and infinities; inline and URL data carry SHA-256. Network sources must have their exact declared length. URL-backed arrays come from `loadSpecData`; inline is the default.
A pipeline's versioned graph and rendered layers are retained without executing unknown operators. Supply the registry to restore a runnable graph; otherwise `pipelineState` retains the dormant graph. Custom layers need an explicit codec. Native factories and mesh, glyph, graph, geo, flow, LIC, fusion, bricked and cinematic factories record creation/state on opted-in figures. Transfer callbacks become their renderer's 256-entry table; arbitrary application callbacks and unregistered live objects reject. Applications choose which code to trust; JSON cannot fetch modules.
Timeline export pauses playback, captures each frame and returns to the original index; callbacks become concrete frame states. It does not serialize application timers, event handlers, simulation code or in-flight tasks. Interactive 2D limits, selection indices, camera, drag mode, annotations and layer order are saved. Exact pixel reproduction requires the same dimensions, backend and hardware plus the engine's `exactSize` capture mode. Default MSAA blending is not a byte-stability guarantee, including for repeated draws of one unchanged scene.

### Automatic scatter LOD rings (batch 64 job 5)
scatterLODs(mesh, { ratios, signal }) from @margoengine/scatter/simplify returns { meshes, triangles, deviation }. Defaults: ratios [0.4, 0.12], two triangle fractions decreasing within (0, 1]. Ring 0 is the source object; ring 2 is simplified from ring 1. Input is a core Geometry (positions and normals only) with triangles, up to 200,000 vertices. Every ring vertex is a source vertex, so normals are never interpolated or recomputed; a ring keeps more than its ratio when no collapse is left that keeps seams and hard edges closed (a box keeps all 12 triangles). deviation is a one-sided bound (source vertices to ring surface), tested over every vertex and triangle pair, so it costs source vertices times ring triangles: fine for scatter meshes, slow for a 200,000-vertex one. A collapse may lower a blade's tip: Scatter's blades check refuses a ring whose top falls to the root. ringDistance(deviation, pixels = 1, height = 1080, fov = pi / 3) is the pinhole projection of that bound, ignoring wind bend and instance scale (multiply deviation by the largest scale yourself). Needs the optional peers @margoengine/lod and @margoengine/mesh-edit; no GPU work and no speed claim. Entry size is in scripts/quality/baselines/sizes.json; core plus stage unchanged.

### Water bodies (batch 67 job 1)
water/bodies WaterBodies takes 1 to 64 bodies: closed outlines (3 to 4096 points, even-odd inside, self-intersections not checked) at one level, or river paths (2 to 4096 [x, level, z] points, width 0.01 to 10000 per point) on a uniform Catmull-Rom spline at 16 steps per span. The body map is corner-sampled rgba32float, 16 to 2048 texels on the longer side (default 256), with two texels of margin; past the margin the map clamps, so distances there read at most the margin. The CPU rasterization is brute force over texels and segments with a bounding-box skip and refuses more than 4e8 texel-segment visits. Shorelines are smooth at the map resolution, but the Water grid's triangles still carry level changes between bodies across one grid cell. The Water grid stays origin-centred and is shaded and discarded outside the bodies, so a large grid around a small lake costs its full vertex work. Overlaps: the later body covers the earlier one; there are no holes. Water's wave velocity is scaled by the body's wave share in WaveQuery; coastal flow is not body-aware.

### List 3 batch 66 job 5: underwater view

The waterline is one probe plane under the camera per frame; the surface seen from below keeps Water's own shading; several views per frame share one uniform. Focusing is clamped to 0.1..10. Owned GPU memory: three rgba32float plus depth32float targets (viewport, resolution squared, 1x1).
